As there is no book or treatise which this author has written that does not bear the footsteps and marks of *Divine Light* and knowledge—imprinted and visible within them for the special use and benefit of the impartial Christian reader—so also these letters of his, written at various times and on different occasions to several friends, and now gathered and bound together, may rightly be considered as a single book. This book offers significant benefit and guidance to the reader, lover, and practitioner of that divine light and knowledge which his writings contain and present. Indeed, the mere *written word* <note>original: "bare Letter"</note> of any man’s writings—even if written from a divine gift and a real manifestation of light within the authors themselves—cannot breathe the *spirit of wisdom* into us. For the sound of understanding cannot be captured or painted on paper, any more than the notes and symbols of music can provide the actual sound and melody to the ear. Instead, they serve as a guide for how the skillful *musician* shall play on the instru-

For *to the pure, all things are pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but even their mind and conscience are defiled.* <note>original: "To the pure, all things are pure; but to the impure, all things are impure; for their very Mindes and Consciences are defiled." ...are printed in a treatise by themselves, called *The Teutonic Messenger* <note>original: *Mercurius Teutonicus*; "Teutonic" refers to the author's German heritage, and "Mercurius" implies a messenger or guide</note>.

In a word, courteous and Christian reader, these epistles will serve as an introduction and proper information to show you who this author was, from where he obtained his great knowledge, and upon what foundation and center it is built. Likewise, they show how you may come to truly understand the intent and meaning of his writings and effectively find their excellent use. Whether you are learned or unlearned, rich or poor, master or servant, parent or child—no matter your calling, profession, temperament <note>original: "complexion"; in this period, it referred to a person's physical and mental nature based on the balance of bodily fluids</note>, astrological alignment <note>original: "constellation"</note>, or disposition—you may find such knowledge here as may better and improve you correctly in Christianity.

Therefore, be like the industrious bee that seeks honey at every flower; where she does not find it, she does not leave her sharp sting behind. Likewise, if you find something that does not please you, let it alone. Do not leave a taunting scoff or the stinging venom of scorn and rash judgment behind you. Instead, pray that God would give you His Holy Spirit to lead you into all truth. Then you shall know God within yourself, according to that divine promise: "They shall all be taught by God, and know the Lord" <note>John 6:45 and Hebrews 8:11</note>.

# Theosophical Letter,

<margin>* Or Letter of Divine Wisdom.</margin>

### WHEREIN
### The life of a true CHRISTIAN is described.

->Showing what a Christian is, and how he comes to be a Christian; and likewise what a titular <note>one who holds the title of Christian without the reality of it</note>, nominal, or historical <note>one who believes the historical facts of the Bible but lacks a personal, living faith</note> Christian is, and how the faith and life of each differ.<-

->*May the fountain of Jesus Christ’s heart be our life-giving <note>original: "quickning"</note> consolation, renewal, and eternal life.*<-

<margin>1.</margin>
BELOVED, and much-respected friend in Christ. Out of an obligation as fellow members (just as one branch on a tree is bound to another) and a shared desire for our spiritual work, I wish for you the open well-spring of grace which God has manifested in our humanity through Christ Jesus. I pray that it may richly spring up within you, and that the Divine Sun may thereby cast the influence of its love-beams into your soul. May it also stir up and open the soul's great magnetic hunger (which is the true divine mouth) for Christ's flesh and blood, as well as for your physical welfare.

K.*, and also observed during my time with you, that through the Father’s drawing <note>referencing John 6:44, "No man can come to me, except the Father... draw him"</note> you feel a unique thirst and an earnest, sincere longing for His life—which He, out of His highest love, has manifested...

...in Christ Jesus; therefore I would not (at the request of Mr. D. and also of yourself) fail—out of our mutual obligation as fellow members of the body of Christ—to visit and greet you with a short letter. In doing so, I hope to revive, quicken, and refresh myself somewhat along with you in that same fountain of the life of Jesus Christ. For it is pure joy to me to see that our paradisiacal coral <note>original: "Paradificall Corall"; likely a metaphorical reference to the spiritual growth or the "hidden manna" of the soul, common in mystical writing</note> flourishes and brings forth fruit in my fellow members, for our eternal restoration and delight.

3. And based on this, Sir, I will explain to you out of my small gifts and knowledge: *What a Christian is, and why he is called a Christian*. Specifically, only he is a Christian who has become capable of this high title within himself. He has surrendered himself—including his inner core <note>original: "inward ground"; a term often used in mysticism to describe the deepest part of the soul where God dwells</note>, mind, and will—to the free grace in Christ Jesus. In his soul's will, he has become like a young child who only longs for its mother’s breasts, who sincerely pants for its mother and sucks the breasts of the mother from which it lives.

4. In this same way, a person is only a Christian if their soul and mind enter again into the first Mother from whom the life of man originates; *namely*, into the Eternal Word. This Word has revealed itself with the true milk of salvation in our humanity (which is blind regarding God). The person sucks this milk of the Mother into their hungry soul, from which the new spiritual person arises. Through this, the fiery [dark and dry] soul—proceeding from the Father’s nature <note>original: "property"</note>—reaches and obtains the place of God's love. In that place, the Father begets His beloved Son. Only there is the temple of the Holy Spirit, who dwells in us, found. There also the spiritual mouth [or believing desire] of the soul, which eats Christ's flesh and drinks His blood, is understood, or experienced and enjoyed in its very essence.

5. For only he is a Christian in whom Christ dwells, lives, and has His being—one in whom Christ has arisen and been made alive in the heavenly essence within the inner core of his soul, which had disappeared and departed in *Adam*. Even he, I say, is only a Christian who has "put on" Christ's victory (that is to say, Christ’s incarnation, humanity, sufferings, death, and resurrection, which stand against the anger of God, as well as against hell, the devil, death, and sin) in his eternal core. There, the "seed of the woman"—namely, Christ in His conquest—also conquers within him. He daily tramples upon the serpent’s head <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15</note> within the wicked, worldly <note>original: "carnall"</note> will, and kills the sinful lusts of the flesh.

6. For in Christ alone are we accepted as children of God and heirs with Christ. This does not happen through an outward, accidental <note>original: "adventitious"</note>, or foreign show of some separate, selected appropriation of grace—I say, not through a foreign...

7. 8. But to turn and become like a child, and be born anew of God’s grace-water of love and the Holy Spirit—that does not please him. 9. For what is born of the flesh is flesh and cannot inherit the kingdom of God (*John 3*). *To be fleshly minded is enmity against God, but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.* And he alone hears God’s Word who is born of God, for only the spirit of grace in Christ hears God’s Word.

10. For no man has ever seen God; the Son alone, who is in the immeasurable bosom of the Father, declares the word and will of God within us. Thus, we hear and understand His will and good pleasure within ourselves and are willing to follow it. Yet we are often held back by the outward sinful flesh, so that the operation or effect of that same divine power [purpose and godly resolution in our mind] does not always manifest in the outward form <note>original: "Figure"</note>. However, it does enter the inward form in the inward spiritual world, concerning which St. Paul says, *Our citizenship <note>original: "conversation"; meaning conduct or citizenship</note> is in heaven.*

13. Our own human will died in the death of Christ, turning away from its self-centeredness and selfish desires; and the first human will (which God breathed from His Spirit into Adam) blossomed anew through the victory of God’s sweetness and love in Christ’s heavenly blood. Then the Devil and Hell, which held humanity captive, were confounded and put to shame. This was symbolized by the dry rod of Aaron, which budded in a single night and bore sweet almonds <note>Reference to Numbers 17:8</note>.

...of God in our humanity, in himself, into love. 15. Now, the uncovering of death must be accomplished in the person of Christ himself within our own soul and humanity. This occurred so that the eternity in Christ—with which he came from heaven and by which he remained in heaven (John 3)—overcame time (that is, the life and will of time) and changed time and its will into the eternal will of the Deity. All of this must be brought to pass within our own received humanity. In the same way, the desire of our soul must receive into itself that same eternal will in Christ, in which time and eternity stand in equal agreement and harmony. Through the power of that will, the soul must immerse or cast itself into the adoption of free grace in Christ. This allows the same inward Paradisiacal ground <note>original: "ground"; the deepest, essential core of a person's being</note>—which died in Adam—to spring forth again in the will of Christ's obedience, through his heavenly blood and the human blood he assumed from us.

16. The atonement and expiation must be made manifest and experienced within ourselves through that atonement which Christ once made. Indeed, <insert>the atonement and reconciliation</insert> was once fully finished and brought to pass in Christ’s blood and death. However, that which was once wrought in Christ must also work in me. Even now, through Christ’s shedding of his blood, it must be brought to pass in me. Christ also pours forth his heavenly blood into the desire of faith in my poor soul, and infuses and transforms <note>original: "tinctureth"; an alchemical term for spiritual transformation</note> the anger of God which is within it. By this, the first Adamic Image of God may appear again and become seeing, hearing, feeling, tasting, and smelling.

17. For that same Image—which died in Adam from the essence of the heavenly world—being the true Paradisiacal Image, does not dwell in the four elements <note>The physical components of the material world: earth, air, fire, and water</note>. Its essence and life do not exist in this world, but in Heaven (which is made manifest in Christ within us). That is, it exists in that one pure, holy Element from which the four elements sprang at the beginning of time. This same inward, new spiritual man eats Christ’s flesh and blood; for he is and lives in Christ. Christ is his trunk <note>original: "stock"</note>, and he is a branch on that trunk.

18. For every spirit eats of that from which it takes its origin. The animal <insert>sensual</insert> mortal soul eats from the spirit of this world—from the stars and elements, and from the kingdom of the world. But the true eternal soul—which was inspired out of the Eternal Word into man as Divine life—also eats of its Mother: that is, of the holy, essential Word of God.

He infused his heavenly essence into our human nature to serve as a body for the soul. With this, he embraced and clothed our poor captive soul and reopened her heavenly mouth (which was previously dead in the anger of God) with the infusion <note>original: "tincture"; a spiritual essence or quality that can transform and "color" a substance</note> of love. Consequently, the poor soul can now eat heavenly **Manna** again. This eating was first tested in Christ's person within the humanity he received from us during his temptation in the wilderness. There, Adam—acting through Christ—once again ate **Manna** from Paradise for forty days.

20. Therefore, I say that no one becomes a true Christian through a mere appearance or a specific form of grace that is simply assigned or credited <term>credited: historically termed "imputed" grace, meaning righteousness given by God from the outside rather than something that changes a person's inner nature</term> from the outside. For if a person is truly a Christian, his sins are not forgiven simply by the speaking of a word, or by claiming a ritual or a promise of absolution for himself from the outside—in the way a lord or prince in this world might freely grant a criminal his life through an external favor. No, this accomplishes nothing before God.

21. There is no grace or favor by which we reach adoption as God's children, except only in the blood and death of Christ. God has foreordained and appointed him alone to be a throne of grace or reconciliation <note>original: "propitiation"</note> in his own love, which he has infused into him (in the **Sweet Name Jesus** <note>original: "Jesu"</note> out of **Jehovah**). He is the only sacrifice that God accepts to reconcile his anger.

22. Now, if this sacrifice or free offering of grace is to do me any good, it must be worked and brought to pass within me. The Father must beget or impress his Son into my desire of faith, so that the hunger of my faith may take hold of and understand him. And if the hunger of my soul’s faith grasps him in his promised Word, then I "put him on" through the entire process of justification <term>justification: the process of being made righteous and aligned with God's will</term> in my innermost being. Immediately, the putting to death <note>original: "mortification"</note> of anger, the Devil, death, and Hell begins and moves forward through the power of Christ's death within me.

23. For I can do nothing; I am dead to myself, but Christ does it in me. When he arises in me, then I am dead to my old self in regards to the true man, and he is my life. In that I live, I live for him and not for my own self-centeredness <note>original: "selfehood"</note>. For grace puts my own will to death and sets itself up as Lord in place of my ego, so that I may be an instrument of God, who does with me whatever he pleases.

26. And hence it is that a Christian must be a bearer of the cross; for as soon as Christ is born in him, the assault of Hell and the anger of God in the eternal nature begins. Then the Hell in man is destroyed, and the Serpent is trodden underfoot. From this, great disquiet, persecution, and reproach from the Devil and the corrupt world arise against the outward sinful man. Even then, the outward sinful man must allow himself to be condemned and judged to damnation by the "children of anger" and by God’s severe justice in that anger. This is because another man <note>the new, spiritual man</note> lives in him, who is not like or conformable to the outward mortal man; and so God’s justice executes its judgment in anger upon the "house of sin," and all the ministers of God’s wrath help to carry out that execution.

27. 28. The holy Scripture witnesses in all places that we are justified from sins by faith in Christ, and not by the works of our merit, but by the blood and death of Christ. This is indeed taught by many, but it is rightly understood by very few who teach it.

29. They depend on a historical faith (*James 2*), which is only a bare knowledge or a literal guess. With this, the "man of sin" tickles and comforts himself; through imagination and blind persuasion, he flatters and soothes himself, calling himself a Christian, though he has not yet become either capable or worthy of this...

[enjoys] this so high a title, but is only a titular and nominal <note>In name only</note> Christian, externally clothed with Christ’s *purple mantle* <note>original: "Purpur-Mantle"; symbolic of royalty or a superficial covering of righteousness</note>; of whom the Prophet speaks, saying: <margin>They draw near to me with their lips, but their heart is far from me: And Christ said, "Not all that say Lord, Lord, shall enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, but those who do the will of my Father in Heaven."</margin>

31. 32. Now there is no mercy except only in Christ, and if I am to reach that mercy, then I must reach Christ within me; are my sins to be destroyed in me? [She] is able to protect herself, for she sees that she stands in the jaws of death and hell, surrounded by evil spirits who continually fire the strong influence of their evil desires into her to destroy and corrupt her.

36. And then she dives into that same newborn spirit of the will and wholly immerses herself into true humility itself. In this way, the spirit of Christ takes hold of her and brings her into the spirit of this new will, so that the soul essentially and experimentally <note>original: "experimentally"; here meaning "through direct experience"</note> feels and finds him. At this point, a divine glimpse and beam of joy arises in the soul, acting as a new eye. In this eye, the dark, fiery soul conceives the <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for "being," "substance," or "essence"</note> and essence of the divine light within herself. Consequently, she hungers and thirsts for the grace of God, enters into an effective repentance and sorrow, and laments the evil she has committed.

37. And in this hunger and thirst, she receives Christ’s flesh and blood. For the spirit of the New Will (which in the beginning entered into the grace of Christ, and which Christ received into himself) now becomes substantial and essential through the magnetic attraction <note>original: "impressure"; referring to the way the soul "pulls" or "shapes" spiritual reality into substance</note>, hunger, and desire of the soul.

38. And this essentiality is called <term>Sophia</term> <note>original: "Sophia"; Greek for "Wisdom," often personified in mystical theology as the "heavenly bride" of the soul</note>, which is the essential wisdom or the body of Christ; and in this, faith in the Holy Spirit consists. *Here, Christ and the soul believe on one common ground.*

39. For true faith does not consist in thoughts or in merely agreeing to the history—that is, when a person imagines <note>or visualizes in their mind</note> to themselves that Christ died for their sins [and, by a historical understanding or blind persuasion of a particular election, clings to his merits and righteousness without the innate righteousness of Christ and the life of God essentially working in them and birthing them as a new creature]. For faith is a receiving of the promised grace in Christ; it receives Christ into itself. It presses him into its hunger, along with his heavenly flesh and blood, and with the grace that God offers in Christ.

40. Christ feeds the soul with the essence of <term>Sophia</term>, namely with his own flesh and blood, according to his saying: "Whoever does not eat of the flesh of the Son of Man has no life in him, but whoever eats the same remains in him." <note>referencing John 6:53–56</note>

41. And herein consist the Testaments of Christ and also the right Christian faith. For an insubstantial [unessential, speculative, or verbal] faith is like a glimmering fire smothered in smoke or moisture; it wants to burn but has no proper <term>Ens</term> to fuel it. But when a proper <term>Ens</term> is given to it, that little spark of fire increases, from which a beautiful, shining light arises. Then it becomes clear that such a fire and beautiful light lay hidden in the wood, which was previously unknown.

42. But when the soul—being a small spark of divine fire—receives into itself God’s love-*essence* <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for the essential substance or "being" of a thing</note>, namely Christ’s flesh and blood, then that spark grows into a great fire and light. This light shines and sends forth its brilliance through fair virtues and good works; it lives with great patience amidst the vanity of this world, and yet grows like a beautiful flower out of the wild earth.

43. We have a comparison for this in the sun and the earth. Specifically, if the sun did not shine upon the earth, no fruit could grow. But when the sun shines upon the earth and penetrates into the *essence* <term>Ens</term> of the earth, then the essence of the earth receives the sun's virtue or powerful influence into itself. This results in a great hunger arising in the essence of the earth for the virtue of the sun; this hunger absorbs and feeds upon the sun's virtue and influence. Through this hunger of the earth's essence, which eagerly reaches for the sun's essence, a plant is drawn out of the earth with a stalk. In this stalk, the essence and virtue of the sun also ascend throughout the growth and flourishing of the plant. Thus, the sun, with its beams of light, becomes substantial within the essence of the earth in the stalk and root. We see how, through the power of the sun and stars in the spirit of the world, another body arises from the stalk that is different from the root in the earth. We also see how the stalk puts forth a bud into a beautiful flower, and afterwards into fruit; and we see how the sun, from time to time, ripens and sweetens that fruit.

44. And so it is with man. The ground of the soul is the divine field; when it receives the divine sunshine into itself, a divine plant springs forth. This is the "new birth" of which Christ speaks. Now, this plant must be nourished from above by heavenly influence, drawn up in growth by the divine sun and the divine water, and preserved by the divine "constellation" <note>original: "constellation"; here referring to the alignment of divine powers or the spiritual atmosphere</note>—namely, the divine virtue or power of God—until it becomes a divine body with a divine and angelic form, like the body on the stalk.

45. And just as the body on the stalk must stand in rain, wind, and storms, in heat and cold, and allow the sun to ripen it, so must a Christian stand in this thorny world. He stands amidst the awakened anger of God and the kingdom of the Devil, among many wicked people, and allows himself to be beaten with scorn and contempt. Yet he must turn his hope and confidence away from all created things...

58. Thirdly, we shall find the poisonous, envious serpent in our properties, which tears and rages like a poison; I mean Envy, which wishes no man as well as itself. 59. 60. Fifthly, we shall find many hundred evil beasts in our desire, which Pride loves and honors more than God. An early term for an egoist or someone focused entirely on their own self-interest at the expense of the whole.</note>.

63. All of this is contrary to the Divine will and foundation, and is a betrayal <note>original: "perjury"</note> against God; indeed, it opposes the course and order of nature. We see this by the trees and plants of the Earth—how all stand and grow lovingly by one another and rejoice in one Mother, and how one branch on a tree imparts its sap and power to the others, mutually serving each other.

64. For in such a lovely equality and harmony, the life of man (*John 1*) was inspired out of the eternal Word into the human image, which was made from the clay <note>original: "Limus." Latin for mud, slime, or clay; refers to the "dust of the ground" from which Adam was formed in Genesis 2:7.</note> of the Earth. So it was that all the properties of life stood in an equal proportion in the temperament <note>original: "temperature." In this context, it refers to a perfectly balanced state or mixture of elements.</note>, in one love, and they mutually loved each other.

65. But when the Devil mixed his poison and false desire into it, the properties of life were divided into many desires. From this, strife, discord, sickness, infirmities, and the burdensome coarseness and mortal frailty of the body have arisen through the false desire and the introduction <note>original: "insinuation"</note> of beast-like <note>original: "Bestiall"</note> properties. Because of this, the Image of God (which was from the heavenly essence) disappeared. Concerning this, God said to them, "*In the day that you eat of the Tree of the Knowledge of good and evil, you shall surely die*." That is, you shall die to the Kingdom of God, as it indeed came to pass.

In that state, we are only the children of Hell and of the anger of God, and we cannot therein...

# The First Epistle.

...[anyone with these desires can neither] inherit nor possess the Kingdom of God. Neither is God manifest in any such desire; rather, only His anger and the characteristics of the dark, earthly world are present. We live in those desires only for the vanity of this world, and thereby we stand upon the abyss of the dark world and the anger of God—that is, of Hell. Hell continually gapes and hungers after these characteristics, and it counts these traits as its own fruits and children, which it shall reap and take into its barn; for they belong to it by natural right. These desires all originate from it and have their root in the foundation of Hell and destruction, and indeed nowhere else.

67. Therefore Christ said, "*Unless a man be born again, he shall not see the Kingdom of God.*" All these false wills and desires are destined for damnation. If anyone wishes to see God, he must be converted and become like a child, and be reborn in the Holy Spirit through the water of eternal life—namely, through the heavenly *Ens* <note>original: "Ens." A Latin term meaning "being" or "essence"; here Böhme refers to a divine spiritual substance or the fundamental nature of heavenly life.</note> which God has revealed in Christ. This allows the first true man—who died in **Adam** and proceeded from the essence of the heavenly world—to spring forth again in Christ and become alive.

68. All these "evil beasts" <note>Böhme frequently uses "beasts" as a metaphor for the various sinful impulses and animalistic instincts that dominate fallen human nature.</note> are condemned and must die within us. Although their desires still somewhat cling and stick to our flesh, they must all be mortified <note>original: "mortyfied." To subdue or "put to death" the sinful nature through spiritual discipline.</note> within the soul during this lifetime. That is, in the "inward ground" of the soul, which must be tinctured <note>original: "Tinctured." A term from alchemy used by Böhme to describe a spiritual infusion or transformation where the "blood of Christ" purifies and alters the soul's nature.</note> by the true tincture in the blood of Christ. This ensures the qualities of the internal ground may again live in harmony and concord; otherwise, they cannot reach the Divinity within themselves.

69. Now, when a person knows this, he can find no better way to be rid of his evil, beastly desires than to immediately, at that very instant, commit himself with all his strength to a strong will and earnest purpose: that from this time forward, he will hate and abandon these evil beasts of the Devil, seeing as they are only the Devil's servants. He must return to his "lost country," into adoption and atonement. He should view and look upon himself as nothing other than the lost swineherd (or the Prodigal Son), for he himself is that lost swineherd and no better. He should forthwith approach the Father with the conversion of his soul in deepest humility, acknowledging his unworthiness, admitting how shamefully and unworthily he has misspent and misused the free inheritance of Christ's merits, and so enter into repentance.

70. Let him commit his earnest will with all his strength to the goal that, from this very time forward, he will repent and amend his life and no longer love these evil beasts. But this must be in earnest, in real sincerity without delays—not thinking of another day or week...

# A Letter to
# CASPAR LINDERN,
## Customs Official <note>original: "Cuſtomer." In this period, a "customer" was a collector of customs duties or a tax official.</note> at Bytom <note>original: "BEVTEN." Now Bytom, a city in Upper Silesia.</note>.

### Is described the plain and simple way which the author took for the attainment of his high knowledge;
### ALSO,
### His evaluation <note>original: "Cenſure," which at the time meant a formal opinion or judgment rather than just a criticism.</note>, judgment, and answer concerning various authors of different opinions, aiming to lead Christians into the excellent and desired way of love and union.

The open fountain in the heart of Jesus Christ refresh us and lead us to himself, so that we may live in his power and rejoice in him; so that we may love and understand one another and enter into one single will.

2. Much respected and discreet Sir, my most worthy friend in the love and humanity of Jesus Christ; after offering my hearty desires to God in our *Immanuel* <note>original: "Immanuel." Hebrew for "God with us."</note> for the prosperity of your soul and body, I wish to inform you, Sir, that I have received your letter. In it, I perceive that you are a seeker and a great lover of the Mystery—that is, the knowledge of God—and that you diligently take care to gather divine crumbs everywhere, bearing a great desire and hunger for them.

3. This brings me great joy on my part, seeing that God does thus—

...thus draw and lead his children; as it is written: "Those who are led by the Spirit of God are the children of God" <note>A reference to Romans 8:14.</note>. And just as one branch on a tree rejoices in the other and they mutually provide sap and assistance to each other, so too do the children of God in their tree, *Jesus Christ*. At this, my simple self rejoices exceedingly—that God, from the fountain of his heart, draws us (like simple children to our mother) to himself, even to the right breast and bosom of our mother, so that we should long for him as children long for their mother.

4. For it is the pleasant food of my soul to see that my fellow-branches and members flourish in the Paradise of God.

5. But I will not hide from you the simple, childlike way that I walk in Christ Jesus; for I can write nothing of my own accord, but only as a child who neither knows nor understands anything. I have never been formally educated, but only know that which the Lord grants me to know, according to the measure in which he reveals himself in me.

6. For I never desired to know anything of the Divine Mystery, much less did I understand the way to seek or find it. I knew nothing of it, which is the condition of poor laypeople <note>original: "Lay-men." This refers to those without formal theological training or clerical standing; Böhme was a shoemaker by trade.</note> in their simplicity. I sought only the heart of Jesus Christ, so that I might hide myself there from the wrathful anger of God and the violent assaults of the Devil. I earnestly prayed to the Lord for his Holy Spirit and his grace, that he would be pleased to bless and guide me in him, and take away from me whatever turned me away from him. I resigned myself wholly to him, so that I might live not according to my own will, but to his, and that he alone might lead and direct me, so that I might be his child in his Son, Jesus Christ.

7. During this earnest Christian seeking and desire (in which I suffered many a sharp <note>original: "shrewd," which in this context means piercing, severe, or painful</note> repulse, but at last being resolved to risk my life rather than give up and quit), the gate was opened to me. In just a quarter of an hour, I saw and knew more than if I had spent many years together at a university.

8. For I saw and knew the "Being of all Beings," the *foundation and the †bottomless abyss <note>original: "Bysse" and "Abysse." 9. Immediately, it came powerfully into my mind to set this down in writing as a memorial for myself. Afterward, it fell upon me like a sudden shower that hits whatever it lands on; just so it happened to me—whatever I could grasp and bring into the external [part of my mind], I wrote down.

</margin>

13. I did not see this first book for three years; I assumed it was dead and gone until certain learned men sent me some copies of it and urged me to continue and reveal my talent. To this, my outward reason would not agree at all because it had already suffered so much for it. Furthermore, my spirit was very weak and timid, for my "High Light" was also withdrawn from me for a long time. It glowed within me like a hidden fire, so that I felt nothing but anguish and distress. Outwardly I found contempt, and inwardly a fiery prompting; yet I was not able to grasp that light until the breath (or inspiration) of the Most High helped me again and awakened new life in me. Then I obtained a better, deeper, and more grounded style of writing. I could express everything better in outward words, as is demonstrated in the book treating the 
<margin>† Or, According to.</margin>
*Threefold Life* †according to the three Principles; and the godly reader, whose heart is opened, shall see that this is so.

14. Thus I have now written, not from the instruction or knowledge received from men, nor from the learning or reading of books. Instead, I have written from my own "Book" which was opened within me—the noble likeness of God. This book of the noble and precious Image (meaning God’s own likeness) was granted to me to read. I have studied it as a child in its mother’s house, who watches what the father does and, in child-like play, imitates him. I have no need for any other book.

...the fire more strongly in me. In such inflammation, knowledge, and manifestation, I wrote my works.

17. Yet I did not intend to make myself known through them among such people as has now happened. I still thought I was writing for myself alone. Even though the Spirit of God—within the Mystery of God in my spirit—clearly showed me what the purpose was, my outward reason <note>Böhme uses "Reason" to mean the limited, worldly intellect that lacks divine insight.</note> was always opposed to it. The only exception was when the "Morning Star" <note>A symbol of divine illumination or the dawning of spiritual truth.</note> arose. Even then, my reason was ignited by it and danced along as if it had understood "the Pearl" <note>In Böhme’s work, the "Pearl" represents the precious, hidden truth of Christ or divine wisdom.</note>, yet it was far from doing so.

18. God dwells in the Noble Image <note>The "Noble Image" refers to the divine spark or the original, pure state of the human soul.</note>, but not in the spirit of the stars and elements. He possesses nothing but himself alone in his own likeness. Although he does possess all things, nothing can comprehend him except what originally arises and springs from him—namely, the soul created in the likeness of God.

19. Furthermore, all my writings are like those of a young student attending school. God, according to his will, has brought my soul into a wonderful school. In truth, I cannot claim or take credit for anything myself, as if my own person <note>original: "selfehood"</note> were anything or understood anything on its own.

20. No one should think more highly of me than what they see. The work in my studying or writing is not my own; I receive it only in the measure that the Lord is pleased to give it to me. I am nothing but his instrument, through which he accomplishes whatever he wills. I tell you this, my beloved friends, for your instruction and information, so that no one might value me more than I deserve—as if I were a man of great academic skill, deep understanding, or high reason. Instead, I live in weakness and frailty, in the childhood and simplicity of Christ. My sport and pastime is the childlike work he has assigned to me. Indeed, I take delight in it, as if it were a pleasure garden where many noble flowers grow. In the meantime, I will enjoy and refresh myself with it until I once again obtain the Flower of Paradise in the New Man <note>The "New Man" is the spiritual self reborn in Christ.</note>.

21. But because, dear sir and beloved friend, I see and perceive that you are seeking this path, I write to you diligently about my own simple, childlike journey. I understand that you use various authors and writings, and you desire my judgment on them. I will share my thoughts with you as a fellow member of Christ, so far as God has given me knowledge, but only in a brief summary. In my book *The Threefold Life*, you will find these matters explained at length, covering all details.

I do not wonder at this, for such learning comes from the outside, while God’s Spirit comes from within. Worldly reason consists of both good and evil; it is like the wind, which is moved and driven to and fro. It <margin>* Highly prizes.</margin> *esteems human judgment; and according to how the high and great ones—who hold the respect and authority of the world—judge and criticize, it gives its credit and verdict. It does not know the mind of the Lord, because His mind is not in it. Its understanding comes from the stars <note>In Böhme’s worldview, "the stars" represent the astral or natural influence on the human mind, which provides worldly intelligence but lacks divine light.</note>, and it is nothing else but a counterfeit shadow of fancy compared to divine wisdom.

23. How can a person judge divine matters if the Spirit of the Lord is not in him? The Spirit of the Lord alone tests, proves, and judges all things, for to Him only all things are known and revealed. But worldly reason judges only by outward appearances, and one person's reason always matches its judgment and opinion to that of another. The inferior person judges and criticizes just as his superior does—the layperson <note>term: "Lay-man" — A person who is not a member of the clergy or a specialized scholar.</note> follows the doctor <note>term: "Doctor" — Here, a highly educated theologian or academic authority.</note>. Yet neither of them understands the meaning, mind, and truth of the Lord without the Spirit of God, which judges within a person and respects no one’s status. To the Spirit, the layperson and the scholar are both the same.

24. Now, although the children of God have diverse and manifold gifts in writing, speaking, and judging, they do not all share the same manner of expression, phrasing, or style. From this, selfish reason afterward uses artificial conclusions to extract whatever serves its own purpose, building a Babel <note>term: "Babel" — A reference to the Tower of Babel, symbolizing the confusion and pride of human systems that lead to spiritual division.</note> for itself. From this, such a multitude and wearisome heap of opinions have arisen. Out of these writings, people have forged and invented various theories and ways to God, and others are forced to follow those paths. This has caused such controversies and unchristian contentions that people currently focus only on the strife of words and disputes about the literal text. Those who—according to their own logic and principles—win through verbal bickering and trading scripture for scripture are applauded. But this is nothing but Babel, a mother of spiritual prostitution <note>original: "whoredome"</note>, where reason does not enter through the door of Christ by Christ’s Spirit. Instead, it pushes its way in and climbs up by its own power, strength, and pride while remaining a stranger or unregenerated. It always wants to be the most favored child in the house, demanding that people honor and adore it.

26. For God does not bring a new or foreign spirit into us; instead, he opens our own spirit with his Spirit—namely, the Mystery of God's Wisdom, which lies within every person according to the measure, manner, and condition of their internal, hidden constellation. For Christ said, *My Father is working, and I am working as well* <note>John 5:17</note>. Now, the Father works in the essence of the soul's own nature <note>original: "property"</note>, and the Son works in the essence of God’s own image—that is, in the **divine likeness** or harmony.

27. The nature of the soul belongs to the Father; for Christ said, *Father, the people were yours, and you have given them to me, and I give to them eternal life* <note>John 17:6</note>. Since the nature of the soul is from eternity—of and from the Father—he has worked in it from eternity and still works in that same image forever. This includes both light and darkness, toward either of which the *will* of the soul’s nature tends to incline and surrender itself.

28. Since the Father’s nature or wisdom is immeasurable and infinite, and since he, being wisdom itself, works so that all things arise through his wisdom, the souls of men are therefore diversely constellated. Indeed, they all arise and originally proceed from one single essence, yet their operation is diverse and manifold, all according to God’s wisdom. Now the Spirit of Christ opens the nature of every soul, so that each speaks from its own unique nature about the wonders in the wisdom of God.

29. For the Spirit of God creates nothing new in a person, nor does he infuse a foreign spirit. Rather, he speaks of the wonders in God's wisdom through humanity. This happens not only from the eternal constellation but also from the external constellation—that is, through the spirit of the external world. He opens the soul's internal constellation within a person so that they may prophesy and foretell what the external heavens are working and producing. He is also driven to speak through the *Turba Magna* <note>original: "Turba Magna" — Latin for "The Great Turmoil." In Böhme's theology, this is the chaotic, destructive power of God's wrath that is triggered by human sin and disorder.</note>. As the prophets often spoke, they denounced the punishments that would come upon the people through the *Turba Magna* (with God’s permission) because of their violence and sinfulness. [And their bitter curses, wicked arguments, and wrathful indignation in their envious will toward one another awaken the sword of anger in the *Turba Magna*.]

31. And though it often happens that the spirit of the outward world makes its sport with its fantasies <note>original: "phansie" — imagination or mental images not grounded in divine truth.</note> in man—and from its own power and strong influence insinuates itself into the spirit of man, showing various strange and marvelous figures (which only find a place among those who follow their own reason alone in proud self-will, from which false prophets often arise)—yet I say that everyone speaks from their own constellation. One speaks through the manifestation of God’s spirit, truly and sincerely; and the other through the manifestation of the external *astral* spirit <note>original: "Astrall spirit" — In Böhme's philosophy, the "astral" refers to the influence of the physical stars and the natural world, which can provide natural intuition but lacks the certainty of divine revelation.</note>, which is uncertain and based on conjecture and guesswork. 32. And I say further, that all those precious men who have been illuminated by God (some of whose writings you may have at hand) have spoken from their manifestation and revelation, each according to his understanding or the capacity of his mind. Yet the center is the soul, and the light is God; the revelation is achieved and brought to pass by the opening or manifestation of God’s spirit through the constellation of the soul.

33. All the prophets from the beginning of the world have prophesied of Christ in different forms—one this way, another that. They have not all concurred in one style, phrase, and form; but each spoke according to how the Spirit of God revealed it to him in the eternal constellation of the soul. Yet they have all spoken from one center and ground. And even so it is nowadays: the children of God all speak from the revelation of Christ’s spirit, which is God’s; and every one according to his capacity, or that idea <note>original: "Idea" — In this context, a spiritual form or divine archetype shaped within the mind.</note> of wisdom which is formed in his mind. Therefore, I remind you as a friend, and exhort you not to listen to the vain babbling and prating of Reason, or to be moved by its proud censure and judgment, so as to condemn or despise the gifts of any man; for he who does so condemns the Spirit of God.

34. These authors whom you mention, and others besides (concerning whom you desire my judgment, and whom I have not read in full, but only in part), I do not wish to judge [or despise them]. God forbid; let that be far from me, even though they have not all written in the same style or form of expression. For knowledge is diverse and manifold. Yet it is necessary for me to test (according to my own gifts) their heart and will. But since I find that their heart and spirit do flow and spring from one and the same Center—namely, from the spirit of Christ—I therefore rest content with that Center. I commend their manner of expression to the *Highest Tongue, namely*, to the spirit of God's wisdom, which through that wisdom opens and reveals truth to everyone according to the measure and manner that pleases Him. <note>original: "Highest Tongue" — Böhme refers to the direct, divine language of the Spirit that transcends human dialects and academic terminology.</note>

35. I judge no one, for to condemn anyone is a false and idle arrogance and vain chatter. The spirit of God himself judges all things; if that spirit is in us, why should we care for such chatter? I much rather rejoice at the gifts of my brothers. If they have had a different manner of presenting their gifts than I have, should I therefore judge them?

36. Does any herb, flower, or tree say to another, "You are sour and dark; I will not stand by you"? Do they not all have one Mother from whom they grow? Even so, all souls proceed from One, and all men from one. Why then do we boast and glory in being the children of God, while we are more unwise than the flowers and herbs of the field? Is it not the same with us? Does not God impart and reveal his wisdom to us diversely? Just as He brings forth and manifests the *Tincture* <note>original: "Tincture" — In Böhme’s alchemy-influenced theology, the 'tincture' is the essential, life-giving spiritual quality or "dye" that imparts specific characteristics to a soul or substance.</note> of the *Mystery* <note>original: "Mystery" — The hidden, divine plan and the inner workings of creation.</note> in the earth, through the *earth* with beautiful plants, it is even so *in us men*. We should rather congratulate and heartily love one another because God reveals his wisdom so variously *in us*. But he who judges, condemns, and despises in a wicked way only runs on in pride to show himself off and to be seen. Such a person is the *Oppressor in Babel* <note>original: "Babel" — For Böhme, Babel represents the "city of confusion," specifically the institutionalized, prideful, and argumentative religious structures of his day.</note>, a perverse agitator who stirs up contention and strife.

37. The true test of God’s children is this, which we may securely and safely follow: namely, an humble heart that neither seeks nor honors itself, but continually seeks the good of its brother in love. It is a heart that seeks not its own profit, pleasure, or applause, but seeks after righteousness and the fear of God. The plain and simple way to come to God is this (so far as it has been made known to me): that a person depart from their sinful courses and make a sincere, constant purpose never to continue in those sins they have committed. In this forsaking and turning away from sin, they must not despair or doubt God’s grace.

38. And although reason suggests doubts (by which a sinner is terrified and stands amazed and astonished at the anger of God), yet let the will alone, in all simplicity and unfeigned sincerity, directly cast itself into the mercy of God. Let it wholly lie down and shroud itself in the suffering and death of Christ, and surrender itself to God through Christ. It should be like a child that betakes itself to its mother's lap, willing to do only that which is the mother's will. The child only cries and calls to the mother, always hoping to receive refreshment from her, and only longs for the mother's breasts. In the same way, our desire must be wholly and only turned and directed toward our first Mother, from whom we departed in Adam when we entered into <term>Self-Will</term>. <note>Self-Will: In Böhme's theology, this is the root of sin—the desire of the creature to be its own master rather than relying on God.</note>

39. Therefore Christ says, *Unless you are converted and become as children, you cannot see the Kingdom of God*. Also, you must be born again. This means we must wholly disclaim and depart from our own reason and return into resignation [and self-denial] into the bosom of our Mother. We must give up all disputing and, as it were, stun or mortify our reason so that the spirit of the Mother <note>namely, of the Eternal Word of God</note> may take a form in us. She must blow upon or enkindle the divine life in us, so that we may find ourselves in the spirit of the Mother, as if in a cradle, if we desire to be taught and guided by God.

40. And if we will be taught and guided by God, then we must arise again from the cradle and wholly submit and give ourselves up to Him. This is so that God's spirit may be in us wholly, both the will and the deed. We must acknowledge that knowledge is His and not ours, so that He alone may be our *knowing*.

41. We must take no thought or anxious care about what we are to know or how we will know it. We must merely enter into the incarnation and birth of Jesus Christ, and into his suffering and death. We must continually and willingly tread in *his footsteps* and follow him. We should think of ourselves as being here only on a pilgrim's path, walking through a dangerous way to enter again through Christ on the narrow path into our native country, from which Adam led us astray. In this way alone lies the pearl of the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: *Mysterium magnum*</note>. All studying, book-reading, seeking, searching, and building a foundation upon our received principles or "orthodox" understandings—if done outside of this way—are but dead means. They do not obtain the <term>Virgin's Crown</term> <note>original: the pearl of *Sophia* or Wisdom. Böhme often personifies Divine Wisdom as a Virgin.</note> but only gather heaps of thistles and thorns which sting and gall the children of God.

43. I have no controversy with the children of God because of the variety and diversity of their gifts. * I can reconcile them all within myself [I can form a good understanding of them for myself]. 44. Whatever it does with him is all the same to him, whether it be prosperity or adversity in this world, life or death; it is all the same to him. No adversity or calamity reaches the *new man*, but only the old man of this world. The world may do what it pleases with the old man, for it belongs to the world; but the new man belongs to God.

45. This is my way, my dear friend, in which I walk, and in which I must know without my own prior knowledge. I do not plan, premeditate, or muse beforehand what I am to write or speak; instead, I submit and resign myself to the knowledge of God. He may know in me whatever he pleases. In such a way as this, I have obtained a <term>Pearl</term> <note>Pearl: A reference to the "Pearl of Great Price" (Matthew 13:45-46), representing the discovery of the divine kingdom within the soul.</note> which I value more than the whole external world.

They may do this just as well at **home** in their own places. That which they think they are running from, they are likely to run into. It would be more acceptable to God for them to walk at home in a godly, divine way, so that others might follow their example.

49. Among them are arrogant, proud, scornful, and mocking people who do nothing but despise and look down on others. In many of them, this is only a mere habit or ritual, and a spiritual pride or selfish, <term>Pharisaical</term> <note>Pharisaical: Referring to the Pharisees of the New Testament; used here to describe someone who is legalistic, hypocritical, or performs religious acts for outward show rather than inward sincerity.</note> devotion. I can speak from my own experience on this: I besought and admonished one of them in a Christian, brotherly, and friendly manner because of a book he published. In that book, I found some points of great importance that were against God and the foundation of truth. I hoped that he would become enlightened, but he answered in a proud, contemptuous, and slanderous way. He gave an answer in which no marks or imprints of God's Spirit could be seen. Their **confession** [of faith] is more of an **opinion** than a true and sincere earnestness, for not all of them are what they boast and glory to be. There may be many honest hearts among them, but many are only <term>historical and titular</term> <note>historical and titular: Böhme is criticizing people who are Christians in name (title) and historical knowledge only, lacking a living, personal connection to the divine.</note> and desire only to show themselves and be applauded. I myself had experience with one of the chief men among them. They could learn at home how to despise other men [without running to an **outward, supposed Zion** <note>Zion: Often used by Böhme to represent the state of true spiritual peace or the "New Jerusalem" within the soul. He is mocking those who think they can find it by traveling to a specific physical location or group.</note>].

<margin>* To recall or retract themselves.</margin>
50. This is the way for the children to enter God’s Kingdom; moreover, their way is <term>*Revoca*</term> <note>original: *Revoca* (Latin). Meaning: "Recall" or "Retract." In this context, it refers to the spiritual act of turning back from the world and retracting one's selfish will.</note>. They make a show of this, but privately they remain as they were before. I pray to God that they were as earnest as they pretend to be, for then I would commend them too. But to slander, mock, and despise others is nothing else but **Babel** <note>Babel: A biblical reference to the Tower of Babel, used by Böhme to represent the confusion, pride, and false structures of worldly religious institutions.</note>. The world is already full of such people; I do not follow after them.

<margin>* Hans Weyrauck.</margin>
51. Concerning **John Weyrack**, as far as I can see from these writings of his, he may be one who walks in the love of God—if this way of his is held in the real sincerity of the heart. However, the fact that he taunts and disparages others because of their knowledge of the <term>light of nature</term> <note>light of nature: A central concept in Böhme’s thought, referring to the innate capacity of human reason and the natural world to reveal divine truths, provided it is guided by the Holy Spirit.</note> shows that he has no knowledge of it himself, and his gifts do not reach that far. Since he does not have such a gift, we must overlook it; yet despite this, we should still regard him as a true and honest brother. For God produces his gifts not only in simplicity, but in many people in a "high strain" [that is, in a deeply grounded understanding or a <term>magical</term> <note>magical: In Böhme’s terminology, "magical" (magisch) refers to the creative, spiritual power of the will and desire that brings things into being, rather than common sorcery.</note> meaning]. For He alone is high, and he orders and directs all his works as he pleases.

# The Second Epistle.

52. ...were not sufficiently capable of comprehending everything; yet for their *time*, they have done enough. But because this present time has need of another *medicine*, there are also found at this time other skillful, understanding demonstrators who know and point out the disease. All of this is according to God’s loving, providential care, who does not want any to perish, but that all people should be *helped and cured*.

53. If those same authors were alive today, they might have written more clearly on some points and in a different form. Although they did enough for their time, they are in no way to be despised and rejected, even if some points might be amended. But their doctrine concerning the *union of the Divinity and Humanity* is very clear; and we can see how God's Spirit was in them. However, Reason turns all things to the worst, and by its false explanations and logical commentaries <note>original: "glosses"</note>, twists <note>original: "wresteth"</note> them into a perverse sense.

<margin>* Schwenckfeld</margin>
54. * Schwenckfeld <note>Caspar Schwenckfeld von Ossig (1489–1561) was a German theologian who argued that Christ’s humanity was "celestial" and not a created thing, a point Böhme clarifies here.</note> stumbles at this point, in that he holds Christ to be no creature. He has not yet understood the <term>principles</term> <note>Principles: In Böhme's philosophy, the "Three Principles" are the foundational forces of reality: the dark fire-world, the light world (God’s love), and the physical world.</note>, and therefore it is impossible for him to distinguish how and in what way Christ is not a creature. For in respect to the *Deity*, he is no creature; but in respect to the heavenly *essence* (concerning which he said, *that he had come from Heaven and was also in Heaven*), he is <term>creatural</term> <note>creatural: having the form, limits, or properties of a created being.</note> within the humanity, and <term>uncreatural</term> <note>uncreatural: existing in an unformed, infinite, or universal state.</note> without the humanity.

55. Just as we humans live in the four elements, and we ourselves are the property of the four elements, they are creatural in us; but outside of us they are uncreatural. Yet the unformed, un-creaturalized elements outside of us in which we live, and the formed, creaturalized elements within us, are but one thing; and so it is in the person of Christ.

56. The whole Angelic World (which is the Second Principle) is his bodily being or personal essence. Regarding the heavenly essentiality in the person of his humanity, it is creatural, and outside the person it is uncreatural. For he is the *Father’s Heart and Word*, and the heart is everywhere in the *Father*; so wherever his heart is, there also is Heaven, and the divine essentiality is surrounded with the complete fullness of Wisdom.

57. Concerning his soul—which he commended into his Father’s hands, and of which he said upon the Mount of Olives, *that it was afflicted and heavy, even unto death*—it is of the same property as our soul. For it was for the soul's sake that God became man, so that he might bring the soul back into himself and draw our will back to him out of its earthliness; this soul is a creature.

If it were well considered, there would not be so much condemning and contending; the spirit of God does not care for any controversy; he judges all things in himself.

<margin>* Valentin Weigel <note>Valentin Weigel (1533–1588) was a German theologian and mystic whose ideas on the internal "living word" influenced later thinkers like Böhme.</note></margin>
59. Also, Weigel writes that Mary is not the daughter of Joachim and Anna, and that Christ assumed nothing from us, but that she is an eternal virgin. This indeed is true in respect to the mark or sign of the covenant, according to the Virgin of the Divine Wisdom. But how would this benefit me? What would become of my soul and my heavenly essence <note>original: "essentiality"</note> which disappeared in Adam [which is the paradisiacal image], if Christ had not taken upon himself the essence of our soul and brought the disappeared image back to life? This is explained at length in my book, *The Threefold Life*.

60. Apart from this, Weigel also writes very well about the new birth and of the union of humanity in Christ, in agreement with us. I will not speak more of it here because I have written clearly and precisely about it; I neither condemn nor despise his writings, nor those who read them.

61. Does not a bee gather honey from various flowers? And though one flower is better than another, she does not stop at that but takes what serves her purpose. If the sap and power <note>original: "vertue"</note> of the flower does not please her, should she therefore thrust her sting into it, as the despiser and mocker usually does? Men argue and dispute much about the shell [the outside of knowledge and religion] but disregard the precious sap [of love and faith] which serves and is useful for life.

62. What good does knowledge do for me if I do not live in and according to it? Knowing, as well as the will and the actual performance of that knowledge, must be within me. The cloak of Christ’s suffering and satisfaction <note>Satisfaction: The theological concept that Christ’s death paid the debt for human sin.</note>, which people now usually drape around themselves, shall become a snare and hellish fire to many. This is because they only tickle and flatter themselves with the merits and satisfaction of Christ, while still keeping their cunning hypocrisy and wickedness.

63. It is said, "*You must be born again, or else you shall not see the kingdom of God: You must become like children if you wish to see the kingdom of God.*" This means not only to argue and dispute about knowledge [and opinions], but you must become a new person [a new creature].

[The] week after *Easter*, but God disposed it otherwise; by his providence I happened upon another man, who led me out of that intended way to one who had need of me; so that afterward I understood that my way was from the Lord.

76. Mr. *Balthasar Walter* stayed this last Winter and Spring with the *Prince Augustus of Anhalt at Plötzkau* <note>original: "Tanhalt at Peltzka"</note>; and has written to me from there. Now he is with the *Earl of Gleichen* <note>original: "Gleyken"</note>, three miles from *Erfurt*; he is his physician and is to stay with him an entire year.

<margin>* Ezekiel Meth.</margin>
77. * Ezekiel Meth <note>A German mystic and associate of Böhme</note> is also at the same Court, yet they are not both of one mind, as the letter from *Balthasar* shows, which I received three weeks ago. If you have a desire to write, and no messenger is traveling this way, please send it to *Christianus Bernard*, the Receiver <term>Receiver</term> <note>A financial official or tax collector</note> at *Zagan* <note>original: "Zagan"; modern Żagań, Poland</note>. I have the opportunity to send mail to him weekly; he is a pious Christian companion.

78. If you find anything that is too hard and obscure <note>original: "dark"</note> to be understood in my writings, I pray you set it down and let me know, and I will make it plainer for you so that you may understand it. For the "wise" and "fully taught"—who are high and advance themselves in their own knowledge, who think they can walk alone and are already rich in wisdom—I have written nothing; but only for the infants and sucklings <note>A reference to Matthew 21:16 and Psalm 8:2, suggesting spiritual humility</note> who suck at their mother's breasts and would gladly learn.

79. He that can understand it, let him understand it; but he that cannot, let him not criticize or quibble over it. For such critics and mockers, I have written nothing; I have written for myself.

80. But if a brother thirsts and asks water of me, I give him a drink; he shall personally <note>original: "experimentally"</note> find and feel what I have given him, if the Lord grants him the drinking. I commend myself to your favor, and all of us into the pleasant and gracious love of *Jesus Christ*.

# A Letter to ABRAHAM of SOMMERFELD, Concerning the Book *AURORA*:

### ALSO,

# A Description of his process, and the excellence and surpassing virtue of *Sophia's Pearl.* <note>In Böhme’s theology, "Sophia" represents Divine Wisdom, and the "Pearl" symbolizes the precious spiritual insight or rebirth found within the soul.</note>

->*Light, salvation, and eternal power flowing from the wellspring of life, Jesus Christ, be our refreshment and comfort.*<-

<margin>1.</margin> Noble Lord, (first wishing you the grace of God and all health and happiness), having been informed that you take great delight, love, and affection in my writings—which until now were unknown to you—I must answer you that this brings an even greater delight and surpassing joy to my spirit. I say this because I understand that God is driving and carrying out His work in such great and high-ranking persons. This is not something commonly found in the world, for the temporal <term>temporal</term> <note>Worldly, material, or related to time, as opposed to eternal or spiritual things.</note> honor and pleasure of this life are usually a hindrance to it.

<margin>2.</margin> But I can clearly perceive how God’s Spirit has touched and awakened your noble heart. As a sign of this, you have devoted so much effort and expense to this work, which was written by a very simple and plain hand, without any "art" <note>original: "Art"; here meaning formal academic training or human scholarship</note> or great intellectual understanding (or extensive academic talent), but only through the knowledge and manifestation of the gifts of God. And more—

Moreover, it was not the author's intent that it should come into the hands of such high-ranking persons; because he wrote it only as a memorial to himself, to stir and rouse himself up from the dark and drowsy sleep of flesh and blood, and not with the intention to create such a work.

3. Indeed, there was a fiery prompting, but without foreknowledge of this work, which lay hidden in him as a mystery that the Spirit of God stirred up and awakened. At this, a great longing and desire to write arose. Yet, regarding the "outward man" <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "outward man" refers to the physical body and the rational, worldly mind, as opposed to the "inward" spiritual man.</note>, the author had no desire, capacity, fitness, or ability for it; for he sought only the heart of God, to hide himself there from the storm and raging tempest of the Devil.

4. And he considered the nature of evil and its working influences, and often the deceit of the Devil and the anger of God, as well as the love and mercy of God. Indeed, many a storm and strong encounter was held against Reason, and also against flesh and blood and the Devil—all driven by a powerful impulse and prompting of the Spirit. Finally, a most precious *garland* or *diadem* was set upon his head, which this hand cannot describe in writing. Instead, I wish the reader of this *epistle* <note>original: "Epistle"; a formal letter intended for instruction.</note> might find it through experience; then he would understand what the sweetness of God is, and not marvel so much why a layman <term>layman</term> <note>A person without formal university education or clerical status.</note> should undertake to meddle with such things [or write of such mysteries].

5. Therefore, I say now that when the precious grain of mustard seed <note>A biblical reference (Matthew 13:31) to something small that grows into a great spiritual reality.</note> was sown, this work was brought forth to be written. At that time, it was seen as a mystery buried very deep, without a full understanding, yet with exceeding joy. This work (being the first book) shows this; the great mysteries are set down very simply, without sufficient explanation or expression, and with much brevity and many gaps—like a sudden shower that passes by, hitting whatever it lands upon. The Spirit of Wonders works in the same way.

6. For the author was an unlearned man, of very small understanding and shallow capacity compared to the learned, skillful, and expert. Yes, he was like a mere child in the mysteries, who did not even understand the path he should walk or what might happen to him, except what the Spirit suggested and declared to him. He has also set down in writing the persecution, disgrace, and shame that would fall upon him before it actually happened—before Reason felt it or knew it through experience. This was shown as clearly as if it were already present, as can be seen in the book *Aurora*, which is the first part of my writings, produced before my persecution. And now it is a comfort to me, in that

# The Third Epistle.

...which the Spirit of God showed and foretold to me so much beforehand; so that I know what His counsel is in His way. Therefore, I willingly and patiently yielded myself under the Cross and committed my cause to God. I often entreated Him that if it did not come entirely from His own counsel, He should take it from me and not let me know or understand anything of that kind or proceed in that way.

7. I also intended (after the persecution) <note>Böhme was persecuted by the local Lutheran pastor, Gregorius Richter, who viewed his mystical writings as heretical.</note> not to write anymore, but only to keep myself still in obedience to my God, and to let the Devil roar over me with his scorn, revilement, and derision. In this, many a hard combat was fought against him, and what I endured I cannot well tell or declare. But it happened to me as with a grain that is sown into the earth, which, against all reason, springs up fresh in all storms and tempests; whereas in the winter everything seems dead, and reason says, "Now all is gone." Thus the precious grain of mustard seed <note>A biblical reference to the Kingdom of God starting as something small that grows into something great.</note> sprung up again under all dispraise, contempt, disdain, and derision, like a lily, and returned with a hundredfold increase, and also with deeper and more unique knowledge, and came forth again in a fiery prompting <note>original: "instigation"; here used as a divine impulse or driving force.</note> or forcible driving.

8. But my external man <note>The "external man" refers to the physical body and the rational, worldly mind.</note> would write no more; it was somewhat discouraged and timid, until it reached the point that the internal man <note>The "internal man" refers to the spiritual soul or the Christ-nature within.</note> captivated and overpowered the external. Even then ***the Great Mystery did Appear***; and then I understood God's counsel and cast myself upon His will. Also, I would not invent or feign anything out of Reason; neither would I give any more way or place to Reason. Instead, I resigned my will to God's will, so that my Reason might be as if it were dead, so that He (the Spirit of God) might do and work what and how He pleased; I willed nothing in Reason, so that it might be His will and deed alone.

9. And when this was done, then the internal man was armed and received a very faithful guide, and to him I wholly yielded my Reason. I did not study or invent anything, nor did I give Reason leave to dictate what I should write, except only that which the Spirit showed me as if in a great depth and full *Chaos* <note>original: "Chaos"; in Böhme's work, this refers to the *Mysterium Magnum* or the formless void from which God brings forth all things.</note> in the *Mystery*—yet without my having sufficient comprehension, for the creature is not like God, who does and comprehends all things at ***once*** in His wisdom.

10. And there was then a purpose in me again to write something, and in the space of nine months ***Three Books*** were made. One concerned the three principles of the Divine Essence—that is, of the ***Being*** of all Beings—wherein the great Mystery has somewhat opened and revealed itself. In that work, there are many excellent things contained that are much deeper than in this first work [<insert>namely, the Aurora</insert>].

# The Third Epistle.

(which Your Honor has sent here for me to examine), and it has about a hundred sheets of paper.

11. After this, there was another work produced containing sixty sheets, which treats the threefold life of man and also the whole of Creation. It is a great, open gate to the Mystery, and it is even a wonder that surpasses and goes beyond the reach of all reason. At this, I myself in my own reason wonder and marvel at what God intends to do—that He uses such a humble <note>original: "meane"</note> instrument for such weighty matters. For within it, those Mysteries are revealed and laid out which the world has fought and contended over since the heavy fall of Adam. Yet, such a foundation <note>original: "Ground"; referring to a fundamental spiritual basis or underlying reality.</note> has never been brought to light until now—which, nonetheless, will not be understood by the world, but only by the children of God, as is already manifest and known.

12. And then thirdly, forty questions were sent to me by a learned and insightful man who is also a lover and a great friend of the Mystery. He encouraged me to answer them according to these gifts and spirit. These are indeed very deep questions, and they contain the great depths and secrets of the origin of the soul <note>original: "Originall of the soule"</note> and all the secrets or mysteries of the Mystery. From these, an answer has been produced in which the world might well rejoice, if the anger, iniquity, and malice of the Devil did not hinder it. Yet, the counsel of God must stand.

13. Now, because I perceive that your noble mind and heart have a singular hunger and thirst for such Mysteries, and you do not care for the world which despises them, I recognize God’s counsel in this. It is my bounden duty to share this with you; for bread belongs to the children and they are worthy of it, but the pearl must not be cast before swine. My spirit and mind show me clearly enough that Your Honor does not search for such things out of curiosity, but by the prompting <note>original: "instigation"</note> and guidance of the Spirit—which many times leads Peter to Cornelius <note>A reference to Acts 10 in the New Testament, where the Apostle Peter is divinely directed to the Roman centurion Cornelius to share spiritual truth.</note> so that he may declare the words of eternal life to him.

14. And though I am a stranger and very simple, your desire and will embolden me to write to Your Honor, albeit with a simple hand <insert>in a plain and coarse phrase and style</insert> (for God’s gifts are not bound to any human arts). I am the more bold with you because I perceive that your noble heart appears so lowly and humble as to send for me, who am but a humble <note>original: "meane"</note> and abject person. But seeing it is thus, I also assuredly hope that the Spirit of God shall open the doors and gates of the Mysteries for your soul, and grant a right understanding to apprehend and know His wonderful gifts—which I heartily wish for Your Honor.

# The Third Epistle.

15. My writings will seem somewhat strange to you, for in some places the zeal is intense or earnest, especially against **Babel** <note>In Böhme's work, "Babel" refers to the "city of confusion"—the corrupted and divided state of organized religion.</note> and the **Antichrist**, who is known by God in His anger (or has come to His memory in wrath). Therefore, I say that I could not, nor dared not, write otherwise than what was given and dictated to me. I have continually written as the Spirit dictated it, and did not yield to human reason (or to the wisdom of the natural and astral spirit <note>original: "Astrall spirit"; referring to the influence of the stars and the physical cosmos on the human mind.</note>). I also do not acknowledge this as a work of my own reason, which was too weak; rather, it is the work of the Spirit, who has shown what He intends to do, what shall come to pass, and also what has already been done. For He proceeds out of the **Abyss** into the **Ground** <note>original: "Abysse into the Bysse"; Böhme uses "Abyss" for the groundless void of the divine, and "Bysse" (from the German *Bysen* or *Büsen*) to mean the 'ground' or the manifestation of that void.</note> and searches through all things. He tests the heart and mind <note>original: "reyns"; literally kidneys, used biblically to refer to the seat of emotions and hidden thoughts.</note> and proves the thoughts of men. Moreover, He hereby announces and declares the last *Judgment*: that He will test and examine every *being* through fire. I could not, nor was I permitted, to write at all (even during that fiery inspiration <note>original: "instigation"</note>) unless I set it down exactly as the Spirit represented it. Therefore, I have made it as a *memorial* to myself; I have no further intention for it beyond that.

16. But because you are eager to read it, I will send it to you. I pray that you return it to me afterward, for I wish to keep it as a memorial. I am certain that—as long as your noble mind gives praise to God, reads it diligently, and takes this path to heart with a desire for understanding—the Lord will open the door of His love to you within the Mystery. He will crown you with the diadem <note>A crown or headband worn as a symbol of sovereignty.</note> of His wisdom, which is more precious than the created Heaven and this world. For the precious *Philosopher's Stone* <note>A legendary substance in alchemy. For Böhme, it represents the spiritual catalyst that transforms the human soul back into its divine state.</note>, the basis of all *mysteries* and *secrets*, lies within it. This same diadem (or garland of wisdom) is set with this Stone. This diadem and crown of light in the Holy Spirit is what the soul puts on like a garment, becoming a new body in and for the Kingdom of God. In this state, the soul is a child of God and is able to stand in the fire of God's anger without any hurt or grief. Through it, the soul can overcome the Devil, Death, and this world. It can even rule over the stars, the poisonous influences of the constellations, and this outward life—which is otherwise impossible for human reason. For it provides that knowledge of things which no skill (or literal cleverness <note>original: "acrument"</note> from external reason) is able to discover or dive into. It sees through Heaven and Earth, and it reaps where it has not sown. It does not ask the question, "Is it true or not?" It possesses the sign of truth and righteousness within itself. It holds all virtues in hope; there is no fear of God's anger in it. It provides a very joyful hope, confirming and assuring the soul that it is indeed a child of God.
