# The Third Epistle.

17. This garland is a Virgin <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Virgin" represents Divine Wisdom (Sophia), the pure, feminine mirror of God’s glory and the bride of the soul.</note>, a chaste purity, and divine Beauty. It is a joy of the life; it comforts and rejoices the mind in affliction. It goes along with man into death, but it has no death or dying in it; it lives from eternity, and it is a guide into Heaven and the joy of the Angels. Its taste is more precious and pleasant than all the joys of this world; and he that once obtains it esteems it higher than all the goods and riches of this world. It cannot be paralleled except only with the Deity, but it lies hidden in a dark valley. The world does not know it; the Devil blows against it like a storm of wind and often so covers and disguises it that Reason does not recognize it. But it springs forth in its time as a fair lily with manifold fruits; it is sown in tears, and it grows in tribulation and affliction, but it is reaped with great joy. It is condemned and despised by reason, but he who obtains it holds it for his *best Treasure*.

18. Such a garland is set upon him who seeks after it with earnestness and wholly resigns himself unto it, but not to his "self" <note>original: "but not his selfe"; Böhme emphasizes "self-resignation" (*Gelassenheit*), the act of letting go of the ego to allow God to work through the person.</note>. Reason in flesh and blood does obtain it, as my writings fully testify; for what is written there, the author has known by experience. There is no strange hand or spirit foisted in. I write this not for my own vainglory (my boasting is only in God) but for a rule and direction to the children of God, so that they may know what reward God gives to those who put their trust and confidence in him and ignore the disapproval and contempt of the world.

19. I also wonder how you and many others in **Silesia** <note>A historical region in Central Europe, mostly in modern-day Poland.</note> have obtained my writings, for I have no acquaintance with any of them. I am so private regarding the publishing of them that the citizens here around me know nothing of them, except only for the first part, which was taken from me by force. By means of a person in the **Mystery of Babel** <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to represent the corrupted, worldly, and divided state of institutional churches.</note>—who persecuted it out of envy—it was proclaimed among them as heresy. Yet they never even read it, nor was it ever properly examined.

20. Indeed, I never asked any man’s advice about it, nor have I ever submitted it to human judgment or criticism until this very hour; instead, I entrusted it to God. Yet by this, I know and acknowledge the way of God. I also understand that it is known not only in **Silesia** but also in other countries without my prior knowledge. I must even say that he who so persecuted it has actually published it; for my intent was to keep it by me as long as I lived, and I wrote it for myself only.

...accordingly wonder and marvel at what God intends and will do; for I acknowledge myself to be altogether unworthy and ignorant, and yet the greatest and deepest mysteries are revealed to the internal man <note>The "internal man" refers to the spiritual soul or the "new man" born of God, as opposed to the "external man" governed by earthly reason.</note>, which I give to you and other lovers of God to consider in humility. For in truth, I cannot say at all that it is the work of my own understanding or reason; rather, I acknowledge it to be a *Wonder* in which God will reveal great things, into which my reason speculates and at which it continually marvels.

22. For I never in all my life studied these mysteries, and likewise knew nothing of them; for I am a layman <note>original: "Lay-man"; Böhme was a shoemaker by trade and lacked formal university education in theology or philosophy.</note>. And yet I must bring such things forth to light which all the higher schools or universities have not been able to do—compared to whom I am but a child and have none of their arts or wisdom. I must write from an entirely different school. And what is even greater than all this, the <term>Language of Nature</term> <note>The "Language of Nature" (*Natursprache*) is Böhme's concept that the inner essence of all things is expressed through their outward form, sounds, and names.</note> is made known to me, so that I can understand the greatest mysteries in my own *mother tongue*.

23. Though I cannot say that I have learned or comprehended it on my own, as long as the hand of God stays upon me, I understand it. But if it hides itself, then I do not even recognize my own labor and become a stranger to the work of my own hands. By this I may see how altogether impossible a thing it is to search out and apprehend the mysteries of God without God's Spirit. Therefore, I ascribe and attribute nothing to myself; it is not my work, and I desire no human applause or honor for it.

24. I am only a simple, humble instrument; God works and makes what He pleases. What God wills, that I will also; and whatever He does not will, I also do not will. If it is His will for me to know anything, then I will know it; but if He does not will it, then I do not either. *I will be nothing, and dead, so that He may live and work in me whatever He pleases.* I have cast myself wholly into Him, so that I may be safe and secure from the Devil.

25. And though I must leave my outward body and life to the world's disposal and suffer the Devil to roar against me, yet I will not trust either the Devil or the world with my internal man. Neither will I do (according to the inward man) what the world wants me to do. And although my outward man is bound and obligated to the world, and in its obligation and allegiance must obey the laws and ordinances of the world and do what that outward obligation requires of me, yet my internal man shall only be obedient to God and not to the world. For he is not in the world, but has made himself dead to it, so that God might live in him and be both the will and the deed in him. And though I cannot say that it is possible to live so in perfection, yet my will is...

# The Third Epistle.

17. This garland <note>The "garland" or "crown" is a frequent metaphor in Böhme’s work for Divine Wisdom (Sophia) or the spiritual state of a soul reunited with God.</note> is a virgin, a chaste purity, and divine beauty; it is a joy of the life that comforts and rejoices the mind in affliction. It goes along with man into death, but it has no death or dying in it. It lives from eternity and is a guide into heaven and the joy of the angels. Its taste is more precious and pleasant than all the joys of this world; and he who once obtains it esteems it higher than all the goods and riches of this world. It cannot be paralleled with anything except the Deity, but it lies hidden in a dark valley. The world knows it not; the Devil blows against it like a storm of wind and often so covers and disguises it that **reason** <note>In Böhme’s terminology, "Reason" (*Vernunft*) often refers to the limited, earthly intellect that cannot perceive divine truths without spiritual illumination.</note> does not recognize it. But it springs forth in its own time as a fair lily with many fruits; it is sown in tears and grows in tribulation and affliction, but it is reaped with great joy. It is condemned and despised by reason, but he who obtains it holds it for his *best treasure*.

18. Such a garland is set upon him who seeks after it with earnestness and wholly resigns himself to it; but one's own **reason** in flesh and blood does not obtain it, as my writings fully testify. For what is written there, the author has known by experience; no strange hand or spirit has been foisted in. I do not write this for my own vain glory (my boasting is only in God) but for a rule and direction to the children of God, so that they may know what reward God gives to those who put their trust and confidence in him and ignore the criticism and contempt of the world.

19. I also wonder how you and many others in *Silesia* <note>A historical region now mostly in Poland, but then part of the lands of the Bohemian Crown.</note> have obtained my writings, for I have no acquaintance with any of them. I am so private regarding the publishing of them that the citizens here around me know nothing of them, except for the first part, which was taken from me by force. By means of a person in the **Mystery of Babel** <note>original: "Mysterie of Babel"; Böhme used this term to describe the institutional, sectarian, and argumentative church structures of his day, which he believed confused and imprisoned the true spirit of Christianity.</note> (*who persecuted it out of envy*), it *was proclaimed among them as heresy*. Nevertheless, they never read it, nor was it ever examined as was appropriate.

20. Indeed, I never asked any man's advice about it, nor have I ever committed it to the scrutiny and judgment of man to this very hour, but instead commended it to God. Yet by this, I know and acknowledge the way of God; likewise, I understand that it is known not only in *Silesia* but also in other countries without my prior knowledge. I must even say that he who has so persecuted it has thereby published it; for my intent was to keep it by me as long as I lived, <margin>* The Three Principles, and the Threefold Life <note>These are two of Böhme's major works: *The Three Principles of the Divine Essence* (1619) and *The Threefold Life of Man* (1620).</note></margin> and I wrote it for myself alone.

21. But what God purposed in his counsel is now revealed, and it shall yet appear more clearly when the *two latest books shall be read, at which I myself in the external man* <note>The "external man" is the physical, earthly personality, as opposed to the "internal" or spiritual man.</note> *do exceedingly*

# The Third Epistle.

21. I greatly wonder and marvel at what God intends and will do, for I acknowledge myself to be altogether unworthy and ignorant. Yet the greatest and deepest mysteries are revealed to the internal man <note>The "internal man" refers to the spiritual self or soul, which Böhme distinguishes from the "external" physical body and the "reason" of the flesh.</note>, which I give to you and other lovers of God to consider in humility. For in truth, I cannot say at all that it is the work of my own understanding or reason; but I acknowledge it to be a *Wonder*, wherein God will reveal great things, into which my reason speculates <note>original: "speculate"—in this context, meaning to contemplate or behold deeply.</note> and continually marvels.

22. For I never studied these mysteries in all my life and likewise knew nothing of them, for I am a layman <note>Böhme was a shoemaker by trade and had no formal university training in theology or philosophy.</note>. And yet I must bring such things to light that all the high schools or universities have not been able to do; compared to them, I am but a child and have none of their arts or wisdom. I must write from an entirely different school; and what is even greater than all this, the *Language of Nature* <note>The "Language of Nature" (Natursprache) is a central Böhmean concept suggesting that the true names and essences of things can be understood through spiritual illumination.</note> is made known to me, so that I can understand the greatest mysteries in my own *mother tongue*.

23. Although I cannot say that I have learned or comprehended it on my own, I understand it as long as the hand of God stays upon me. But if it hides itself, then I do not recognize my own labor and am made a stranger to the work of my own hands. By this I may see how completely impossible it is to search out and grasp the mysteries of God without God's Spirit. Therefore, I ascribe and attribute nothing to myself; it is not my work, and I desire no human applause or honor for it.

24. I am only a simple, humble instrument; God works and makes whatever He pleases. Whatever God wills, that I will also; and whatever He does not will, I likewise do not will. If it is His will for me to know anything, then I will know it; but if He does not will it, then I do so also. *I will be nothing and dead, that He may live and work in me as He pleases.* I have cast myself wholly into Him, so that I may be safe and secure from the Devil.

25. And though I must leave my outward body and life to the disposal of the world and suffer the Devil to roar against me, yet I will trust neither the Devil nor the world with my internal man. Neither will I do (according to the inward man) what the world wants me to do. And although my outward man is bound and obligated to the world—and in its obligation and allegiance must obey the laws and ordinances of the world and do what the outward obligation requires of me—yet my internal man shall only be obedient to God and not to the world. For he is not in the world, but has made himself dead to it, so that God might live in him and be both the will and the deed in him. And though I cannot say that it is possible to live so [in perfection], yet my will is...

26. I have related this to you at length so that you may know and acknowledge what kind of man I am, and what the beginning and cause of my writing is, and from what art <note>original: "Art"—here meaning a systematic skill or spiritual knowledge rather than formal academic study.</note> and spirit it was produced or generated—and also to what end. Namely, I wrote it to keep as a memorial for myself; but because I perceive honest, religious hearts thirsting after it, I will not conceal it from them <insert>but impart it</insert> in a brotherly and Christian way. 27. Although God has His children among them as well, I do not care to have my name attached to this or credited to me. For the praise belongs to God, who is the giver; I do not seek to make a great and glorious name for myself through this. Instead, Christ is my reward, my name, and my glory; I hope to have the glory of it in the life to come before angels and men, and to rejoice in it with the saints in Christ, as my writings sufficiently testify.

28. Concerning the book *Aurora*, which your Honor has sent me to peruse, I have read some of it and find that it is my work and well copied. Some syllables are left out for the sake of brevity, yet the sense and meaning are not diminished by that. I am well contented regardless, since (so far as I have perused it in haste) I have found no additions. However, the great mysteries are embedded very deeply within it; they were understood and grasped by the author, but it was not very possible for reason to comprehend them at first. Although they were well known in the depths, the author was not accustomed to them. When heavenly joy met him, he only followed the spirit's guidance; the wild nature is not immediately regenerated <note>original: "regenerated"—meaning spiritually reborn or transformed into a "new creature."</note> <insert>or made a new creature</insert>. Indeed, if a kernel <note>original: "Kernell"—the seed or essence of a plant.</note> is sown, a tree grows; but if the virtue <note>original: "vertue"—referring to the inherent spiritual power or life-force within the seed.</note> is great <insert>if the power of the resolution is strong and the practice sincere and constant</insert>, the tree grows up all the sooner and is the sooner recognized.

# The Third Epistle.

29. In the other three books you shall find the mysteries more clearly, and so on throughout; the further you go, the deeper they become. Each book after the first is grounded ten times deeper, so that the fourth is a very clear mirror in which the "Great Mystery" <note>original: "Great Mystery" or *Mysterium Magnum*—a central concept in Böhme’s work referring to the source of all things.</note> is sufficiently and visibly seen and understood, yet only by its "Children" <note>Those spiritually prepared to receive the teaching.</note>. Reason shall remain blind, for the spirit of God does not dwell in the outward Principle, but in the inward; it proceeds forth from the inward into the outward principle of this world, yet the outward does not comprehend him.

30. But Sir, I must tell you that the book *Aurora* <note>original: "Aurora"—Latin for "the dawn."</note> was not finished, for the Devil intended to make a bonfire of it because he saw that the day would break forth in it. But despite that, the day has even overtaken the *Aurora* [or morning], so that it is already clear day. There belong yet about thirty sheets to it; but because the storm [of persecution] broke them off, it was not finished. In the meantime, it has become daylight, and the morning is extinguished; since that time, the work has been to bring forth the day. Yet it shall remain as it is for an eternal remembrance, because the deficiency is restored and supplied in the *Second* <margin>* The Book of the Three Principles.</margin>; the fault and blame for the deficiency is to be attributed to the Enemy.

31. But I will lay the fault upon no one but the falsehood and iniquity of the Devil, who is an enemy to all good. He even confounds and entangles Kings; how then shall a poor, humble man, being employed in such a work, be so quickly acknowledged and known? If it is surely affirmed that he is a layman and also unlearned, those very wise and skillful in the arts will be offended at the plainness and simplicity of such a thing. When a scholar hears one speak of such wonders and deep mysteries in such a mean and simple way [without academic pomp of words and artificial terms and phrases of logic and rhetoric], then he thinks it is a "Rhapsody" <note>original: "Rapsodie"—here meaning a confused heap of notions or a disorganized collection.</note> [or some confused heap of notions packed together, a fanatical, imaginary "hotch-potch" of whimsies, or a bundle of nonsense]. For he does not understand the gifts of God and is also unable to see into the heart of another. Therefore, I will disturb no man and desire no one to trouble himself about it; but I confess that it is God’s providence, otherwise this book would have still lain in a corner.

32. But thus it was published without my knowledge, consent, or will, and that *by the persecutors themselves*. I acknowledge this to be from the providence and appointment of God, for I had no copy of it for myself. Neither did I ever know those who have it; I do not have it myself, and yet it has been copied out; and

# The Third Epistle.

[The work has been] brought to my sight and hands four times already, so that I see that others have published it. I consider it a wonderful work, that the grain grows against the will of the Enemy; but that which is sown by God, no one can hinder or stop from growing.

33. But what you and others also misunderstand in my book *Aurora* <note>original: "Aurora"—Latin for "The Dawn," the title of Böhme's first book.</note> (which appears to be wrong in its interpretation, and which also needs some clarification and explanation), you shall find sufficiently cleared at length in my third and fourth books. In these, there is an open gate to the mysteries of all beings; indeed, there is nothing in Nature that might not be fundamentally searched out and grounded in this way. For it shows and opens the *Stone of the Wise* <note>original: "Stone of the wise men"—The Philosopher's Stone, an alchemical substance thought to transform matter; Böhme uses it to represent spiritual transmutation.</note> to all the secrets and mysteries of both the divine and earthly Mystery. Through this knowledge and understanding, all the metals of the Earth may be brought to the highest degree or perfection—yet only by the children of the divine *Magic* <note>original: "Magia"—referring to the divine creative power rather than sorcery.</note>, who have the *Revelation* [or experimental science] of it.

34. I see it well enough, but I have no manual skill, urge, or art for it; instead, I only set forth an open Mystery, for which God shall stir up laborers of His own. Let no man seek the physical work from me, or think to get the knowledge and operation of the Philosopher's Stone [or universal tincture] from me. And though it is clearly known and could be explained more clearly, yet I have surrendered my own will and will write nothing except as it is given to me, so that it may not be my own work, lest I should be imprisoned in the *Disturbance* <note>original: "Turba"—Böhme’s term for the source of wrath, confusion, or the "disturbance" of the divine order.</note>.

35. And if you wish to have anything copied out of these writings now sent to you, it is necessary that the transcriber be a learned and understanding man. Many syllables are not fully written, nor do they follow standard spelling; in many words, some letters may be missing, and sometimes a capital letter stands for a whole word. For formal art did not write here, nor was there any time to consider how to set it down precisely according to the correct understanding of the letters. Instead, everything was ordered according to the direction of the Spirit, which often moved in haste, so that the writer's hand (because he was not accustomed to it) often shook. Although I could have written in a more accurate, beautiful, and plain manner, the reason [I did not] was this: the burning fire often forced forward with *speed*, and the hand and pen had to hasten directly after it. For it comes and goes like a sudden shower; whatever it falls upon, it hits. If it were possible to comprehend

<meta>This page continues Jakob Böhme’s explanation of his writing style and the reasons behind the complexity of his books. He addresses the potential for readers to find contradictions in his work and clarifies his use of the first-person plural ("we") versus the singular ("I").</meta>

# The Third Epistle.

[If I were to] comprehend and write all that my mind beholds in the Divine Chaos <note>original: "Divine CHAOS"—In Böhme’s terminology, this refers to the *Ungrund*, the infinite, unmanifested source or "abyss" from which all existence arises.</note>, the work would then be three times longer and more deeply grounded.

36. But it cannot be, and therefore more than one book has been made; there is more than one philosophical discourse, each getting progressively deeper. This was done so that what could not be contained in one might be found in another. It would be well if at last, out of all of them, only one single book might be made and all the others set aside. This is because the multiplicity and variety of books causes strife, opposition, resentment, and wrong understandings. This happens because of the hasty ideas and conjectures of the *Reader*, who does not know how to test and discern the spirit that uses such wonderful phrasing. Often, Reason supposes that the text contradicts itself, and yet in the depths, it is not contrary at all.

37. From this misunderstanding—or rather, from the false interpretations of human Reason and literal, external scholarship applied to the writings of holy men—the *Great Babel* <note>original: "Great Babel"—A reference to the biblical Tower of Babel, used here to represent the confusion, sectarianism, and verbal strife found in institutional religion.</note> has been brought forth upon the earth. In Babel, men contend for nothing but words, while they leave the spirit of understanding in the Mystery alone. But its end and its "number" <note>A reference to the biblical "number of the beast" or the calculated end of an age.</note> are found and committed to the *Turba* <note>original: "Turba"—Latin for "uproar" or "crowd." Böhme uses it to describe the "spirit of the disturber," the awakening of divine wrath that breaks down corrupted or false systems.</note>; for the beginning has reached its limit. There is no longer any withholding or staying of the wrath of God upon Babel; it cannot be quashed by any power or force of arms.

38. I speak not of and from myself, but from that which the Spirit shows, which no man can resist. For it stands in its *Omnipotence* <note>original: "Omnipotence"—all-powerfulness.</note> and does not depend on our imagining or desiring, as the *Fourth Book* of these writings declares very deeply. That book is strongly grounded in the light of nature <note>original: "light of nature"—the understanding of spiritual truths by observing the laws and patterns of the physical world.</note> and can be demonstrated in all things.
<margin>* The Forty Questions.</margin>

39. Furthermore, I want you to understand that in these writings which are now sent to you, the author sometimes uses the words *We* and sometimes *I*. You should understand the word *We* to mean the Spirit speaking through two persons (being spoken in the plural); and by the word *I*, the author refers to himself. I give you this as a direction and information to prevent wrong understandings and suspicion.

40. And herewith I send you the *Fourth Part*, being the *Forty Questions* <note>This refers to Böhme's work *Forty Questions on the Soul* (1620).</note>, and in them you may behold yourself. At the next opportunity, I will send you the *Second and Third Parts* if you desire to have them. I pray that you return this manuscript to me by the next occasion, for I must send it to the person who framed and sent the questions to me. And so, I commend and commit you to the love of God.

# A Letter to
# PAUL KEYM:
### BEING
## An answer to him concerning
->Our Last Times.<-

### Wherein he treats of *the first resurrection of the dead and the thousand-year Sabbath.*

### ALSO,
### Of the fall of BABEL <note>original: "BABEL"—In Böhme’s writing, Babel represents the confused, divided, and corrupt state of the institutionalized church and worldly systems.</note>, and of the new building in ZION <note>original: "ZYON"—Symbolizing the true, unified spiritual community or the heavenly city of God.</note>.

->*May light, salvation, and eternal power, flowing from the fountain of the heart of Jesus Christ, be our quickening consolation.*<-

---

WORTHY and much-esteemed sir, and good friend in the illumination of the Holy Spirit; and beloved brother in the love of our Lord Jesus Christ:

I received from Mr. *C. E.* the letter you sent me, dated around July 20th, along with two small treatises attached. From your letter, I understand that you have received and read some of my short manuscripts concerning the wisdom of God, and as you affirm, they have brought you joy. Furthermore, you express a great desire and longing for them, as you are engaged in a similar exercise in the wisdom of God.

3. Which, for my part, also causes me to rejoice to see that even now the time is at hand when true divine understanding and the true knowledge of God are again springing forth in Zion <note>original: "Zyon"—In Böhme's thought, Zion represents the true, spiritual church of the heart.</note>; and that the ruined Jerusalem shall again be built up; and that man's true Image—which disappeared and died out in Adam—is again putting itself forward in Zion with a true human voice; and that God is pouring out His spirit into us, so that the precious Pearl, in the power and light of the Holy Spirit, is again known, sought, and found.

4. By this, we clearly see and understand what blindness we have lived in for a long time in Babel <note>original: "Babel"—Symbolizing the confusion and corruption of institutionalized religious systems.</note>, going astray in carnal, evil ways. By these ways, we have forsaken the true Jerusalem, shamefully misspent our inheritance <note>original: "Patrimony"</note>, and lightly valued our angelic trophy or crown <note>original: "Diadem"</note> (namely, that beautiful Image), and wallowed in the filth of the Devil. Under a pretense of divine obedience, we have played with the Serpent and walked in nothing but erroneous ways. The divine light now sets this before our eyes and exhorts us to return with the lost son <note>A reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15.</note> and enter into the true Zion.

5. We must not do this with historical assumptions, opinions, or blind beliefs, as if we already perceived and understood it very well. That is not Zion, but Babel, which confesses God with its mouth and makes devout speeches to Him with its lips, but in its heart clings to the great Whore of Babylon <note>A figure from the Book of Revelation representing spiritual corruption and worldly desires.</note>—to the Dragon of self-love, pride, greed, and pleasure—and yet tries to present itself as if it were a virgin. No, this is not the Virgin in Zion; there must be a genuine seriousness.

6. We must be born of God in Zion, and know and also do His will. God’s spirit must bear witness to our spirit that we are God’s children—not only in our speech with knowledge and theories, but in the heart in very deed. It must not be in a way that only seems holy but lacks power [in formal ways of word-worship and cycles of lip-service <note>original: "Lip-labour"—Empty religious rituals that involve speaking without heart-felt conviction.</note>, in which the captive conscience places the power of godliness]. The Devil mocks this and does not care for it. Instead, we must put on the helmet of righteousness, love, chastity, and purity if we intend to battle the Prince of this world <note>A title for the Devil.</note>. He does not care a bit for any outward show [or for the long and loud vocal cries of blind devotion]. It must be power that shall overcome him, and that power must shine forth in goodness and the holy fruits of Christianity; in this way, we may fight for the noble prize, the crown of life.

7. For we have a powerful warrior against us; he attacks us in body and soul and quickly casts us down. There is no other way to overcome him except with power through humility, which alone is able—

...able to quench his poisonous fire, with which he fights without us and within us against our noble Image.

8. Therefore, beloved Sir and brother in Christ, seeing that you apply yourself to Divine wisdom and labor in the same, it is right and necessary that we exhort one another to be vigilant to withstand the Devil. We must continually set before our eyes the way which we ought to walk and also go on in that same way; otherwise, we accomplish nothing. If we know that the world is blind in Babel <note>original: "Babel"—Symbolizing the confusion and spiritual corruption of the institutionalized church systems.</note> and goes astray, then we must be the first who effectively go out of Babel, so that the world may see that we are in earnest.

9. It is not enough that we expose and manifest Babel, yet are found doing as Babel does; for if we do so, we thereby testify that God reveals His light to us so that we see, but we will do nothing but the works of darkness. That very light which enlightens our understanding shall witness against us—that the Lord has called us and shown us the way, but we would not walk in it.

10. It is well that we expose Babel, but we must take heed in what spirit and mind, and in what kind of knowledge, this is done. It is good that we be zealous, but the heart must be upright toward God; otherwise, we run without being sent, and in our course, we are not known or acknowledged by God. By acting so, the Devil mocks us and leads us into by-paths of error.

11. Besides, the Holy Scripture declares that our works and words shall follow us. Therefore, we are seriously to consider in what spirit and knowledge we set upon the high mysteries. For he who will tear down a thing that is evil must set up a better one in its place; otherwise, he is none of God’s builders. Also, he does not labor in Christ’s vineyard, for it is not good to tear down unless a man knows how to rebuild the structure again in a better frame and form.

12. For God alone is the Master-builder of the world; we are but servants. We must take great heed how we labor if we wish to receive a reward, and also ensure that we have learned His work in His school and do not run without being sent when we are not yet capable of His service. Otherwise, we shall be found to be unprofitable servants. This I speak in good-will and in all faithfulness to instruct and direct one another in what we ought to do, so that our labor may be accepted by God.

13. For the dark mysteries are in no other way at all to be known except only in the Holy Spirit. We cannot reach conclusions upon hidden things unless we have the same in real knowledge and experimentally find, in the illumination of God, that what we aver <note>original: "averre"—To state or assert as the truth.</note> is the truth and will of God, and that it is also consistent with His Word; and

# The Fourth Epistle.

...grounded in the light of Nature; for without the light of Nature, there is no understanding of Divine Mysteries. <note>original: "light of Nature"—Böhme’s term for the inherent capacity to perceive the divine order within the physical and spiritual world.</note>

14. The great Building of God is manifest in the light of Nature; and therefore he whom God's light illuminates may search out and know all things. However, knowledge does not come in one and the same way or measure for everyone; for God’s wonders and works are boundless, infinite, and immense. They are revealed to every person according to their gifts, and he to whom the light shines has pure joy in God’s works.

15. Also, that which is old and passed away over a thousand years ago is as near and as easily known in the light as that which is done today. For a thousand years before God are scarcely as much as a minute, or the twinkling of an eye is before us; therefore, all things are near and manifest to His spirit, both that which is past and that which is to come.

16. And if we see in His light, then we must declare His wonders, and manifest and praise His glorious Name, and *not bury* our Talent in the Earth. <note>original: "Talent"—referring to the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25, where servants are expected to use their God-given gifts for the benefit of their master.</note> For we must deliver it unto our Master with *Increase*; He will require an account from us of how we have traded with it. Without knowledge or certain illumination from God, no man should presume to judge, or be a *Doctor* <note>original: "Doctor"—here meaning a high-ranking teacher or scholar of theology.</note>, or Master in the great Mystery; for it is not committed to or commanded of him. Instead, he must labor to attain the true light, and then he goes rightly to work in the School of God.

17. For there are many masters to be found who presume to judge in the Mystery, and yet they are not known or sent by God; and therefore their *School* is called *Babel* <note>original: "Babel"—symbolizing confusion and the corrupt institutional church.</note>, the Mother of Whoredome <note>original: "Whoredome"—in this context, spiritual infidelity or the corruption of sacred truth for worldly gain.</note> upon Earth. They flatter both sides; they play the hypocrites with God, and also serve the Devil. They call themselves the shepherds and pastors of Jesus Christ; they run, and yet are not sent, much less does God own them. What they do, they do for their own honor and for their \* belly's sake; and they would not run at all if they did not obtain profit in their course of spiritual whoredome and hypocrisy.
<margin>Their livelihoods.</margin>

18. They have turned the right and exceedingly precious Mystery of God into a mystery of their whoredome and pleasure. Therefore, the Spirit calls it *Babel*, a Confusion, where men practice a hypocritical service and worship of God; acknowledging Him with the tongue, but denying Him in the power; where men dissemble and flatter God with their lips, but in their hearts they embrace and love the Dragon (mentioned in the *Revelation*). <note>original: "Dragon"—a reference to the beast or Satan as described in the Book of Revelation.</note>

19. We must not be like such people as these if we would obtain the Divine Mystery and be capable of the light. Rather, we must wholly submit our way to God and resign ourselves up to Him, so that God's light may shine...

You also write that the fire of God—which is his anger and the hellish power <note>original: "source"</note>—shall be within them, and that they shall be tormented here upon the Earth in the four elements <term>In Böhme's philosophy, the "four elements" represent the material world defined by conflict and decay.</term> within the anger of God. However, the anger of God is *not* fully revealed in the four elements, for within them good and evil are mixed together.

63. But how shall someone who is already dead to goodness, and cannot have even a single good thought, beg the saints for faith and comfort? This indicates, rather, that when Christ comes to judge the world, they shall all still dwell together in the flesh, within the four elements, where one shall be received and the other rejected. The sins of the wicked shall then appear before them at the revelation of the severe face of God, in the fiery zeal of the first principle <term>The "First Principle" refers to the foundational, wrathful fire of God's essence, separate from His light and love.</term>. At that sight, the wicked will be terrified and would then gladly begin to be honest.

64. And though you mention that they shall only awaken and not truly "rise," it is the uncorrupted who are to be understood here. Now, you say that they shall dwell upon the Earth in the four elements while the saints dwell in Paradise. If this were to happen, there would no longer be any strife or controversy, because they would be eternally separated.

65. But if the saints were to dwell upon the Earth in Paradise—just as Adam did before the Fall—and the ungodly were set in opposition to them, they would be in as much danger as Adam was. They might again eat of the forbidden fruit, by which they would have to die once more.

66. Furthermore, if they are to be hidden from the ungodly for a thousand years, and hidden from the four elements as well, why should they be revealed in the four elements at the very end, so that Gog and Magog <note>Biblical names for the enemies of God's people who gather for a final battle in the Book of Revelation.</note> could then enter into battle with the children of Paradise? This agrees with neither Scripture nor reason.

67. The first epistle of Saint Paul to the Corinthians, chapter 15, does indeed teach of Christ’s resurrection and of our own, yet it does not mention a third resurrection. It speaks first of Christ's, and then of ours; for he says there *that Christ is the first fruits*, and then those who belong to Christ. This is the general resurrection. And though he says, *then comes the end*, he does not mean that "the end" is a different resurrection. Rather, "the end" is our resurrection itself. This is a much better understanding than suggesting that by "the end" he meant another resurrection entirely.

<summary>Böhme argues that a physical, earthly "Sabbath" shared by the resurrected saints and the wicked is illogical, as the resurrection transforms the saints into a spiritual state beyond the "four elements" of the material world. He uses St. Paul to argue for a single general resurrection rather than multiple stages.</summary>

All of this was finished in *six days*; and in such a time, the mystery of God’s kingdom shall be *finished*, and a thousand years are to him as one day <note>2 Peter 3:8</note>.

71. Concerning the seventh day of rest—whether or not the world shall yet be at rest for a thousand years—that is hidden from mankind. We cannot certainly determine this; we must leave it to his power. I have no knowledge of it, since the Scripture does not give clear evidence as to when the thousand years begin, what years they are, or to what they relate. Therefore, I leave it alone for what it is worth, and will hinder no one who has certain knowledge or a command to teach it. I give you this to consider, intending it for your benefit.

72. Whatever further answer I might give concerning this matter, you can find it sufficiently in my writings. Although I could set down a lengthy answer about it, I did not think it appropriate <note>original: "expedient"</note> since this knowledge is not given to me. Therefore, I leave it alone, for I know that I must give an account of my works. I am returning your two books by the bearer of this letter, and I thank you for them.

74. To me, indeed, it is given to know that the time is near and even now at hand, but the year and day I do not know. Therefore, I leave it to God’s counsel and to those to whom God shall reveal it; I cannot conclude anything without certain knowledge, otherwise I would be found a *liar* before God.

76. Humans can hardly understand that which is before their eyes, much less that which is hidden and mystical, unless God is their light. # The Fourth Epistle.

...had been left out, since you have not understood *their* opinion, as you say—and so it certainly seems. You shall find sufficient and extensive information in my book, the *Forty Questions* [specifically around the thirtieth question] concerning the Last Judgment, as well as in other questions, if they are read and rightly understood.

92. There is no need for any further searching; it is clear enough there what the Mystery is that encompasses body and soul. It also explains the condition of separated souls, both regarding their expectation of the Last Judgment and their dwelling place, source, life, and differences in the meantime. I had thought it was so deeply and highly grounded that the human mind should be satisfied with it. And if you have not set forth—or cannot set forth—anything more fundamental, then my explanation rightfully remains in its place. The thousand-year Sabbath <note>The "thousand-year Sabbath" refers to the Millennium, a period of rest and divine rule mentioned in the Book of Revelation</note> and the four hundred years in *Zion* will only find fault with everything and bring it under suspicion; though many objections might be made, they would be of no service or value.

93. Furthermore, the manifestation of the thousand-year Sabbath is not of much importance or concern to the world, since we do not have sufficient grounds for it. It should rightfully rest in Divine Omnipotence <note>original: "Omnipotence," referring to God's absolute power and sovereignty</note>. We have enough in the Sabbath of the new birth <note>original: "Regeneration," the process of spiritual rebirth in the believer</note>; for the soul that obtains this Sabbath will have enough of a Sabbath in Paradise after the death of the earthly body. We may very well leave and commend the rest to Divine Omnipotence, and wait upon God to see what He will do with us when we are in Him and He is in us.

94. For I suppose there would be a better Sabbath in God than in this world. And if man were to dwell upon the earth in Paradise, then God would have to restore that which entered into the Mystery through His curse, as can be seen in the *Forty Questions*.

95. But your assumption that the righteous shall *not* be brought with their works before the judgment is contrary to the words of Christ, who says, *that all things shall be tested through the fire.*

96. I do not say they shall come *into* the judgment—for the judgment of Anger is for the wicked. Regarding this, the Scripture speaks of the righteous, or as Christ says: *He who believes in me does not come into judgment.* By this, He means the source of pain or the suffering of the judgment. Yet His words hold true: that they shall all come together before the judgment and every one hear his sentence; the ungodly depart from here, and the righteous come here, etc.

97. Also, everyone shall stand forth with his own works in the Mystery <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "Mystery" refers to the eternal, spiritual reality where all things are recorded and revealed</note>, and they themselves will be judged according to their works.

<meta>This page continues Jakob Böhme’s response concerning the state of the soul, the nature of human works, and the process of the Last Judgment. It follows his discussion of the "thousand-year Sabbath" and the purification required before the soul can truly enter divine rest.</meta>

Now you know very well that our works in this world have been wrought in both good and evil, and they shall be tested and separated in the fire of God. How then, if they remain unseparated, can they follow the Saints in the Resurrection to the Sabbath, and how can the Saints hold the Sabbath within them? But if the works are to follow them, then they must be tested and separated in the fire; then they shall no longer have any need to come before the judgment. But if they should keep a Sabbath without their works, then they are not perfect.

98. If we would speak of *Paradise* and understand it, then we must have clear eyes to see into it; for the internal Paradisiacal world and the external world hang within one another. We have only turned ourselves out of the internal into the external, and so we work in two worlds.

99. Death cannot separate our works; the fire of God must do it. For they remain in one Mystery <note>original: "Mystery"; Böhme uses this term to describe the hidden, essential spiritual reality or "Mysterium Magnum" that underlies all physical existence</note> until the judgment of God. Everyone, at the hour of the Resurrection, shall come forth in his own Mystery, and he shall see his works before him and feel them within him.

100. It is not understood that they shall answer for themselves with words, for the Kingdom of God consists of and proceeds in power. And although the ungodly shall cry out "Woe!" upon their abominations and those who seduced them, yet every man’s work shall be *Summoned in POWER*, which shall either rejoice or torment him.

101. Now, the old body of this world is the Mystery of this world, and the new body is the Mystery of the Divine Light World. The soul is the Mystery of God the Father, and the Earth with the elements also has both Mysteries, which shall be moved through the Principle of the Father <note>The "Principle of the Father" refers to the first of Böhme's three principles: the underlying fire or energy of the divine essence</note>.

102. And then the doors of the Mysteries shall be set open, and each shall give and set forth its *Figures* <note>original: "Figures"; the spiritual forms, patterns, or records of everything that has happened</note> which it has swallowed up; for the Principle of the soul must stand before the judgment with both the Mysteries.

103. Happy are they who shall have the body of Christ in the Mystery of the wrath <note>original: "the wrath [or fire of God's anger]"; Böhme views "wrath" as the primal, energetic foundation of God's being, which is transformed into love and light for the believer</note>. They shall have the soul’s fire—the Principle of the Father—surrounded with the Light World and illuminated by the Majesty. They shall feel no pain or hurt, and shall pass without feeling it through the fire. There, the outward or third Principle <note>The "third Principle" is Böhme's term for the physical, material world we inhabit</note> shall be tested; and all earthliness or falsehood shall remain in the fire. But the works shall be renovated <note>original: "renovated"; renewed and purified to their spiritual essence</note> in the fire and freed from their earthly source and soil. Then the earthly Mystery remains in the fire and is food for the fire, from which the light arises, and the righteous lose nothing.

<summary>Böhme explains that human works must be purified by God's divine fire during the Resurrection to separate good from evil. He describes how the internal and external worlds coexist and how the righteous, protected by the body of Christ, pass safely through this refining fire while their works are cleansed of earthliness.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Jakob Böhme’s explanation of how human actions (works) interact with the divine fire at the Last Judgment. 104. For the works of love produced in the new body pass with the spirit of the soul through the fire and remain in the Divine Image within the source of the light. But the works of the "third principle"—that is, of this physical world—remain in the soul’s fire-source.

105. But anything that has been worked and acted in a completely evil and malicious way in the third principle, and yet has not been renewed in this world through sincere repentance and reconciliation with one’s brother, falls into the "center of *nature*"; that is, the root of the dark world.

106. The works of the ungodly shall not be able to remain in the fire, for the fire swallows them down into itself toward the dark center—specifically, the original source of nature where the devils dwell. The soul's fire, which is the "Father’s principle," also goes there. However, this fire of the soul will have no fuel to make it burn properly; instead, it will be like a quenched, dark, and painful source-fire—merely an anguish that longs to produce fire. This is called <term>God's wrath</term> (which is a state of being, not a divine principle), a death or a dying source.

107. For the principle of the Father, in which the right and true soul consists, is a flaming fire that gives light. Within that light is the precious Image of God. That light tempers and sweetens the burning fire with the essence of *Love*, so that it is a pleasing delight and a source of *nature* and of life.

108. Therefore, I tell you that you should not think it strange or misunderstand it when I or anyone else (whether it be *Theophrastus* <note>original: "Theophraſtus"; likely referring to Paracelsus (Theophrastus von Hohenheim), whose alchemical and philosophical ideas deeply influenced Böhme</note> or whoever it may be) write that a person shall stand before the Judgment *with the body which they had here*. I perceive very well that you have not yet understood my writings in the *Book of the Threefold Life* or in the *Book of the Incarnation of Jesus Christ* (which discusses Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection, and how we must enter into His death and arise out of it). You shall find it explained and expanded upon clearly enough there; but since you do not have them at hand yet, please be patient. You will very likely get to read them, and then you will be *freed from your perplexity* and this kind of deep searching.

109. For those books lay their foundation much deeper than your current understanding of this matter. If you only read them correctly, you shall truly find what the Mystery is, what the magical *Ground* and *Abyss* <note>original: "Byſſe, and Abyſſe"; "Byſſe" (or Byssus) refers to the Unground or "Ungrund"—the bottomless, foundational source of all existence in Böhme's thought</note> are, and also what the "Being of all Beings" is. There is no need to consult with one person or another; he who understands the Great Mystery from which all beings have proceeded and still proceed does not burden himself with such long, roundabout explanations.

110. You have undertaken a very hard labor that does nothing but confuse, eat up, and consume your life. It is entirely unnecessary.

<meta>This page continues Jakob Böhme’s instructions on spiritual discernment. Böhme emphasizes that true divine knowledge is found through humility and the "new birth" in Christ, rather than through intellectual labor or the premature revelation of esoteric secrets.</meta>

# The Fourth Epistle

110. Nevertheless, he who finds and knows the great <term>Mystery</term> <note>The hidden divine reality behind all things.</note> finds all things within it; there is no need for literal demonstration. God, Christ, and eternity with all its wonders lie within it; the **Holy Spirit** is the **Key** to it. If you are in the "new birth" as you say, then there is no need for such difficult seeking or hard labor. Seek only Christ in the Manger, in the dark Stable; when you find him, then you shall indeed find where he sits at the right hand of God.

111. Searching alone does nothing. The **Philosopher's Stone** <note>A legendary substance in alchemy capable of turning base metals into gold, used by Böhme as a metaphor for spiritual transformation.</note> is a very dark, disesteemed stone of a gray color, but within it lies the highest **Tincture** <note>The spiritual essence or life-force that transforms and enlivens matter.</note>. If you would search out the **Great Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>, then consider only the Earth with its metals, and so you may well find what the **Magical** or **Cabbalistic** <note>Referring to the Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism focused on the nature of the divine and the universe.</note> ground is.

112. The deep and **mystical** numbers, which otherwise no man is able to fathom or find out, all lie in the **Mystery**. But he who finds it does not search after the numbers; he treats gold as earth. He acts like one who has a costly treasure lying in an obscure place. The manger and swaddling clothes of Christ are more acceptable to him than the whole world with its figures [or external pomp and glory]. He hides the **numbers** themselves, for the outward kingdom must accomplish its wonders.

<margin>* Magi.</margin>
113. Why should the earthly mystery be unveiled before **the time**? Inquire of the * Magi <note>original: "Magists"; refers to those who study the "Magia" or the hidden workings of God in nature.</note> who have understood the heavenly and earthly **Magic** <note>original: "Magia"</note>. Why have they kept the **Tincture** secret and not revealed it? There is no other cause at all but that the world is **not worthy** of it; likewise, it is **not worthy** of the numbers of the Mystery.

<margin>Note.</margin>
114. Therefore God has hidden them from us, so that the earthly mystery might accomplish and fulfill all its wonders through us, and that all the vials of God's anger might be poured forth upon us. How can a man undertake to reveal such secret things without the consent of the Mystery? Indeed, he tampers with the outside of the Mystery, but if he is to come inside, he must have the will of the Mystery.

115. The outward impulse to manifest and reveal the Mystery proceeds from the **Stars**; for they would gladly be freed from vanity, and they drive the **Magical Children** <note>Those spiritually awakened to the hidden workings of God's creation.</note> strongly toward manifestation. Therefore, we must prove and examine the impulse—whether it proceeds from God's light, from God's spirit, or from the dominion or government of the stars.

116. For God's spirit speaks plainly of his Mystery; he only declares the **Turba** <note>original: "Turba"; in Böhme's thought, this refers to the "disturbance" or the awakening of God's wrath and judgment in nature.</note> and leaves the **numbers** alone. He has once signed and sealed the Mystery with the power of the first Principle in the **Seven forms of Nature** <note>Böhme’s description of the seven properties or stages through which the divine essence manifests into the material world.</note> for the wonders of God; and again, he has signed it in the love in the humanity of Christ, with the **Seven golden Candlesticks** and lights; and with that he continues until

<meta>This page concludes Jakob Böhme’s Fourth Epistle. He explains why divine secrets, specifically the "numbers" or timing of spiritual ages, are often kept hidden or spoken of in parables to maintain the "magical order" of God's mystery.</meta>

# The Fourth Epistle

...until the judgment; each number manifests itself in its own Age; no creature has the power to manifest it, for he who possesses it dares not. Otherwise, he transgresses the <term>Magical order</term> <note>The divine structure and timing through which God reveals hidden truths to the world.</note> and becomes a loathing to the <term>Mystery</term> <note>The "Mysterium Magnum" or the hidden spiritual reality of God.</note>.

<margin>Note.</margin>
117. And therefore the prophets, and also Christ himself, have spoken entirely in parables, after a magical manner; and even to this day, no one who is capable of the Mystery dares to speak otherwise, unless there is a specific purpose of God for the Number to be plainly revealed. For example, Daniel clearly denoted the time of Christ with its own Number because he was commanded to do so. I tell you this sincerely and in all faithfulness, and also in true Christian love toward you—not out of contempt, but from my own knowledge and gifts, seeing that you desired it of me. I have given you a short hint of what you are to do in this matter, and I entreat you to look upon it in a brotherly way.

118. But yet, whatever I am able to serve you with, using my few gifts, if you desire it further, it shall be done with good will—provided I perceive you are in good earnest, and that it shall serve the honor of God and the welfare of mankind. And so, I commend you to the love of *Jesus Christ*.

->**in the Year of our Lord <note>original: "ANNO DOM:"</note> 1620.**<-

# ANOTHER LETTER TO PAUL KEYM:

## Concerning the Way to True Knowledge, and Regeneration in CHRIST:

### Likewise concerning the thousand-year Sabbath; and how the *Mysteries in the Revelation* are to be understood.

->***Our Salvation in Christ Jesus.***<-

<margin>1.</margin> WORTHY and much-respected Sir, and beloved brother in Christ; I have received your last letter, and in it, I have once more understood and clearly observed your zealous, passionate mind in your intended labor and difficult study. I have also noted your anxious, earnest desire for the light of true knowledge, and thirdly, your great thirst for the fountain and wellspring of Christ. It is in this fountain that the mind is refreshed, quickened <note>original: "quickned"; meaning to be brought to life or revitalized</note>, comforted, satisfied, and appeased. Considering that I am a servant to my brothers, and no less than a debtor to them in the love of Christ, I shall, in that same love, show and impart to you what I know and what has been given to me, as your request requires it.

<summary>Böhme begins a new letter to Paul Keym, acknowledging Keym's intense desire for spiritual knowledge and Böhme's own duty to share his insights into Christ as the source of true refreshment.</summary>

### The Fifth Epistle.

2. Christ said, "I am the vine, you are the branches; he who abides in me, and I in him, shall bring forth much fruit; for without me you can do nothing." Also, "He who abides in me and [has] my words [abiding] in him, he brings forth much fruit." Herein lies the whole foundation, and *it is the only root or spring to the Fountain where the Divine understanding flows.* There is no other ground for true and real knowledge in the wisdom of God; no other seeking, studying, or searching is of any use.

3. For every spirit searches only its own depth—[or reaches no further than its own natural capacity or instinct]—and understands that in which it ignites <note>original: "enkindle"; to set on fire or awaken spiritually</note> itself. And though it searches in its own ignition, yet it finds no more than a type or representation of things, like a shadow or dream; it is not able to behold the Being itself. For if it would see the Being, then it must be in the Being, and the Being in it, so that it may be capable of the Being and see truly in the Being itself.

4. Now then, seeing that we are dead in *Adam* <note>In Böhme's theology, being "dead in Adam" refers to the fall of humanity into a state of spiritual blindness and separation from God's life.</note> to the Divine essence and have become blind and estranged, we have no power in us *of ourselves; we know nothing of God in our Reason*, but only the history—that there is a God. We neither feel his power nor see his light unless we return and become like children, who know nothing but are guided and ruled. And as a child looks upon its mother and longs for her, and she also cherishes and brings it up, so must the external reason be blinded, beaten down, and quite quashed.

5. And the desire must resign and cast itself into the grace and Love of God, and not regard the opposition and contradiction of the outward reason, which says, "It is not so; God is far off; you must search, meditate, and represent him only to yourself through your own understanding; you must seek after his will, and how he has revealed himself."

<margin>How he has revealed himself in his Word.</margin>

*So he will be known, and no otherwise.* Thus the external, historical, astral reason <note>original: "Aſtrall reaſon"; Böhme uses this term to describe human intellect that is governed by the physical stars/universe rather than by the Holy Spirit.</note> judges; and it also rules the whole world, except for a very small number of God's children.

6. Christ said, *“You must abide in me”*; for without me you can do nothing. You can neither know nor search out anything truly and fundamentally concerning God. For *“he who comes to me, I will in no way cast out.”* In me, you shall bring forth much fruit. Now, every branch grows on its own tree and has the sap, power, influence, virtue, and property of the tree; and it bears fruit according to the quality, kind, and property of the tree.

7. Thus likewise, he who desires to be taught by God and to have Divine knowledge must stand in the tree into which God has engrafted <note>original: "engrafted"; a gardening term for joining a shoot onto a different trunk, used here to describe being spiritually joined to Christ.</note> us through the Regeneration <note>original: "Regeneration"; the spiritual rebirth or "being born again."</note>; he must have the sap and virtue of—

8. We must drink the new milk of Christ’s Incarnation <note>The theological concept of God becoming human in the person of Jesus.</note> so that we may be made partakers of his flesh and spirit. His virtue and sap <note>original: "sap"; here meaning the spiritual life-force or essence flowing from Christ as the vine.</note> must be our virtue and sap; we must become God's children through *Divine Eating and Drinking*.

9. *Nicodemus* said: *“How can it be that a man should be born again in his old age?”* Yes, good *Nicodemus*, and good external earthly Reason: how could it be that *Adam*, who was a perfect image of God, perished in his perfection and became earthly? Did it not happen through imagination? Because he directed his desire, longing, and lust into the outward Astral <note>original: "Astrall"; referring to the celestial influences of the stars and planets upon the earthly realm.</note>, elemental, and earthly kingdom—and set his mind upon the dominion of this world—whereupon he, in his desire, lust, and imagination, was immediately impregnated and became earthly. Thereby he fell into the sleep of the external *Magia* <note>original: "Magia"; Böhme uses this to mean the creative power of the will and imagination to shape reality.</note>; and thus it is also with the *New birth*.

10. Through imagination and an earnest, serious desire, we are again impregnated by the Deity and receive the new body within the old. The new does not mix itself with the old—just as gold in a coarse and rough stone is quite another thing, and has another *tincture* <note>original: "Tincture"; a spiritual quality or essence capable of transforming or "dyeing" matter into a higher state.</note> and *spirit* than the rough matter in the stone. So also is the new man within the old; the rough stone knows nothing of the gold, and likewise, the earthly *Adam* knows nothing of the divine heavenly *Adam*. Therefore, there is strife in man, and man is contrary to himself.

11. The earthly *Adam* wants to see, feel, and taste, but he receives only a ray, a pattern, and a twinkling reflection from the internal man. In this state, he may sometimes taste something of the divine man, but not essentially. Just as the light of the sun disperses or swallows up the mournful darkness so that it appears as if there were no darkness at all—and yet the darkness is really hidden within the light, appearing again when the sunlight withdraws.

12. In this way, the new man often swallows up the old through divine power, so that the old man supposes he has grasped the Deity. Yet he is not capable of that essence; rather, the Spirit of God from the new man passes through the old. But when that Spirit enters again into its mystery, the old man does not know what happened to him. He seeks ways to come to God and searches for the purpose and will of God, and yet finds nothing but invention, fiction, and opinion. He is very zealous in his opinions, but does not know what he is doing; he finds—

# The Fifth Epistle.

[...the old nature touch]es not the root; for it is not capable or worthy of it; and this shows that it must die and perish.

13. But the New Man, who arises through an earnest, serious will and purpose, and through Imagination <note>original: "Imagination"; in Böhme’s theology, this is not mere fantasy, but the creative power of the human will to focus upon and be shaped by a divine object.</note> [or the effective operation of true Faith], remains steadfast in the rest of Christ. He remains even in the Tree which God the Father—by his movement when he moved himself the second time according to his heart—grafted into the human soul. This New Man springs forth in the life of God, and grows and flourishes in the power, virtue, and sap of the Divine Essence <note>original: "Essentiality"</note> in God's Love. This New Man receives divine knowledge and skill, not according to the measure of the external will (what the external man wishes to know and search out), but according to the measure of the internal Heaven. The internal Heaven kindles and enlightens the external, so that the understanding or intellectual faculty of the soul comprehends and understands the external world.

14. For God, who is a spirit and also a Being, has manifested himself through the external world in a likeness <note>original: "similitude"</note>, so that the spirit might see itself essentially in that Being; and not only that, but so that the creature might also contemplate and behold the being of God in that form <note>original: "Figure"</note> and know it.

15. For no creature is able to see the Being of God outside of itself. The spirit sees God in the Essence and luster of his Majesty, and sees the same within itself and in its own fellow-creatures who are like itself. For God is himself the spirit of all Beings (meaning heavenly Beings), so that when we see the Divine Creature, we see an image or likeness that proceeded from God's Being; and when we see the will and working of that creature, then we see the will and working of God.

16. Thus also is the New Man born of God; what it wills and does is God’s will and work. Its knowledge is God’s knowledge, for we know nothing of God without God’s spirit.

17. The external cannot see the internal, unless the internal draws the external into itself by a glimpse [or influence of light in its own idea or contemplation]. Then the external apprehends the mirror or resemblance of the internal as an instruction and direction. This shows that the external world takes its rise and origin from the internal, and that *Our works shall follow us in the Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium"; a reference to Revelation 14:13 and the hidden eternal reality.</note>. By the separation of God’s judgment, through the fire of the Principle, these works shall be set into the eternal world.

18. For this purpose God created Angels and Men: specifically for his wonderful deeds, so that the wisdom of the *Divine Power* might appear, and that God might behold himself in the resemblances and ideas of his creatures, and have joy in himself with the beings created out of his own wisdom.

# The Fifth Epistle.

19. Loving Brother, do not take it badly that I speak bluntly to you. You complain that you are not always able to reach, understand, and keep the Divine Mysteries; moreover, you say that many times you get a glimpse of them, and that my writings are *hard* and difficult for you to understand. I will therefore show you—according to the power and ability I have received from God—how the state of your hidden Mystery stands, which at present you are unable to understand.

20. Your intention and will is to keep [the light of the Mystery] in a continued, steadfast understanding. This is the will of the external world within you; it would gladly be capable of the Deity and be freed from vanity. But the spirit of the external world must remain in continual labor <note>original: "travell"; in this context, it refers to "travail" or the painful, earnest effort of spiritual labor.</note> and earnest *seeking*. For by its seeking, it finds the wonders of its own *Magia* <term>Magia</term> <note>For Böhme, "Magia" is not "magic" in a modern sense, but the formative, attractive power of the will and desire that brings spiritual realities into being.</note>, namely, the type and resemblance of the internal world.

21. For God does not always move himself, but the *longing* and earnest labor of the creature *moves the Mystery*, so that the image or idea of the Divine Wisdom may be sought and found. Therefore, Christ commands us to *seek and knock*, and also promises to give us the pearl or jewel in the seeking.

22. The external world is likewise from God and of God, and man was created into the external world for this purpose: that he might bring the external figures into the internal ones—that he might bring the end back into the beginning.

23. The more a person longs for God, and the more they pant and run after him, the more they come out of the end and into the beginning—not only for God’s wonder, but for their own edification. For the twig of the tree continually thirsts after the sap and virtue of the tree; it labors in desire for the tree and draws its sap and influence into itself, and so thereby grows up to be a great branch. In this way, the anxious hunger and earnest longing in the *human mystery draws the Kingdom of God into itself*. Of this, Christ said: *The Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force to themselves* <note>A reference to Matthew 11:12, interpreted here as the soul's intense, active desire "seizing" spiritual life.</note>.

24. A being or essence that is not attractive <note>In Böhme’s physics of the soul, "attractive" means the power to draw nourishment or essence toward oneself.</note> cannot grow or gain a body for itself, but instead starves and pines away. Just as we see the fire of a candle draws or attracts the fat into itself and devours it, yet it provides a shining light from that devouring; so it is with man. He is shut up and enclosed (along with his first Divine Essence) in the darkness of death, but God has again opened this to the soul in Christ.

25. Now the poor, captive soul is this very hungry *magical fire*, which again attracts the divine, revealed essence to itself out of the incarnation of Christ; and so it feeds on God’s being...

This body of light is both similar to and capable of receiving the Deity. In this way, the poor soul becomes clothed with a body of light, much like the fire in a candle, and it finds rest within this body. But in the darkness of this world—inside its earthly carcass and clothing of clay, where God's curse and all evil inclinations and false desires reside—the soul experiences anguish and trouble.

26. But since the soul has, along with Adam, taken this earthly image upon itself, it must now bear it. Just as the fire of a candle must draw its burning light from a dark lump of fat <note>original: "fat"; likely referring to the tallow or wax of a candle</note>, the soul must do the same. If it had stayed within God’s being with Adam and had not put on the earthly image, it would not have needed to bear it; but now, it is bound to do so.

27. For Saint Paul says: *To whom you give yourselves as servants in obedience, his servants you are; whether it be to sin, leading to death, or to the obedience of God, leading to righteousness.* <note>Romans 6:16</note> Since the soul has put on the earthly image—which produces nothing but fruit for death—and has surrendered and devoted itself as a servant to sin, it has now become the sinful servant of death.

28. Why has it fallen in love with a strange master that dominates it? Had it only remained a child and not lusted after the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, it would not have needed to be subject to both governments <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "two governments" refer to the dual forces of God’s love and God’s wrath (or light and darkness).</note>. But because it wanted to be like God in both love and anger—according to both the principles of eternity—it must now bear that image and undergo the force and sway of both. Thus, it must endure the burning fire [the curse and anger of God ignited in the divided properties of nature] until the day of separation.

30. 31. And therefore it must work, labor, and endeavor to obtain the light again; this is why the life of man stands in such anguish, in painful seeking, in continual abstinence, and repentance. It earnestly desires Divine Rest, and yet is held back by the wrath of Nature <note>In Böhme’s theology, "Nature" often refers to the restless, driving forces of existence that lack the peace of God's light.</note>.

32. The more the life desires to fly from the wrath [or fierceness of Nature], the **more** strong and vehement the strife grows in that life. In addition to this, the Devil—through his poisonous incantations, magical imaginations, representations, and insinuations—stirs up and brings into his **nest** [which is the center of the soul] the magical image of the poisonous serpent. He continually presents this before the soul so that the soul might still fix its imagination upon it and become inflamed with its poison, which happens daily; and thus the fire of the soul becomes an evil, poisonous, burning brimstone fire.

33. Yet if the soul departs from the serpent-like image of the Devil and rejects the evil earthly Tree [whereon the serpent has cunningly coiled himself]—which Tree is Pride, Covetousness, Envy, Anger, and Falsehood—and if it no longer longs after these things but makes itself, as it were, dead to this figure, as if it knew nothing of it; and if it casts away the very lust <note>original: "concupiscence"</note> and imagination itself, and desires only the love of God, submitting itself wholly to God’s will and working, so that He may be its only willing, working, and doing; then the Divine light begins to shine in it. It obtains an eye of true sight, so that it is able to behold its own natural form and features, by which it steps into plain, straightforward, and meek humility.

34. It wills nothing and desires nothing, but resigns and casts itself into the bosom of its Mother <note>Here, "Mother" likely refers to the Divine Sophia or the Spirit of God, representing the nurturing source of spiritual life.</note>; like a child that desires nothing but its mother, inclining itself to her and longing only after her. It does not highly value any art, subtle Reason, or much knowledge; and though it may know much, yet it is not puffed up or elevated in its own conceit by its knowledge, but leaves and resigns all knowing, willing, and working wholly to its Mother’s spirit, so that it might be both the will and the work within it.

35. This lily-twig is the true Image of God, for it is the new-born or regenerated spirit of the soul, the spirit of God's will; the Triumphing Chariot of the Holy Spirit, in which he rides into the sacred Ternary, into the Angelic World.

39. And with this twig, or Image [of God renewed in us] as mentioned before, we are in Christ outside of this world, in the Angelic World. The "old Adam" <note>The unregenerate, earthly nature of man inherited from the Fall.</note> has no understanding or perception of this; he does not know it, just as the rough stone does not know the gold which yet grows within it.

->The Gate of the True Knowledge of the Threefold Life.<-

40. Man is the true similitude or image of God, as the precious man Moses testifies. He is not only an earthly image (for the sake of which God would not have become man and put forth, united, and espoused his heart and spirit [in deepest love] to it after the Fall), but he is originally from the Being of all beings. He is made out of all the three worlds: namely, out of the innermost nature-world (which is also the most outward) called the dark world, where the principle of the fiery nature takes its rise, as is declared at length in my book *The Threefold Life*.
