### The Fifth Epistle

41. And secondly, he is outside the light or angelic world, outside the true being of God; and then thirdly, he is outside this external world of the sun, stars, and elements. He is an entire image of God, existing outside the being of all beings.

42. His original image stood in Paradise, in the angelic world; but he lusted after the external world (that is, after the astral and elemental world) which has swallowed up and covered the precious image of the internal heaven, and now rules in that likeness as if it were its own property.

43. Therefore it is said, *“You must be born again, or else you cannot see the Kingdom of God.”* <note>John 3:3</note> And this is why the Word or Heart of God entered into the human essence: so that we, with our souls, might be able—through the power of the Word or Heart of God—to beget and bring forth again from our soul a new branch <note>original: "twig"</note> or image, just like the first one.

44. Therefore, the old carcass <note>The physical body corrupted by sin.</note> must rot, decay, and perish; for it is unfit for the Kingdom of God. It carries nothing but its own mystery into its first beginning—that is, its wonders and works. Understand this as being in the essence of the first principle, which is immortal and incorruptible, being the magical fire of the soul.

45. And not this alone, but he must bring and unite the end with the beginning; for the external world is generated out of the internal and created into a physical <note>original: "comprehensible"</note> being. The wonders of this world belong to the beginning and were known from eternity in the wisdom of God—that is, in the *Divine Magia* <term>Divine Magic; original: "Divine Magia." The spiritual power by which God manifests the hidden, inner ideas into visible, external forms.</term>. This was not in a physical existence or essentiality, but in the mirror of the Virgin-like wisdom of God, from which the *eternal nature* always arises [or takes its origin] from eternity.

46. And to this end, the poor soul stands in the prison of the astral and elemental kingdom, so that it might be a laborer and reunite the wonders of the external nature with the light-world, and bring them back into the beginning. And though the soul must now be bruised and pressed, and endure much, yet it is the *servant* in God’s vineyard who prepares the precious wine that is drunk in the Kingdom of God. The soul is the only cause of understanding; its desire works within the mystery and manifests and brings forth to light the hidden wonders of God, just as we see plainly how man searches out and *reveals <margin>Or, brings forth.</margin> the wonders of nature.

47. Therefore, we must not be amazed or strangely troubled when the noble image is often hidden, so that we cannot receive any refreshment or comfort. We must know that the poor soul is then put into the vineyard, so that it should work and bring the fruit to be set upon God’s table.

...and eternally enjoy. This contributes to our own edification, for our labor remains in our own Mystery <note>original: "Mystery" (Mysterium) — in Boehme's work, this refers to the hidden spiritual essence or the underlying reality of divine manifestation.</note> toward God's deeds of wonder, and toward our own eternal crown and glory before God, as I have set forth at length in my other writings.

62. Regarding the Sabbath in this world—about which you have written and still hold the same opinion—the knowledge and understanding of it has *not* been given to me. Furthermore, I do not know how there can be any perfect being in the "torment-house" of the stars and elements. I cannot find such an understanding within the Mystery, since the first man [Adam] was not able to stand even when the heavenly Ruler reigned within him, but was overcome by the kingdom of the stars and elements. Might it not, therefore, still be dangerous?

63. When we consider the possibility and impossibility of this within the Mystery, it then appears as if there will be no Sabbath in this sad and sorrowful mirror of the Divine Being. For the Devil is a prince of this world; and even if he were bound for a thousand years in the dark world, the fierce, wrathful stars—as well as heat and cold—still hold rule and dominance in this world. This world is nothing else but *a valley of misery*.

64. Now, if the dominion of the stars did not reach us or have any influence on us, then we would not be in this world but in Paradise, where no wicked person could oppose us or see us—for in Paradise, we are "swallowed up" or enclosed within God.

65. Just as we cannot see the angels with our earthly eyes, so too a wicked person of this world cannot see a new <gloss>regenerate</gloss> person in Christ. When we attain the "new man" in Christ, then (as far as that new person is concerned) we are already in the Sabbath and only wait for the redemption from this wicked, earthly life.

66. For we are with Christ in God; we are planted together with him in his death. We are buried in him and arise with the "new man" out of the grave with him, living eternally in our own being or essence—that is, in his spiritual body. We are with and in Christ, in God, and God is in us. Where, then, should we keep the Sabbath? Not in this world, but in the angelic world—the world of light.

67. And if the wicked were to be tormented for a thousand years in this world, then the location <gloss>of this world</gloss> would have to be transformed or withdrawn into the dark world. For in this solar world <note>The physical world illuminated by the sun, which Boehme contrasts with the "dark world" of spiritual fire and the "light world" of divine love.</note>, there is not yet any *hellish torment*. But if the sun were taken away, then it would indeed be so; then the wicked would be separated far from the judgment, and there would be a "gulf of a Principle" <note>Boehme uses the term "Principle" to describe the three fundamental states of existence: the dark fire-source, the divine light, and the physical/solar world.</note> interposed and fixed between them.

<summary>Boehme addresses the concept of a literal thousand-year Sabbath on Earth, arguing that true spiritual rest (the Sabbath) is found within the "new man" in Christ rather than in the physical world, which remains a "valley of misery" governed by the stars.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Boehme's response regarding the "Sabbath." He transitions from arguing why a perfect earthly state is impossible to explaining the nature of divine wrath, the cause of the Fall, and the state of the soul after death.</meta>

68. Moreover, God is not a God of evil who desires revenge or torment. He does not, out of His own vengeance, torment and plague the wicked for a thousand years before the Judgment; rather, the wicked person torments himself within the birth of his own life. One form of life is an enemy to the other, and that will indeed be his hellish torment—God is not to blame for it.

69. He never desired the fall of man; instead, the wrathful Nature gained the upper hand, and the spirit of man's will (which is free, just as God Himself is) freely and willingly surrendered itself to the struggle, thinking it would dominate and rule.

70. It was out of pride that the Devil fell, and man also. If they had remained in humility, God would have continued to dwell within them; but they both departed from God. Yet God loved man's Image so exceedingly that He Himself, out of love, *re-entered* into the Image of man. Why, then, should He desire man's torment?

71. In God, there is no evil desire; however, *His wrath*—which is the dark world—is a desire for evil and destruction. This is what brought the Devil and also man to their fall. The *dark world* caused the Devil to fall, and the *external, wrathful Nature* caused man to fall. Yet both of these are tied and bound to one another, which we would clearly see and feel if the sun were taken out of this world.

72. Therefore, I say again: the righteous keep their Sabbath in Abraham’s bosom <note>original: "Abrahams bosome" — a biblical expression (Luke 16:22) referring to a place of comfort and rest for the righteous dead while they await the final resurrection.</note> and in Christ's rest. For Christ has destroyed the wrathful death that held us captive for our sake; He has opened the way to life, so that we, as a "new man," are able to spring forth, blossom, and rest in Him.

73. But the "old man" <note>original: "old man" — in Pauline theology and Boehme's thought, this refers to the unregenerate, earthly nature of man that is subject to physical corruption and the influence of the stars.</note> made of the stars and elements must remain in his own region—in his house of torment and misery—until he is committed to the earth. Then everything returns to its own Mystery again, and the soul remains in its own principle until the Judgment of God. At that time, God shall again move and ignite the Mystery, and then every thing will separate into its own property. Each world shall take in its own harvest, whether it be good or bad; it shall divide itself as light and darkness.

74. And therefore, I entreat you entirely as a brother and a Christian, that you would be pleased to take care that you understand the Sabbath as being found in the rest of Christ. Do not be so moved by the igniting of the spirit [or the fervent prompting of your mind], but instead search whether you are able to ground your view in the light of Nature. If you are able to ground it and reach it in the light of the Eternal Nature, then indeed you may proceed; but show it to us plainly.

Yet such a person does not have the Divine Magical School, which consists purely in a simple, *childlike mind*.

83. The external guide works and contemplates <note>original: "speculates" — in the sense of looking into or theorizing</note> only in the mirror <note>original: "Glasse" — likely a reference to the "speculum" or mirror of nature and imagination</note>, but the internal guide contemplates the very essence. However, the internal guide is not able to do this unless God’s Spirit leads it; therefore, God makes the choice.

84. Whomever the heavenly school takes, he is made a *master of divine wisdom* <note>original: "Magist" — a practitioner of "Magia," or spiritual power</note> without his own strenuous efforts; although he must work hard, he is ultimately taken by God and *driven by the Holy Spirit*.

85. Therefore, a person must test which guide has taken hold of him. If he finds that <insert>he has the Divine light shining in his vision</insert>, and that his guide <insert>brings him into the heavenly school upon</insert> the way of truth toward *love* and *righteousness*, and <insert>that he is thereby assured and confirmed in his mind with divine certainty</insert>, then he may proceed in his work.

86. But if his motivation is based on guesswork and doubt, yet driven by a fiery passion, then the guide is from this world. This guide should be tested by its will and purpose: whether it seeks *God’s honor* or *its own honor* and *applause*; whether it willingly submits itself to the *Cross* <note>The "Cross" symbolizes self-denial and the patient endurance of suffering in imitation of Christ</note>, <insert>and only desires to labor in Christ’s vineyard and to seek the good of its neighbor—whether it seeks God or mere bread <note>original: "Bread" — meaning material gain or physical sustenance</note></insert>. Accordingly, his understanding must judge and either give permission or reject and tame that impulse as needed.

87. As a brother, I would not hide this from you in a Christian encouragement. I ask that you accept it in no other way than as it is intended—well-meant toward you, as my duty requires. Because of your request, I am your debtor in Christ to your soul's anxious seeking, just as one member of the body is bound to help another.

88. Regarding your very Christian offer, I acknowledge and accept it as an act of love, just as one member of the body comes to help the—

# THE SIXTH EPISTLE:
### BEING
### A very deep and Philosophical Letter,
### WRITTEN
## To Doctor GOTTFRIED FREUDENHAMMER; and to Master JOHN HEUSER.
### Concerning the Knowledge of God, and of all things.
### ALSO
## A Short Declaration of the False and True LIGHT.

*The salvation of our Lord Jesus Christ, by his entrance and manifestation in humanity, work with his Love in us all.*

1. Much respected sirs, and dearly beloved brethren in Christ: when God opens to us by his grace the *right understanding*, so that we are able to *know* and properly understand the image of God—*that is, Man*—regarding what he is in body, soul, and spirit, then we acknowledge that he is the visible and also the invisible spiritual world; namely, *an extract of all the three principles of the Divine Being.* <note>original: "Principles" — In Boehme’s philosophy, the "Three Principles" represent the three realms of existence: the dark "fire-world" of divine wrath, the light world of God’s love/heaven, and the outer physical world.</note>

2. In him <note>man</note>, the hidden God, through expression and impression... <note>The text continues on the next page; the original catchword "fion" suggests the following word is "fashioning" or "formation."</note>

<summary>In this introductory segment of his sixth letter, Jacob Boehme explains that when God grants true spiritual insight, one recognizes that humanity is a microcosm containing all three levels of divine reality: the physical, the spiritual, and the divine.</summary>

2. ...fashioning <note>original: "fion"—a continuation of the word "fashioning" from the previous page's catchword</note> of his various *distinct Power*, and eternal Wisdom has set forth himself in a visible image, through which he does conceive [idea], form, and shape, in the same Being, the wonders of the expressed Word; in that the Word of his powers makes itself substantial <note>original: "essential"—in Boehme’s usage, this means taking on a tangible or "essence-filled" form</note>.

3. And so in or by man he has represented and set forth an image of his speaking and out-spoken substantial word, in which the *Divine Knowledge* <note>original: "Science" (Latin *scientia*)—referring to divine wisdom or the internal logic of God's creation</note> with the various divisions of the *Eternal speaking* is contained.

4. And hence man has the understanding and knowledge of all things, so that he is able to understand the union [conjunction] of Nature, and also its separation [disjunction]. For no spirit has any higher rule, or deeper reach, than in its own Mother from whom it takes its origin; and in that ground it stands or remains in its *center*.

5. This we see in the creatures of the stars and elements, that their understanding and knowledge is no higher than that of their Mother in whom they live. Each leads its life after the nature and condition of its Mother, wherein it is bounded in the distinct division of the expressed Word. And no creature in the four elements whose origin is not out of the *Eternal Knowledge* is able to attain the knowledge of the hidden spiritual world of power, save only <insert>and alone Man, who with his soul and understanding spirit is contained in the eternal breathing [or generation] <note>original: "Spiration"</note> of the Divine power,</insert> and various distinct division of the eternal Word of God.

6. Therefore, the human knowledge receives in the center of its understanding both good and evil, and does conceive [idea] and shape itself both in good and evil, and makes itself *substantial* therein; and so with and by that knowledge, it leads itself into will, desire, and essence.

7. So that the Abyssal <note>original: "Abyssal"—referring to the *Ungrund*, the bottomless or groundless void of God's primal nature before manifestation</note> will, out of the eternal word of various distinct division, brings itself in the *Created Word* (that is, in the *Created Knowledge* of the soul) into a being <note>original: "Ens"—Latin for "entity" or "essence"</note> and existence. It does this in the same manner and form as the breathing [Spiration] of God has brought itself through the various division of the Eternal will, in the visible world, into diverse properties; namely, into good and evil, into love and enmity. This was done so that in such a contrast, existence might be distinct, separate, formal, sensible, and perceivable; so that each thing might, in such a contrast, find and perceive itself.

8. For in God, all beings are but one being; namely, an <insert>eternal One, or unity, the Eternal only Good;</insert> which Eternal One, without variety, would not be manifest to itself.

9. Therefore the same has breathed forth itself out of itself, so that a plurality and distinct variety might arise, which variety or separation has led itself into a peculiar *WILL* and properties.

10. 11. Everything has its own separation within itself; the center of everything is [a] spirit from the origin of the Word. 12. The form and features of bodies arise from the experience of the will, where the center of everything (being a particle or spark from the expressed Word) again expresses or speaks itself forth. 13. Now, if there were no free will in such speaking, then the speaking would have a law and would be confined and compelled; no desire or free *imagination* could arise, and then the speaking would be finite and just beginning <note>original: "inchoative"—referring to something that has just started or is incomplete</note>, which is not the case.

14. It is again an expression of itself, from which nature and the life of creatures take their origin; hence, a self-will has arisen in everything.

15. Thus, everything brings itself from its own experience into form, feature, and shape, as well as into life and operation, as it stands in its center in the *universal experience*—namely, in the *Great Mystery*, the mother of all beings.

16. We see this in the earth, which in the beginning of its materials rose out of the separation of the Divine breathing in a spiritual manner. There, the separation of the Word formed itself by its own proper will into an entity <note>original: "Ens"—a Latin term for an existing thing or being</note> and a being; so, by this formation or impression, it brought itself into the perception <note>original: "Perceivancy"—the state of being perceived or having sensory awareness</note> of the essence.

17. In this perception or sensibility, the *magnetic desire* <note>original: "Magneticall Desire"—in Boehme's thought, a force that draws spirit into matter</note> has arisen, so that the properties of the distinct, distinguishing, or separating will have brought themselves through that desire into bodies, according to and from the nature of the *three principles* of the Divine manifestation.

18. From this origin, the earth has so many and diverse bodies.

Through this center, the Eternal Word breathes itself forth into knowledge—namely, into an infinity of plurality—and brings the plurality of knowledge into imagination, and imagination into desire, and desire into nature and strife, until it reaches the Fire.

22. In that state, the strife in the painful agony dies within the consumption of the fire, losing its own natural right and property. Yet, this is not to be understood as a literal death; rather, in this way, the Power brings itself into sensibility. By killing the self-desire of its properties through the dying or mortification of self-centeredness, it brings itself through the fire and into the light.

23. There, in the light, another Principle—the Great Mystery <note>original: "Grand Mystery" (*Mysterium Magnum*)</note> of the true divine manifestation—is understood. In the fire, the First Principle—the Eternal Nature—is understood. These two are one, just like fire and light.

24. The fire gives the soul, and the power of the light gives the spirit. Within this power of the light of the divine breathing through wisdom—and through the manifestation of the fire (meaning the spirit’s fire)—the Mother of the eternal spirits (namely, of angels and the souls of men) is understood. This also includes the spiritual, angelic world—that is, the hidden internal world of power, which is the Mother of the heavens, stars, and elements; that is, of the Eternal World.

# The Sixth Epistle.

...out of the impression and enclosure of the foreshadowing <note>original: "Adumbration"—a faint sketch or shadowy representation of something</note>; that is, out of the darkness. 27. From this, the third Principle—the visible world with its being and life—has arisen. The whole creation of the visible world, whose life and being has come out of the *Three* <note>Referring to the three Principles of divine manifestation</note> into a state of existence and life, came specifically out of eternal nature and out of the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>. This means it emerged out of the darkness, fire, and light—namely, out of Love and Anger.

28. The Fire is called Anger, as it is a state of pain and enmity. The Light signifies or is called Love, being a sweet yielding and giving of itself. The darkness is a separation of knowledge and skill, so that it may be understood what Light and Life are, and also what is evil and painful.

29. There is a twofold Fire and a twofold Light to be understood. According to the dark impression, there is a *cold fire* and a false light arising through the imagination of the harsh impression. This light has its origin only in the imagination and has no true ground.

30. The second fire is a *hot fire*, and it has a fundamental, true light arising from the origin of the Divine Will. This will also brings itself forth in nature through the fire and into the light.

31. In this twofold fire and twofold light, two principles and a twofold will are understood.

32. For the false light of the imagination arises out of the self-will of nature—namely, from the impression of the properties where they test <note>original: "prove"</note> one another. From this, self-lust and an "imagination" arise, wherein nature models and fancies for itself its own desire in the Abyss. It desires to bring itself into its own power, without the will of God, into a dominion and government of its own self-will and rule.

33. This self-will refuses to be obedient and submissive to the unsearchable and Abyssal will of God (which has its origin in itself, without nature or creature, in the Eternal One). It will not resign or wholly give itself up to Him to be *one* will with Him; instead, it makes itself its own separator and maker.

# The Sixth Epistle.

...makes him an earthly mind, in which the constellations have their influence and operations; and he has the whole visible world for his enemy.

51. He stands like a rose in a bush of thorns, which is continually rent, scratched, and torn by the thorns. Yet he could not be called a rose if Divine Grace had not come to assist and restore him, inspiring him once again and giving itself into his internal ground <term>the deepest, most essential part of the soul</term>, where the love of God for the new rebirth <note>original: "Regeneration"</note> is offered to him.

52. Therefore, I say it is exceedingly necessary for a person to learn to know what they are before they run and seek. Otherwise, their seeking will only prove to be a torment, by which they torment and perplex themselves in a false Separator <term>the power that divides and forms individual will and nature</term>, and yet they cannot obtain rest and true satisfaction.

53. For all these earthly wills [and ways] through which he thinks he can bring himself to rest and quietness are only an adverse will, striving against God—namely <note>original Latin: "Viz." for "videlicet"</note>, the Eternal One.

54. For it does not depend on any man’s own willing, going, or running, as Saint Paul says, but on God’s mercy—that is, on the grace that is breathed <note>original: "inspired"</note> into him.

55. For without grace, a person is dead and blind in relation to God; they are unable to attain any true life unless grace is stirred up, awakened, and revealed within them.

56. Furthermore, there can be no awakening within these earthly wills, for they cannot reach or obtain grace, much less awaken it. Therefore, the whole person—in soul and mind—must only immerse themselves in Grace and be willing to become nothing in their own eyes. They must desire nothing but Grace, so that Grace might be living and working in them, while their own will is silenced <note>original: "Stupifyed"</note>, overcome, and put to death <note>original: "mortifyed"</note>.

57. Just as the sun breaks forth in the night [or darkness] and changes the night into day, the same is true for humanity. Regarding this, Christ says: *Unless you turn and become like children, you shall not see the kingdom of God*—namely, the divine Separator, from which all things have originally risen and sprung.

58. For no knowledge is right or fundamental unless it comes from Divine Science <term>spiritual wisdom or the creative knowledge of God</term>, arising from the differentiation of the Divine Breathing <note>original: "Spiration"</note> from which all things have their origin.

59. Now, if such knowledge is to arise again in man, then the Divine Separator must exist in a substance <note>original: "Essence"</note> like its own—namely, in a Divine Being <note>original: "Ens"</note>—in which the Divine Word speaks, and the Divine light shines within that same speaking or breathing.

60. And even then, human science (which has begun <note>original: "inchoatively"</note> to arise...

# The Sixth Epistle.

...arisen from the breathing <note>original: "Spiration"</note> of the Word) may in that same light see not only itself, but likewise all other natural things according to the separation of the Word; and in a spiritual <note>original: "Magical"</note> manner, work in and with all things in a Divine way, nature, and property.

61. For man is blind to all of God's works and has no true knowledge unless the Divine breathing <note>original: "spiration"</note> or speaking is revealed in his internal ground <term>the deepest, most essential part of the soul</term>, according to the nature and property of that Breathing from which all Beings originally proceed.

62. All of man's searching and seeking, by which he hopes to find the root of a thing, is blind and is conducted only on the shell or outside, which covers the essence of the Tree.

63. If there is to be a true discovery, then human knowledge <note>original: "Science"</note> must enter *into the property of the thing* and be able to behold the very Separator <term>the divine power that divides and forms individual nature</term>.

64. Therefore, it is the greatest and most exhausting misery of mankind that they run and seek entirely in blindness. They begin to seek the "shell" in the literal text <note>original: "bare letter"</note> and its various expressions [or many forms of writings], whereas all things are outwardly marked <note>original: "signed"</note> exactly as they are in their internal being <note>original: "Ens"</note> and essence. The Separator of all things has shown and set himself forth visibly and formally, so that the Creator is known in and by the Creation.

65. For all beings are but one single Being, which has breathed itself out of itself and has separated and formed itself. Yet it proceeds out of that same impression or formation into a uniquely distinct center—that is, with each impression and forming of the desire.

66. Where the separated, partitioned, and divided will impresses and forms itself into a particular individuality, a "Center" arises. In that Center, a Separator or Creator of its own self [or being] arises—namely, a former of the re-expressed or re-breathed will. We see this in the Earth, where every herb has its own Separator within itself, which creates and separates it into its own form.

67. Now, if man (being God’s image, in whom the Divine speaking is manifest according to Divine knowledge) wishes to search the creatures and gain real understanding and knowledge of them—be it in animals, plants <note>original: "Vegitables"</note>, or metals—he must once again obtain grace from God. He needs the Divine light to shine in his knowledge so that he may be able to see through the natural light; then all things will be opened and revealed in his understanding.

68. Otherwise, he continues in his seeking like a blind man who speaks of colors and yet neither sees nor knows any color; this...

<summary>This page argues that true understanding of nature and divinity comes from an internal spiritual awakening ("Divine breathing") rather than superficial study of texts or outward appearances. 68. All states and classes <note>original: "Orders"</note> of the world must consider that they all run blindfolded without the Divine Light, following only an astral and sidereal <note>referring to the influence of the stars/astrology</note> imaginary fancy, according to how the constellations of the stars form and frame themselves within human reason.

69. For *Reason* is nothing more than a *human constellation*, which is a dark draft or resemblance of *all the Principles*; it exists only in an imaginary figure and not in the Divine Knowledge <note>original: "Science"</note>.

70. But if the Divine Light is manifest and shines within it, then the Divine Word begins to speak (or work) there out of the eternal knowledge <note>original: "Science, or Wisdom"</note>. Then Reason becomes a true mansion or receptacle of divine knowledge and revelation, and only then may it be used rightly and truly. But if it lacks this light, it is no more than an *astrum* <term>the "star-spirit" or astral influence that governs the physical world</term> of the visible world.

71. Therefore, it is declared to all lovers of the arts—whose Separator <term>the divine power that divides and shapes nature</term> is a most subtle artist—that they must *first seek God’s love and grace* and surrender themselves to it, becoming wholly one with it. Otherwise, all their seeking is merely a delusion or the "courting of a shadow," and is to no purpose. Nothing of fundamental worth will be found unless one person entrusts another with something.

72. This is forbidden to the children of God, in whom grace is revealed: they must not cast pearls before swine, upon pain of eternal punishment.

73. They are only permitted to declare the light and show the way to attain the pearl.

74. But to give the Divine Separator into unrefined <note>original: "bestial"</note> hands is prohibited, unless one knows the path and the will of the person who desires it.

75. Therefore, my beloved brothers, based on such consideration and instruction, I will (through the permission of divine grace and the cooperation of this present time) briefly decipher and represent the Divine Mystery to you: how God, through his Word, has made himself visible, sensible, perceivable, and furthermore, creaturely and formal. Please consider this further, but let it be done as mentioned above; otherwise, I will be like one who is mute to you, and the blame for that should not be assigned to me.

76. God (what he is in himself) is neither nature nor creature, neither this nor that, neither high nor deep. He is the Abyss and the Ground <note>original: "Bythe"; refers to the foundation or source of being</note> of all beings, an eternal One where there is no physical ground or place. To the creature in its own strength or capacity, he is a *Nothing, and yet he is through all things*. <margin>6</margin>

77. Nature is *his "Something"* with which he makes himself visible, sensible, and perceivable, according to both eternity and time.

<summary>Boehme distinguishes between "Reason," which is merely a reflection of the stars, and "Divine Light," which allows the Word to work within a person. He also defines God as an eternal "Nothing" or Abyss that uses Nature as a "Something" to become perceivable.</summary>

78. All things have arisen through the Divine Imagination, and they still exist in such a birth, station, or government.

79. The four elements likewise have such a foundation <note>original: "ground [birth, or Original]"</note> from the imagination of the *Eternal One*. Concerning this, I will set down a table here showing how one unfolds and breathes <note>original: "spirate," a theological term for the way the Holy Spirit or divine life-force proceeds or flows</note> itself forth out of another.

80. In this attached table, the foundation of all the mysteries of the Divine Manifestation is portrayed for further consideration. The understanding and capacity for this is not within Nature's own ability without the Light of God; but it is easily understood by those who are in the Light, and it is childlike <note>simple and plain</note>.

81. Just as my writings show sufficiently and extensively, here it is only represented briefly in a figure or *scheme*.

82. And so, sirs, I commend and commit you to the greeting <note>original: "salutation"</note> of the *love of Jesus Christ*; *who, by his presence <note>original: "aspect"</note> and greeting, is the very key to understanding this table.*

->*Dated, 11 November,*<-

4. 5. All of these things are worthless before God. Instead, a new creature in Christ, born of God, is what matters before God; for *Christ alone is the Grace that has value with God.*

6. Now, whoever is born of Christ, lives and walks in him, and "puts him on" (according to the inner man) in his *Suffering, Death, and Resurrection*, is a member of his body. From that person alone flow the streams of living water, through the powerful Word of Christ, which—regarding the *internal foundation*—has *become* human within them. Within these spiritual forms, the "Science" <note>original: "Science"; here meaning the innate knowledge or potentiality within the divine powers</note> of the Powers stood in the "Desire"—that is, in the *Fiat* <note>Latin for "let it be done"; God's creative command</note>. In this state, every Science, through its desire for manifestation, brought itself into a physical, bodily existence. *In the same way*, the same grand Mystery—namely, the essential Word of God’s power—lies within humanity (the image and likeness of God) according to both eternity and time.

8. The grace of God in Christ must be made manifest in the mystery of his soul’s life, cooperating and willing within his human life.

He must become like a child who turns with all its affection to its mother and drinks in the mother’s milk of grace. From this, a new *essence* <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for the core being or substance of a thing</note> grows, in which the life of grace arises. That is, *the imputed grace* must be born and become a human reality within him, in his internal foundation. Without this, no one is a Christian, no matter how many devout displays he makes. Let him pretend, flatter, and do what he will, his sins must be forgiven him only through the *Divine Conversation* <note>original: "Alloquy"; from the Latin for speaking to or with someone</note> or *Breathing-in* <note>original: "Spiration"</note> within himself.

14. Then the divine <margin>* Or, breeding or hatching.</margin> *impregnation* begins and proceeds, in which the humanity of Christ is conceived and born. This alone is the *Temple of the Holy Spirit*. From this new birth, the fiery soul eats God’s bread, which comes from heaven. Without this, a person has no life in them (John 6). No hypocrite hiding under the "purple mantle" of Christ can enjoy this. It is only for the person who is not born of flesh and blood, nor of the will of man, but is reborn of God—the person in whom the Word of God (from which the first human was created) speaks, rules, lives, and wills.

16. This present world neither can nor will understand this, for it has wholly and fully turned itself toward a selfish speaking for the *pleasure* of the *flesh*. It speaks from its own self-will regarding purely earthly and transitory things, such as honor, might, power, and authority. Moreover, it speaks of pride, greed, envy, and malice. It utters nothing but the cunning, crafty "Serpent" <note>the devil or the deceptive ego</note> and its offspring. When these offspring cannot obtain or uphold what the self-will desires, it then speaks from a place of cunning, mischievous malice and iniquity—*with money* and through selfish power and violence. It employs many thousands of soldiers who must maintain it by force, so that the self-will which has departed from God may be truly upheld. We see this now before our eyes, through which expression this self-will is also beaten down, and it kills and destroys itself.

17. Therefore, beloved sir and fellow member of the "Life-Tree" of Christ, I would entreat you in a Christian way and stir you up (as one member is bound to do for another) amidst the current *expression* [the ways and courses] of the world. In this world, the *Great Turba* <note>original: "Turba Magna"; the principle of chaos, agitation, or the "great disturbance" that brings destruction and judgment</note> also plays and expresses itself, and there shall be a great contesting, pulling down, or degrading. I urge you to constantly and steadfastly keep yourself in the internal speaking of God's mercy, and continually enter into your internal foundation. In no way should you be persuaded or misled by the Serpent toward the false speaking of *brother-slaughter*. Instead, you (as an honorable lord) should continually behold yourself in the mirror of Christ’s life and teaching.

18. For this current speaking is spoken in the wrath of God through His awakened and ignited anger. It is very evil and dangerous to have a *hand and voice in it*, especially when the *Turba* <margin>Punishment or severe execution <note>Boehme uses "Turba" to refer to the spirit of destruction or divine judgment</note>.</margin> must be spoken. It is altogether unfaithful; it devours its father and mother who bring it forth, and it is a broom <note>original: "Besom"; a broom made of twigs, here used as an instrument of cleansing or destruction</note> of God’s anger.

19. Also, great care must be taken regarding the acceptance of or joining with any of the *supposed religions* for which men contend and fight. Do not assent with a conscience of faith to any party simply because it wins the victory. For there is no other true faith that saves except *CHRIST IN US*. He alone destroys sin in us and crushes the head of the Serpent's imagination in us. He arises from the *sleep of death* in God’s righteousness (which He has fulfilled in us with His blood).

I have written to him asking that he send them to me in Zagan <note>now Żagań, Poland</note>, to Mr. Christian Bernhard, from whom I shall receive them by one means or another. Or, if you yourself have any reason to travel toward Zagan, please send them to Mr. Christian Bernhard, who lives by the marketplace. A year ago he was a customs official <term>original: "Customer"; a collector of customs duties or taxes</term>; he is a young companion of the *Theosophic School* <note>The circle of students and friends who studied Boehme’s mystical "Divine Wisdom"</note>, and I have a convenient opportunity to reach him every week.

25. These treatises are very much desired by the lovers of truth and may do much good. I pray you, send them at the first opportunity, for it is of great importance. When you find convenient leisure to study, I will send you something deeper, for I have written throughout this autumn and winter without ceasing. I commend you to the love of Jesus Christ and His gracious protection.

# THE EIGHTH EPISTLE:

### An Answer to four QUESTIONS.

1.  ***Regarding the Serpent, which after the Curse must eat earth and creep upon its belly.***
2.  ***Regarding Paradise and the Garden of Eden.***
3.  ***Whether the beasts (since they were in Paradise, and yet entirely earthly) also fed upon paradisiacal fruit?***
4.  ***Whether the beasts, before the Curse, were as wild, hairy, and rugged as they are now?***

->**Our Salvation is in the Life of Jesus Christ within us.**<-

24. I entreat you to send my three treatises (*namely*: 1. *Of Repentance*; 2. *Of the New Birth*; 3. *Of Resignation*; some of which I gave you myself, and the rest I sent by Mr. Rudolf) to Mr. Rudolf of Gersdorf. I have written to him asking that he send them to me at Zagan, to Mr. Christian Bernhard, from whom I shall receive them through one person or another. Or, if you yourself have any reason to go toward Zagan, please send them to Mr. Christian Bernhard, who lives at the Market Place. A year ago he was a Customer <note>original: "Cuftomer"; a collector of customs duties or tolls</note>. He is a young companion of the *Theosophic School*; I have a convenient opportunity to reach him every week.

25. These treatises are much desired by those who love this work and may do much good; please send them at the first opportunity, for it is of great importance. When you find convenient leisure to study, I will send you something deeper, for I have written this autumn and winter without ceasing. I commend you to the love of Jesus Christ and His gracious protection.

->**Dated, 19 Feb. 1623.**<-

# THE EIGHTH EPISTLE:

## An Answer to Four Questions.

1. *Concerning the Serpent, which must eat earth and creep on its belly after the Curse.*
2. *Concerning Paradise and the Garden of Eden.*
3. *Whether the animals (given that they were in Paradise and also entirely earthly) also fed upon paradisiacal fruit?*
4. *Whether the animals, before the Curse, were as wild, hairy, and rugged as they are now?*

->**Our Salvation is in the Life of Jesus Christ within Us.**<-

Worthy, much-respected, very learned, and beloved friend and brother in Christ, our only life: I heartily wish you a happy New Year. May you begin this year in the Divine Will, through the drawing of the Father toward Christ. May you also finish it in this time through the effective, working power of the Spirit of Christ in His vineyard, so that many grapes may grow in the Garden of Christ within you. I pray that God would be pleased to preserve you "in the bundle of the living" <note>A biblical phrase from 1 Samuel 25:29, meaning to be kept safe under God's protection</note> during this year, when the constellation <note>original: "Constellation"; Boehme often uses astrological terms to describe the spiritual and physical alignment of divine judgment or natural forces</note> of His wrath draws the sword; as I do not doubt, but...

I do not doubt that the time is at hand when strife and controversy shall be transformed into truth.

...are arisen; where the pride of the Devil has been involved in these questions and has so imprinted and modeled <note>original: "immodellized"</note> itself on the image of man that they have sought for their own images and opinions, and have therein extolled and advanced themselves. *Christ’s Humility*—in which we should die in Christ from our evil nature—is quite forgotten; so that for the present, we are more like a monster of an image than a living Christendom in spirit and in power.

10. For a Christian must and ought to stand in the Tree of Christ with the increase and growth of Christ’s life; he must also live in the spirit of Christ and bear fruit. In such a person, Christ himself (as to the internal ground) lives and is all in all. He continually breaks the head of the serpent's will <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, symbolizing the defeat of temptation and sin within the human heart</note> in the flesh and brings to nothing the works of the devil. He must know, will, and do from Christ; it must come to effective action (that is, into the Divine working), for without this, *no one is a Christian*.

11. Christ must wholly receive and take possession of the internal ground of the soul, so that the severe justice of God (which holds us captive in anger) might be satisfied with Christ’s fullness [and effective merit]. Thus, Christ may fill the anger of God in us with love and mortify the will of the devil, as well as the nature in the wrath of God, and wholly annihilate its will. In this way, the person may die in the love of Christ and bring forth a new will in the love-spirit of Christ through the nature of the soul, which lives and walks in God, as St. Paul says, *Our conversation <note>original: "conversation"; in 17th-century English, this meant "way of life" or "citizenship"</note> is in the Lord*.

12. Lip-service <note>original: "Lip-labour"</note> and the chatter of the mouth avail nothing; they do not make a Christian. A Christian must always be born again (or regenerated) of Christ; otherwise, he is no Christian. No outward imputed righteousness or grace helps at all.

13. All the comforting, flattering, soothing, and dissembling is but in vain where the purple mantle of Christ is put upon the man of iniquity and malice [or the Cain-like hypocrite], who wants to be an adopted child of grace from the outside while remaining evil within.

<margin>* One who is pregnant.</margin>
14. For no prostitute, or *one who is pregnant*, can be a virgin, even if she puts on a maiden’s garland; indeed, no prince or potentate can gift her with any virginity.

15. This is how the flattering hypocrisy and comforting [with Christ’s merits and promises] is to be understood: unless we are converted and become like children who hang on the breasts of their mother, and receive and conceive in us the <term>Ens</term> <note>Latin: "being" or "essence." Boehme uses this to describe the spiritual substance or power of Christ entering the soul.</note> [or essential power] of Christ, which destroys the harlot within us. We must do this so that a new spirit may be born in us out of Christ, which carries within it Christ’s sufferings and death; so that we are born out of his resurrection and resign ourselves to the whole process of Christ. This is what "imputed grace" in Christ truly means.

<summary>Boehme argues that true Christianity requires an internal spiritual rebirth and the actual presence of Christ's spirit, rather than just intellectual belief or outward claims of righteousness. 16. A Christian must be born again and regenerated by the same grace, so that they are a Christian in and of Christ—specifically, a true branch on the tree that is Christ. This allows the engrafted Word of life to spring forth and become essential, living, and active in the soul. 17. Beloved friend Mr. Frederick, your questions require a detailed explanation. In my treatise or commentary on *Genesis*, <note>Boehme refers to his work *Mysterium Magnum*, an expansive commentary on the first book of the Bible.</note> they are all addressed at length. ## The First Point.

->*Regarding the Serpent, which must eat dust and crawl on its belly after the Curse.*<-

18. First, concerning the topic of the serpent (which after the curse must feed on the earth and crawl on its belly), I answer that although this was its *shape and form*, its body and spirit were not as evil within the "fiery science" <note>original: "fiery Science"; here meaning the energetic or alchemical inner workings of nature's foundation</note> of nature's foundation as they became after the curse.

19. For both "tinctures" <note>term: Tincture refers to the essential spiritual quality, life-force, or "color" of a being's soul or essence.</note> of good and evil—originating from the first and second principles—were manifest in it. Therefore, it was so exceedingly cunning that its nature was able to see the foundation of the whole creation within its own center and qualities.

20. Before its origin as a creature (when it was brought out from the "Grand Mystery" <note>original: "Grand Mystery"; translating the Latin *Mysterium Magnum*, the undifferentiated source from which all things were created</note> into the distinct state of a created being), it was in its foundation a fair and excellent *Ens* <note>term: Ens (Latin) refers to a spiritual essence or 'being-ness' before it takes physical form.</note> of great power and virtue.

21. But the Devil's imagination—from the time he sat like an enthroned prince with great power and dominion in the foundation of nature—poisoned this *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note>. When it was separated into a specific creature, it formed itself into a serpent. Therefore, the Devil used the serpent as his instrument, employing the same cunning and poison which held the greatest power to make Eve monstrous <note>meaning: to corrupt Eve's divine form into a fallen, earthly one.</note>.

22. You physicians! You certainly ought to know and understand the mystery of the serpent and what lies hidden within its poison. If you extract it and follow the correct process, you may obtain a *tincture* against poison unlike any other that can be found.

23. It existed as an essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> within the *Grand Mystery* before it was a creature...

She was a creature and a virgin, but after the curse, she became a whore—this is to be understood magically or parabolically.

24. She saw within herself the foundation of both the inward and outward world. Therefore, one must emerge from the inward world and kill the monster that she has forced upon Eve. An entire book could be written about what the desire of the Devil has accomplished through her.

25. But when she helped to deceive the Image of God <note>This refers to Adam and Eve as they were originally created in God’s likeness before the Fall.</note>, then God cursed her so that she became blind to the internal foundation. She also became entirely manifest in the four elements <note>The physical elements of fire, air, water, and earth.</note>. Thus, she fell into the earth from which the body was taken; moreover, she fell only into the "wrath" (the corrupt or bad part) of the earth. She can no longer obtain or reach the good part or quality of the earth as other animals do. Therefore, she must eat "earth"—specifically, the quality of the curse within the earth.

26. She was a flying worm <note>original: "Worme"; in this period, "worm" often referred to a serpent, dragon, or creeping creature.</note>; otherwise, nature would have provided her with legs as other worms on earth have. However, her nimbleness, wily subtlety, and cunning caused Eve to long for the forbidden fruit.

### The Second Point.

#### *Regarding Paradise and the Garden of Eden.*

27. Paradise was the <term>temperature</term> in Man—a state of perfect balance and harmony—when he did not yet know what good and evil were. There, the divine light shone through nature and <term>tinctured</term> and tempered all things. Paradise is revealed in us again through Christ, within our internal foundation.

28. But when God saw and knew that man would fall, Paradise no longer sprang forth with fruit through the earth across the whole world (even though it had been manifest everywhere). Instead, it remained only in the Garden of Eden where Adam was tempted. For Eden is the place, but Paradise is the *quality*—namely, the life of God existing in the harmony of universal being.

### The Third Point.

#### *Whether the animals (being that they were in Paradise and also entirely earthly) also fed upon Paradisiacal fruit?*

29. Beloved friend Mr. Frederick, every spirit eats from its mother <note>This is a foundational principle in Boehme's thought: every being draws its primary nourishment from the source or "mother" from which it originated.</note>.

* The <term>fifth essence</term> <note>original: *Quint-essence*</note> in the Spirit of the World <note>original: *Spiritu Mundi*</note>.

29. The beasts likewise ate of their "Mother"—meaning that which they were made from. Specifically, they ate of the **fifth essence** of the earth within the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: *Cosmick spirit*</note>. For the deepest nature of animals is not at all like the nature of humanity. Thus, they fed upon their "Mother"; their spirit feeds upon the Spirit of the World, and their body feeds upon the four elements.

30. God knew very well that man would not remain steadfast but would fall. Therefore, what use or profit would <term>Paradisiacal</term> <note>Having the qualities of Paradise—perfect, pure, and incorruptible.</note> food be to the beasts? In the fifth essence, there remains a Paradisiacal property, and animals feed upon that even to this day. For in every beast, there is a power that is incorruptible, which the Spirit of the World draws back into itself at the **Separation of the Last Judgment**.

### The Fourth Point.

->*Whether the beasts were as wild and rough before the Curse as they are now?*<-

31. Beloved Mr. Frederick, the "garment" which **Adam** had before the Curse (when he was still "naked") was exceedingly beautiful and suited him very well. Likewise, the hides of the beasts were rough and hairy to them even then. However, in the Curse, all things—both in the beasts and in the plants of the earth—were deformed and changed into a monstrous, strange form. Originally, they did have such a covering, but it was far more glorious in its colors, features, and appearance because of the pure **Tincture** <note>In Boehme's philosophy, the "tincture" is the spiritual life-force or inner quality that gives a thing its beauty and vitality.</note>.

<margin>
* Or, the book called the *Great Mystery* <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*</note>; An Exposition upon **Genesis**.
</margin>
32. Regarding these questions, I entreat you to look into the **Great Mystery** <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*</note> with the eyes of Christ, in whom all the treasures of wisdom lie. Then you shall see these things better in your understanding than I can briefly set down in writing in this haste. I commit you to the love of Jesus Christ.

<margin>1.</margin>Worthy, much respected, and very learned Sir: I heartily wish for you exactly what my very soul desires from God; namely, the real, true **Divine Knowledge** in the love of Christ. I pray that God would graciously open the **Center of the Soul**, whereby the paradisiacal lily-branch <note>Boehme frequently uses the "lily" to symbolize the flowering of the spiritual life or the "new man" within the believer.</note> in Christ’s rose garden might spring forth, grow, blossom, and bear fruit; and that the streams from Christ’s fountain might flow from you; and that you might be taught by God, so that his Holy Spirit might guide and rule you. *As it is written: Those who are led and moved by the Spirit of God are the children of God.* <note>Referencing Romans 8:14.</note>

2. I have received your letter, and through it, I understand that you have read my writings and that you delight in them. I wish from my very heart that the sense and right meaning of them may be apprehended and understood; then there would be no need for any further questioning and searching.

<margin>3.</margin>For the book in which all **mysteries** <note>original: *Mysteries*</note> lie is man himself; he himself is the book of the Being of all beings, seeing as he is the likeness <gloss>or similitude</gloss> of God. The great **mystery** <note>original: *Arcanum*; Latin for a profound secret or hidden mystery used in alchemy and mysticism.</note> lies within him, and the revealing of it belongs only to God's Spirit.

This same <gloss>Spirit</gloss> seeks and finds all **mysteries** <note>original: *Mysteries*</note> in the **Divine Wisdom**.

5. For the lily-branch which springs forth in the **new birth** out of Christ’s humanity (meaning the **newborn spirit**, out of the soul’s essence and out of Christ’s power) is the true, real branch springing from and remaining in God’s tree.

# THE
# NINTH EPISTLE.

->*May the open fountain of God in the heart of Jesus Christ be our refreshment and constant light.*<-

<margin>1.</margin> Worthy, much respected, and very learned sir, I heartily wish for you exactly what my very soul desires from God: namely, real, true *Divine Knowledge* in the love of Christ. I pray that God would graciously grant the opening of the *center of the soul*, so that the paradisiacal lily-twig in Christ's rose-garden might spring forth, grow, blossom, and bear fruit, and that the streams from Christ's fountain might flow from you. May you be taught by God, so that his Holy Spirit might guide and rule you: *As it is written, "Those who are led and moved by the Spirit of God are the children of God."* <note>Romans 8:14</note>

2. I have received your letter and understand from it that you have read my writings and delight in them. I wish from my very heart that their true sense and meaning may be grasped and understood; then there would be no need for any further asking and searching.

<margin>3.</margin> For the book in which all mysteries lie is man himself; he himself is the book of the Being of all beings, since he is the likeness <gloss>or similitude</gloss> of God. The great secret <note>original: *Arcanum*</note> lies within him, and the revealing of it belongs only to God’s Spirit.

4. But if the lily in the humanity of Christ springs forth in the *new birth* out of the soul, then the Spirit of God proceeds out of that same lily as if from his own origin and ground; and that same <gloss>spirit</gloss> seeks and finds all *mysteries* in the Divine Wisdom.

5. For the lily-branch which springs forth in the new birth out of Christ’s humanity (understand this as the *newborn spirit* arising out of the soul’s essence and out of Christ's power) is the true, real branch springing from and remaining in God’s Tree.

<summary>In this opening to his ninth epistle, Jacob Boehme explains to a learned seeker that true divine wisdom is found within the human soul—the "book" of all mysteries—rather than through external study. He describes the spiritual "new birth" as a lily-branch growing from the soul through the power of Christ.</summary>

13. 14. Then the Kingdom of Christ and of God is freely given to him out of grace.

15. For no one can claim this glory for themselves unless the love of God again presses out of grace into the center of the soul. This love brings the divine will out of the "fire" of the soul as a new sprout or new image into heavenly essentiality <term>essentiality: the actual substance or being of God</term>, just as light shines out of fire. <margin>6</margin>

16. Therefore, everything that Babel <note>original: "Babel"; Boehme's term for the confused, divided, and worldly institutional churches</note> teaches regarding external "imputed" righteousness, external assumed adoption, and the idea of specific election and rejection from eternity <note>A reference to the doctrine of double predestination</note> is without foundation or footing. Christ said, "*You must be born again, otherwise you cannot see the Kingdom of God.*"

17. The seemingly holy, flattering comfort found in Christ's death is useless unless one actually enters into Christ's death to spring up anew in him—to rise in him and with him, and to become Christ (or an anointed child of God) in the "new man."

18. Just as Christ has mortified <term>mortified: killed off or subdued</term>, extinguished, and overcome the world—as well as the anger of his Father (which is the center of Eternal Nature)—within the soul's property by his love (that is, with the new fire of love introduced into the soul’s essence, where the Devil had previously placed his desire); even so must we, in and with Christ's spirit, quell and quash the earthly Adam within God's anger. We must mortify it through God's love so that the new man may spring forth. Otherwise, there is no forgiveness of sin, nor any adoption (or filiation <term>filiation: the process of becoming a child of God</term>), nor any righteousness. <margin>6</margin>

19. The Kingdom of God must be inwardly innate and born within us, or else we cannot see with the eyes of eternity into the angelic world.

20. All imaginations, inventions, and methods—all reading, studying, and teaching—are to no purpose without this path of the new birth. No art or human reason can attain it. We must enter only through the gate which God has opened to us in Christ, springing forth in God’s Kingdom and dying to the earthly will so that it neither hinders us nor sticks to and clogs us. *The seed of the woman must continually bruise the serpent's head within us.* <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted by Boehme as the divine spark in the soul overcoming the fallen, serpentine nature</note>

21. *Self-reason cannot make a child of God; for it does not depend on our willing, running, or making a great effort (as Saint Paul says), but on God's mercy and compassion.*

22. My selfhood <term>selfhood: the ego or the "I" that seeks its own will apart from God</term> cannot attain it. My selfhood must die in Christ's death and fail—or resign itself—unto "the nothing." Then my selfhood falls into God’s mercy and is at the starting point of the first man, standing again in the word *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be done," referring to the creative word of God</note>, where God’s mercy, through Christ's entrance into our humanity, recreates the new man out of grace.

23. And therefore, the corrupt earthly will must die in a real, true, and upright repentance, and enter into Resignation <term>Resignation: the total yielding or surrender of one's own will to the will of God</term>; that is,

26. 27. Thus (beloved Sir, and Brother), and in no other way or manner, have I found the Mystery; I have not studied or learned it from books. But if you or any other person thirsts after it, I am committed as a brother in my affection and love to show him the way I encountered it, as I have set down at length in my writings—chiefly in the book *The Threefold Life of Man* and in the book *The Three Principles of the Divine Being*.

28. Indeed, I wrote these for myself as a spiritual exercise in the knowledge of God, regarding the mystery of the great wonders of God. Nevertheless, by God’s providence and guidance, they have come far enough to be published and read. I would gladly wish that everyone who earnestly desires to understand them might have them; and I wish from my heart that this truth may be truly manifest and made known within the reader of this Epistle, and within everyone personally. Then there would be no need for any further searching and seeking.

29. But seeing that God has promised through the Prophets (especially in *Joel*) that he will pour forth his spirit in the last days upon all flesh, the timing of this must be considered and noticed.

<margin>Note.</margin>
30. I say, as I have known it, that whoever at present will die to himself, the spirit of the Lord shall apprehend <term>apprehend: to take hold of or seize</term> him according to *Joel’s* prophecy and manifest His wonders through him. Therefore, if anyone is in earnest, he shall find it by experience.

31. Yet let everyone be faithfully warned: if God’s light arises within him, he must continue steadfast in great humility and resignation—namely, in the death of Christ.

32. (For the Heaven shall now at last pour forth its long-contrived *outpouring* <note>original: "Egestum"; Latin for a discharge, waste product, or something cast out. <meta>This page concludes the Ninth Epistle, in which Jacob Boehme warns against the spiritual pride of certain radical groups and offers a final exhortation regarding the spiritual urgency of his era.</meta>

# The Ninth Epistle.

<margin>The proselytes <note>original: "Prosolites"; converts or followers</note> or disciples of Isaias Stiefel and Ezekiel Meth, who claimed perfection in this physical body <note>Stiefel and Meth were contemporaries of Boehme who taught that the physical body could become divine and sinless in this life, a view Boehme rejected as spiritual pride.</note>.</margin>

33. As can be seen by the *Methists* <note>Followers of Ezekiel Meth</note>, who reached even to the gates of the *Abyss* <note>original: "Deep"; the divine foundation or "Ungrund"</note> but were again captured by the influences of the worldly realm <note>original: "starry Heaven"; the physical world governed by astrological forces</note>. They turned inward toward themselves and became arrogant; they ceased their struggle against the Serpent <note>a reference to the devil or the ego's temptation</note> and entered into a state of "selfhood"—a unique, devilish pride <note>original: "Luciferian conceit"</note> in their own holiness—supposing that they were transformed into a deity. In doing so, they have confused the external world with the internal spiritual world.

34. This view is unsound and lacks any foundation; we must be very careful of it. We must ensure that we remain steadfast in the deepest humility, so that the seed that is sown may grow into a tree and reach its blossoming, and that the *Spirit of God may take shape within us.*

35. For from that blossom arises *the Morning Star*, so that a person may learn to know who they truly are, and what God and Time are.

36. I tell you this, Sir, out of genuine affection: this current time must be taken very seriously. The *seventh angel in the Book of Revelation has prepared his trumpet*; the powers of heaven are in a unique state of motion. Furthermore, both gates stand open, and both light and darkness are in a state of intense longing; whatever path a person chooses, that is the one they will enter.

37. While some will rejoice exceedingly at this, others will mock it; and then the painful and severe judgment upon *Babylon* <note>original: "Babel"; Boehme used this term to represent the corrupt and divided institutional churches of his day</note> will follow.

38. And so I entrust you and your family to the pleasant and lovely *Love of Jesus Christ*.

# THE TENTH EPISTLE,
### CONCERNING
## The Killing of the Antichrist within Ourselves
### AND ALSO
## How we may attain Divine Contemplation.

->*Our Salvation is in Christ Jesus.*<-

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'W' featuring intricate floral and vine patterns within a square border.</image-desc>

HONORABLE and much-respected Sir, I wish you the grace, knowledge, and blessing of God in Christ Jesus. After I was informed by D. K. <note>original: "D. K."; likely Dr. Balthasar Kober, a physician and close friend of Boehme.</note> that you, as a Christian brother and fellow-member in the Lord, possess a sincere desire for the Father’s drawing toward Christ Jesus <note>A reference to John 6:44: "No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws them."</note>, and that you also strive in your mind to reach divine contemplation and vision within yourself, I did not want to miss the opportunity, at the Doctor’s request, to greet you with a short letter. I wish to briefly declare to you, out of my own spiritual gifts and Christian love, the way to divine vision and feeling. By this, I present to you in brotherly love the "sap of my little coral" <note>original: "Sap of my little Corall"; Boehme frequently uses organic metaphors. "Coral" here likely refers to his modest but precious spiritual insights or his writings.</note> in the spirit and life of Jesus Christ, just as one branch or twig on a tree is bound to support the other. I hope to be clearly understood, so that perhaps I might further encourage your zeal.

2. Since you clearly perceive within yourself that the Antichrist in Babel <note>original: "Babel"; Boehme uses this term to represent the "city of confusion"—the corrupt institutional churches and the spiritual blindness of the world.</note> holds sway and governs throughout Christendom, and acts...

[...nourishes] self-interest and the desires of the flesh; and our dear *Immanuel* <note>meaning "God with us."</note> has faithfully warned us of this, saying, *“Flesh and blood shall not inherit the Kingdom of Heaven” (John 6).* <note>Boehme is likely paraphrasing John 6:63 ("the flesh profits nothing") and 1 Corinthians 15:50.</note> And yet the Antichrist seeks and desires nothing else but earthly honor, might, and power, to climb up and promote himself in the desires of the flesh. This has been clearly revealed to me through the grace of the Most High; therefore, I would briefly declare to you what a Christian is, and also what the Antichrist within a person is, for your further consideration.

3. Christ says: *“Whoever does not forsake houses, land, money, goods, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, and deny themselves and follow me, is not my disciple or servant; also you must turn and become like children, or be born anew of water and the spirit, otherwise you shall not see the Kingdom of God.”* This does not mean that one should run away from their vocation and <margin>* Or, employment.</margin> calling, leaving their wife and children for a solitary desert and wilderness and abandoning everything; rather, one must only forsake the Antichrist. That is, the *SELF* in everything—the [mine and thine] <note>original: "meum and tuum"; Latin for "mine and thine," referring to the concept of private ownership and ego-driven attachment.</note>.

4. Whoever wishes to reach divine contemplation and feeling within themselves must put to death the Antichrist in their soul and depart from all self-interest of the will—yes, even from all created things. They must become the poorest creature in the self-interest [selfishness or self-seeking] of their mind, so that they no longer have or own anything as their own property, no matter what their status or condition may be.

5. Even if he is a *King*, his mind must abandon all sense of ownership and consider himself in his position, dignity, and earthly goods as nothing other than a servant of God. He must realize that he ought to serve God and his brothers there, and that he holds and possesses all he has not by natural right—as if it were his own [to do with according to his own will and pleasure]—but that it belongs to his fellow brothers and members. God has placed him as a steward and official over it, and he must remember that he serves his Lord, who will require an account from him.

6. He must wholly and fully surrender his own will (which drives him to such a possessive attachment [or selfish affection or union with created things]) to the suffering and dying in the death of *Jesus Christ*. He must humbly beg God in sincere repentance and conversion to put to death this evil will of selfishness and earthly desire through the death of *Jesus Christ*, and bring the will of his soul into the true adoption or sonship <note>original: "filiation"; the state of being a child of God.</note> of God. In this way, he would no longer will or desire anything for himself, but that...

<summary>Boehme defines the "Antichrist" as the internal spirit of selfishness and possession, arguing that true Christianity requires a mental surrender of "mine and thine" rather than a literal abandonment of one's social duties.</summary>

--- Page 156 ---
<meta>This page continues Boehme's internalizing of the "Antichrist," identifying it as the "self-will" or ego that separates the human soul from the divine will. He explains the process of spiritual rebirth through humility and the restoration of the "Angelic Image" lost by Adam.</meta>

-># The Tenth Epistle<-

May God's will be his own will and desire; let him be dead (regarding the soul's will) to his own **self-interest** <note>original: "owne-hood," from the German *Ichheit*, meaning the ego or the state of being focused on oneself.</note>, so that God in Christ might be his life.

7. He must completely submerge his will into God's mercy with the deepest humility. He must seize a resolution, based on the Divine promise of grace, that at this very hour he will depart from all self-interest in the pleasures of this world and never enter into them again—even if he should become the fool of the entire world because of it. He must wholly immerse himself in the deepest submissive lowliness and unworthiness before God with repentance. Yet, within his soul, he must seize and hold fast the promise of grace, standing firm like a soldier before his enemy when his life and body are at stake.

8. When this happens, his own will—which is the **Antichrist**—will be captured and put to death through the death of Christ. His soul will soon become like a simple young child who has lost its natural understanding of self-interest; it begins to cry out before God like a young child before its mother, trusting the mother to give it whatever she pleases.

9. And this is what Christ meant when he said, *“You must turn and become as children, and forsake all, and follow me.”* For Adam turned away from God’s will into self-will. In his own self-desire, he brought the deceptive suggestions of the Serpent, and the will and desire of the Devil, into himself. Thus, he brought himself and his life’s comfort—which previously stood in mutual harmony and agreement in one single will, which was God’s—into division and disunion. The properties of nature departed from their equal agreement and concordance. Each property entered into its own self-interest (being a private or peculiar self-desire), from which the lust and imagination for both good and evil arose in him. Heat and cold immediately fell upon him, and he died to the holy life of mutual harmony in which he had lived within one single, pure **Element** <note>In Boehme’s theology, the "one pure element" is a spiritual substance where the four material elements (fire, air, water, earth) exist in perfect balance.</note>, where the four elements were in him in equal weight or **balance** <note>original: "Temperature."</note>.

10. And God warned him of this, saying: *“Eat not of the Tree of the knowledge of good and evil, or else you shall die.”* By this, He meant the death to the Kingdom of Heaven—namely, the loss of the beautiful **Angelic Image**. That image died immediately in the false, introduced desire of the Serpent. Therefore, this false will of the Serpent must first die in Christ’s death through true conversion. Out of this death, Christ arises in his spirit again within us, in the heavenly image that died in *Adam*; thus, the inward man is regenerated and born anew in Christ's spirit.

11. This new spirit comes to **Divine vision** <note>original: "Divine vision or contemplation," likely referring to *Theoria* or spiritual insight.</note> within himself.

<summary>Boehme describes the "Antichrist" as the internal ego (self-will) that must be put to death through humility and repentance to allow for spiritual regeneration. He explains that the Fall of Adam was a shift from divine harmony to a divided "self-interest," which can only be reversed by becoming like a child before God.</summary>

himself; it hears God’s Word and has <term>Divine understanding</term> and inclination, and can behold the <term>Grand Mystery</term> <note>original: "Grand Mystery" (Mysterium Magnum); in Boehme's thought, the chaotic or unmanifest source from which God brings forth the world.</note> in Divine and natural mysteries. And although the earthly flesh still clings to him in its inclination, it does not hurt or spoil the new-born spirit in him at all.

12. In this new birth, he is like solid, fine gold in a rough, drossy stone; the drossy casing of the stone is unable to destroy or spoil the gold. For his true will is dead to earthly desire and continually desires to kill and mortify the lust of the flesh. 13. And, beloved Sir, I give you to understand—as a Christian and brother in all faithfulness, sincerity, and uprightness—that we in our *Supposed Religion* (where men do nothing but contend, confute, and revile one another about the literal text and the different opinions devised from it) are still in the midst of <term>Babel</term> <note>original: "Babel"; symbolizing the confusion of tongues and the divided, sectarian state of the church.</note>. It was never worse than it is now, even while men boast that they have left <term>Babel</term> and have the true religion—a claim I leave for you to consider carefully.

14. But they have only used it to cover the Antichristian child of self-will, and so they have painted over the Antichristian bastard with a different color.

15. For men flatter it excessively, covering it with Christ’s suffering, merit, and death. They comfort it by saying that Christ has paid for everything, suggesting that it only needs to apply or comfort itself with the merit of Christ and receive it in faith as a satisfaction. Thus, they show us only an outward <term>imputed righteousness</term> <note>original: "imputed righteousnesse"; the theological concept that Christ's righteousness is credited to the believer's account, which Boehme argues is being used as an excuse to avoid internal transformation.</note>. <margin>6</margin>

16. But true understanding has a completely different *A-B-C*. No amount of self-comforting, self-willing, striving, or ritualistic repetition <note>original: "keeping a round"; likely referring to formal, repetitive religious ceremonies.</note> is worth anything. The suffering and death of Christ will not be given to the Antichristian beast within the self, but to those who depart from and relinquish all attachment to the ownership and properties of created things. They must wholly resign themselves to the suffering and death of Jesus Christ; they must die to their own will, in and with Christ, and be buried with Him. They must also rise in Him to a new will and obedience, and hate sin. To those who put on Christ in His suffering, reproach, and persecution—taking up His cross and following Him under His *Red Banner*—to them, I say, it will be given. These people put on Christ through His own process and become, in the inward spiritual man,

<summary>Boehme distinguishes between the "new man" (gold) and the "earthly flesh" (dross) and critiques contemporary religion for using Christ's merit as a "cover-up" for internal sin rather than undergoing a true death of the self-will.</summary>
