<meta>This page continues the discussion of how a true Christian must be a "member" of Christ and a "temple of God" through inner transformation rather than mere outward profession.</meta>

->### The Tenth Epistle<-

...Christ’s members and the Temple of God, who dwells in *us*.

17. No one has the right to take comfort in Christ’s merits unless they truly desire to fully "put on" <note>original: "put on Christ"; a biblical metaphor from Galatians 3:27 for adopting Christ's nature and character.</note> Christ within themselves. A person is not truly a Christian until they have put Him on through genuine repentance and conversion to Him, with absolute <term>resignation</term> <note>original: "resignation" (Gelassenheit); a central concept in Boehme’s thought meaning the total surrender of the self-will to God's will.</note> and sincere self-denial, so that Christ may be united and betrothed to them.

18. This begins to take place in the <term>Covenant of Baptism</term>, where the child promises and swears loyalty under Christ’s red banner—a promise that must later be followed by actual practice. If someone has turned away from the practice of what they then promised, they must return to it through a conversion of their will. I say with absolute certainty that for many, the "Mantle of Christ" will turn into hellish fire because they use it to hide their inner <term>Antichrist</term>, remaining nothing more than a beast in their nature.

19. For a Christian must be born of Christ and die to the <term>Adamical will</term> <note>original: "Adamical will"; the fallen, self-centered nature of humanity inherited from Adam.</note>. They must have Christ within them and be a branch or member of His flesh and spirit—not according to their animal nature, but according to the spiritual person.

20. For the Spirit of God does not take possession of the "beast"—that is, the outward, sensual, natural, or rational person—but rather the Temple of Christ, which is Christ’s spiritual flesh and blood in *us*. For Christ said, *“Whoever does not eat the flesh of the Son of Man has no life in himself.”* <note>original: John 6:53.</note>

21. Now, there must be a mouth that is proper and fit to eat it, for it will not be given to the beastly nature, and much less to the <term>essence of the Serpent</term> <note>original: "Ens of the Serpent"; the poisonous, sinful nature introduced by the Fall.</note>. Every spirit eats from its own "mother"—the source from which it arose. I leave this for every understanding person to consider; here I only mention what a Christian ought to be if they wish to call themselves a Christian.

22. For a beast is not a Christian. A Christian is one who is baptized with the Holy Spirit into the death of Christ, who has "put on" Christ, and who lives in Christ’s heavenly flesh and blood. They have tasted Christ’s <term>Supper</term> and sit at the table with Christ. A Christian is one who walks in Christ’s footsteps and continually <term>mortifies</term> <note>original: "mortyfieth"; to put to death or subdue the sinful desires of the body.</note> the antichristian, evil beast within their flesh and blood (which still clings even to a Christian). They bind it, strip it of its strength, and patiently surrender themselves during the temptations which are offered in a hundred different ways for their trial and purification.

23. A Christian must learn the "ABC’s backwards" <note>This phrase suggests unlearning worldly logic and prideful reason to start over with spiritual simplicity.</note> and consider the wisdom of their own reason to be foolishness, so that Christ may take form within them and they may become capable of receiving heavenly wisdom.

24. For the wisdom of the outward world is blind in respect

...of God, yet does not see Him. Although all things live and move in God, and He Himself is through all things, yet He possesses nothing except that which dies to its own will. 25. I could mention more about this to you, if the occasion allowed. 27. I have done this at the request of the doctor mentioned above, in all sincerity and uprightness; and so, I commend you to the tender love of Jesus Christ.

# THE ELEVENTH EPISTLE:

### Our Salvation is in the effective, working Love of Jesus Christ in Us.

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'D' featuring floral and leaf patterns within a square border.</image-desc>

1. Dear Brother in the life of Jesus Christ, I wish from my heart the Divine working Love unto you, so that your noble lily-twig <term>lily-twig</term> <note>original: "Lilly-twig"; in Boehme's mystical writing, this represents the blossoming of the spiritual life or the "new man" within the soul.</note> sprung forth in Christ may grow great in the power of Christ and bring forth much fruit in the Paradise of God, to the heavenly joy of us all and our eternal brotherly fellowship.

2. I rejoice in my soul when I perceive that a goodly, virtuous, fair *Branch* has sprung up in our Tree of Life, Christ; and I hope also to be a sharer of its good fruit.

3. As one branch on the Tree enjoys the sap and power of the others, and they all mutually grow and bear fruit in one single Power; so likewise we are all only One in the Tree of Christ—which [Tree] *is CHRIST in us ALL.*

4. Seeing then that you freely and sincerely, with all acknowledgment of heart and mouth, commit yourself to this Tree of Life, and on the contrary renounce and reject the poison and delusion of Satan; therefore, I wish for nothing more at present than that I might be able, in the power of this Tree which is Christ, to impart the influence of my power received from Him to you, so that we might grow together as members in one Power.

5. And I have no doubt that the Most High has begotten His *lily-twig* in you; for without Divine Power we have no longing or hunger for God, and we also cannot know Him without His Spirit in us. All that we understand and know of Him fundamentally <note>original: "fundamentally [or in reality]"; knowing something from its very basis or essence.</note> comes from His Revelation and Operation.

6. For although the world prates and talks much of God, it only does so out of custom, and receives its knowledge from history <note>original: "Hyſtory"; here meaning "historical knowledge"—an intellectual or book-learning of scripture that lacks direct, living spiritual experience.</note>...

<summary>Boehme greets his "brother in Christ," using the metaphor of the Tree of Life to describe the spiritual unity and mutual growth of believers. He emphasizes that true knowledge of God comes only through His direct revelation and the "lily-twig" of spiritual rebirth, rather than mere intellectual study.</summary>

# THE TWELFTH EPISTLE:
### TO Mr. JOHN BUDOFSKY.
->*Our salvation in the life of Jesus Christ.*<-

*Worthy, much respected Sir,*
### All sincere wishes of divine salvation in holy power, and of all temporal <note>original: "temporall"; relating to worldly life and physical well-being as opposed to spiritual life.</note> welfare, are here offered.

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial 'I' decorated with scrolling foliage and floral patterns.</image-desc>

I have received your letter sent to me for Christian friendship and refreshment in divine knowledge, in divine desire, and affectionate, hearty Christian love; it is exceedingly welcome and acceptable to me.

2. And I also rejoice that God still has his children and a little flock <insert>here and there</insert>, whereas otherwise, at present, the world is deeply drowned in wickedness and is caught in the <insert>fire of anger, which shortly shall make a great tear in antichristian Christendom</insert> <note>Boehme frequently used "Antichristian" to describe the established church structures of his day, which he believed had lost their true spiritual essence.</note>, as it is known and manifest.

<margin>* Or, Following,</margin>
3. <insert>And that man does very well and rightly who learns to know himself correctly—what he is</insert>, which cannot be brought to pass through **Reason** and sharp searching [or deep studying and speculation in the natural arguments of **Reason**] but in the true * <term>process of Christ</term> <note>original: "processe of Christ"; Boehme's concept that a believer must spiritually relive the stages of Christ's life—humility, suffering, death to the self, and resurrection—to be saved.</note>, in a truly resigned soul <insert>which disclaims and forsakes **Reason** and its own wit and human selfhood <note>original: "selfnesse"; the state of being focused on one's own will or ego instead of God's will.</note></insert>. Such a soul enters with a true conversion from the earthly way into the highest simplicity of Christ—into the true and deepest humility under the <term>Cross of Christ</term> <note>The "Cross of Christ" here refers to the internal struggle and the "death" of the ego or self-will.</note>, as Christ has faithfully taught us and said: *Unless you turn and become as children,*

<meta>catchword: Children,</meta>

<summary>In this opening of the Twelfth Epistle, Boehme greets John Budofsky, celebrating their shared faith and warning that true spiritual understanding comes through humility and the "process of Christ" rather than intellectual reasoning.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, John Budofsky, self-knowledge, humility, Reason, selfhood, Antichristian Christendom, process of Christ</keywords>

--- Page 165 ---
<meta>This page continues the Twelfth Epistle to John Budofsky. The previous page established that true self-knowledge cannot be achieved through intellectual reason alone, but through the "process of Christ" and childlike humility.</meta>

<page-num>121</page-num>
<header>The Twelfth Epistle.</header>

*Children, unless you are born anew of the water and the Holy Spirit, you cannot see the Kingdom of God.*

4. To this, a true and real **Resignation** <note>original: "Resignation"; translating the German *Gelassenheit*, a central concept for Boehme meaning the total surrender of one's own will to God.</note> and a renouncing of the <term>human self</term> belongs. In this state, a person completely retreats into their inward **Ground** <note>original: "Ground" or *Grund*; the deepest, most essential part of the soul where the human meets the Divine.</note> and entirely annihilates their own "Self." They turn themselves through earnest repentance, with an entire inward desire, away from this world's being and toward God. They must die to their own strength and self-will in the death of Christ, falling down or sinking into the mercy and compassion of God. In this way, they may be seized by the Holy Spirit within their own inward ground, so that the Spirit may see, will, and act through them in whatever is pleasing to God. The Spirit alone is the true Searcher of divine knowledge and the light of the soul; in this light, the soul beholds and knows God, and in no other way can it attain divine and natural knowledge, vision, and contemplation.

5. For the natural, rational man understands nothing of the mystery of God's Kingdom, for such reason is outside of God and not within Him. This is plain and manifest in those learned in human reason, in that they contend and wrangle about the being and will of God and yet do not know it, for they do not hear God's Word within themselves.

6. Everything is dead and void of understanding regarding God if it does not have the living voice and the divine hearing of the **new birth** within the <term>essence of Christ</term> <note>original: "Ens of Christ"; from the Latin *ens* (being/essence). It refers to the spiritual substance of Christ that Boehme believed was birthed within a believer.</note>. This allows the Spirit of God to give testimony to the person's outward hearing and teaching. Only in this internal seeing is God known and His Being understood; the outward literal or written Word is merely a form and a prepared instrument for this.

7. But true understanding must flow from the inward ground, out of the living Word of God (which must first be opened and revealed within a person) and then enter into the written Word so that there may be one agreement and harmony. Otherwise, all teaching of the divine Being and Will is nothing but building upon the great **Babylon** <note>original: "Babylon"; used here to represent the "city of confusion," or a state of spiritual blindness and intellectual pride.</note> of earthly reason and wonders.

8. In this internal ground, all my knowledge concerning the divine and natural foundations has its rise, beginning, and understanding. I was not born of the schools of this world, nor was I educated in scholarly arts; I am a plain, simple man. But by God's spirit and will, I have been brought—without my own purpose or desire—into divine knowledge and high natural investigations.

9. This knowledge and free gift of grace I shall heartily and willingly share with my dear brothers and fellow members in the **Tree of Life** of Jesus Christ. I daily pray to God that their hearts might be opened to divine hearing and understanding, so that such knowledge might be manifested and made known in them as well.

<summary>Boehme argues that true divine knowledge comes from the total surrender of the self to God's inner light rather than academic study. He identifies himself as an uneducated man whose profound spiritual insights were granted directly by the Holy Spirit.</summary>
<keywords>Resignation, Inner Ground, Holy Spirit, New Birth, Reason vs. Revelation, Essence of Christ, Babylon, Jacob Boehme</keywords>

...[them], so that we might be delivered from the contentious, disputing <term>Babylon</term> <note>original: "contentious Disputing Babylon"; for Boehme, Babylon represents the confusion of warring religious sects and intellectual pride that obscures divine truth.</note> and be brought into a single brotherly love, hearing within ourselves what God's will and being is.

10. And Sir, I want you to know that your acknowledgment and the friendship you have shown are very welcome to me. I also wish to discuss divine matters with you and find refreshment in them. Since we are so far from one another, this cannot be easily done, and yet it may still happen. At that time, I will answer the points you raised and speak with you about them in depth, which cannot be done now in haste. I commend you and your family to the gentle love of Jesus Christ.

# THE THIRTEENTH EPISTLE.

## A LETTER Written to one in TEMPTATION and trouble of mind, showing where it arises.

->**Our salvation is in the life of Jesus Christ in us.**<-

---

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'D' featuring floral motifs, a central chalice or urn, and two small human figures or faces in the bottom corners.</image-desc>

1. DEAR Sir, my fellow-member and brother in Christ our Savior; sharing first my heartfelt wish and cooperative desire for divine love and grace: I want to let you know in Christian love that I have considered your condition with Christian sympathy and fellow-feeling. I have brought it before the gracious compassion of the Most High to see what he would be pleased to reveal to me about it.

2. Therefore, Sir, I must tell you that through that same gracious compassion, I obtained such an insight and *vision* of your condition and temptation <note>original: "Temptation"; in this context, it refers not just to the urge to sin, but to a profound spiritual trial or "dark night of the soul" where one's faith is severely tested.</note> that its ground and cause has been made known to me. I will set it down briefly as a *memorandum* <note>original: "Memorandum"; here used as a formal record or note for the recipient to keep and reflect upon.</note> so that you may consider and ponder it seriously by yourself.

3. The first cause of such a strong, active temptation is the supernatural, superabundant, and unspeakable love of God (that is, the divine...

<meta>catchword: Divine</meta>

<summary>Jacob Boehme writes to a fellow Christian experiencing severe spiritual distress, claiming that he has received a divine vision revealing the source of these trials. He begins by identifying the paradoxical first cause of this suffering as the overwhelming love of God.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, spiritual temptation, mental distress, divine love, vision, Christian sympathy, internal life of Christ, 17th-century spirituality</keywords>

--- Page 168 ---
<meta>This page continues the Thirteenth Epistle, detailing the internal spiritual conflict between the divine will and the "created" human will. Boehme explains that the recipient's distress is actually a sign of Christ working within them to overcome their fallen nature.</meta>

<page-num>124</page-num>
<header>The Thirteenth Epistle.</header>

...Divine goodwill, and the created <note>original: "creaturall"</note> will of man (struggling against one another). The human will refuses to fully resign and give itself up with total confidence to such great grace of God, which is offered <note>original: "tendred"</note> to it out of pure love. Instead, it seeks itself and its own love of transitory things <margin>Or, Things.</margin> and loves itself and the material things <note>original: "beings"</note> of this world more than God.

4. Therefore, man’s own nature (which, in its own center without the love of God, exists in mere anguish, strife, enmity, and restless <note>original: "unquiet"</note> conflict) tempts him. Into this nature, the Devil also shoots his false desires to lead man away from such high grace and the love of God.

5. This temptation is the greatest of all. It is the very combat that Christ maintains—with his love poured out into human nature—against such selfishness. He also fights against God's anger, sin, death, the Devil, and hell. In this combat, the "human Dragon" <note>Boehme uses the "Dragon" to represent the prideful, rebellious, and fallen aspect of the human ego or "self-will."</note> must be devoured by the love of Christ and transformed into an angelic image.

6. And if the love of God in Christ *did not have its influence in you*, you would have none of this combat. Instead, the Dragon (namely, the false, devilish will) would maintain its natural rights and possession without any such conflict or disturbance.

7. Now, therefore, this perplexing and distressing temptation is felt very intensely in one's nature because of the Dragon. He is in the labor pains <note>original: "travelling anguish"</note> of his own nature when such great love of God enters him and seeks to change his natural rights into a *divine*, self-denying will.

8. For here Christ, the Serpent-destroyer, stands within man—even in "hell"—and storms or attacks the Devil’s strong fortress. This is where the strife arises, where Christ and Lucifer fight for the soul, as God has allowed you to see and know through experience in this first temptation.

9. Thus Christ *bruises the head of the serpent, and the serpent stings Christ in the heel* <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15, interpreted here as the spiritual struggle between divine grace and the fallen human nature.</note>. The poor soul stands in the middle in great trembling and sadness. It can do nothing but stand still in hope; it is not even able to lift up its face before God and pour out its effective prayers. For the Dragon turns its face toward the vanity of this world and shows it the beauty and glory of this world. He mocks the soul because it wants to become another creature, and he presents to it the kingdom in which it lives and its natural foundations.

10. And here the soul stands with Christ in the wilderness, during the *forty days of temptation*, where the power, glory, riches, and pleasures...

<summary>Boehme describes the spiritual struggle as a "combat" between Christ's love and the "human Dragon" of self-will, identifying the recipient's distress as a sign of Christ's active presence. He likens this inner turmoil to Christ's forty days of temptation in the wilderness and the bruising of the serpent's head.</summary>

[plea]sure <meta>The text begins mid-word, likely completing "pleasure" from the previous page.</meta> of this world is offered <note>original: "tendred"</note> to it, alluring it to elevate itself and enter into its own self-will.

11. The second temptation of *Lucifer* and the selfish "Dragon of nature" <note>Boehme uses the "Dragon" to symbolize the prideful, unregenerate human ego or "self-will" that resists God.</note> is this: when the soul has tasted divine love and has been once illuminated, the soul then wants to have that same light as its own property <note>original: "propriety"</note>. It wants to work within that light by its own power and ability as if it were its own peculiar possession. Understand this: the nature of the soul, which is a Dragon like *Lucifer* when it is without God’s light, wants to have that light for its own property. But this Dragon will not resign its natural right; it wants to be a maker and disposer of the divine power and live within it with great joy in its fiery, selfish nature. And this cannot be.

12. This Dragon (namely <note>original: "Viz."</note>, the fiery nature) must be changed, along with its own will, into a Love-fire and let go of its natural right. But it is unwilling to do so. In such a change or transformation <note>original: "transmutation"</note>, it looks for its own self-power and yet finds none. Therefore, it begins to doubt grace because it sees that in such work it must forsake its natural desire and will. Because of this, it is continually afraid and will not die to its own natural right in the divine light; instead, it always thinks that the light of grace (which works without such sharpness and fiery might) is a false light.

13. Whence it comes that outward reason (which is blind and sees nothing correctly on its own) continually thinks: **Oh!** Who knows how it is with you—whether it be true or not that God has illuminated you, or that he is in you? It likely proceeds from such a delusion <note>original: "Fansie"</note>. You do not see the like in other people, yet they think they will be saved as well as you. You only make yourself the fool of the world by this, standing in fear and trembling at God’s anger more than those who comfort themselves only with the promise of grace upon the future revelation.

14. Thus it happens that the internal ground <note>Boehme uses "ground" (from the German *Grund*) to refer to the deepest, most fundamental center of the human soul.</note> then sighs and pants for the inflammation and movement of the light and would gladly have it. But nature is able to do nothing; it is as if it were wholly rejected by God. This is also true regarding the self-will, for God has planted a new will *into it*. It must die to its own will and be changed into God’s will.

15. And because the will of nature must die here and resign its own right to the will of God, there are such grievous temptations within it. For the Devil will not have his stronghold <note>original: "Prey-Fort"</note> fall or be demolished; for if Christ shall live in man, then the spirit of self-lust...

<meta>This page continues Jacob Boehme’s Thirteenth Epistle, further exploring the spiritual "temptations" that a soul faces during its regeneration. # The Thirteenth Epistle.

15. Self-lust and imagination must die, and yet they do not *wholly die during this life because of the flesh; they die daily, and yet live*. Because of this, there is a conflict that no wicked person feels, but only those who have "put on Christ" <note>A biblical reference to Galatians 3:27, meaning to be spiritually clothed or transformed by Christ’s nature.</note>, in whom Christ fights with *Lucifer*.

16. The *Third Temptation* is in the strongholds of the Devil—namely, in the will and mind, as well as in flesh and blood. This is where the false centers lie in a person, such as a selfish will toward a proud worldly life, the lust of the flesh, and earthly things. It also includes the many curses people have wished upon one's body and soul through temptation. All the sins that have taken root and concentrated still remain in the *Astral spirit* <term>Astral spirit: In Boehme's philosophy, this refers to the "starry" or psychic part of the human soul influenced by the physical universe and worldly desires.</term> as a strong fortress. Christ now fights against this and will destroy it. The human will still values and holds this stronghold of power, pleasure, and the beauty of this world as its own property and best treasure; it will not surrender it or be obedient to Christ.

17. Therefore, beloved sir and Christian brother, I tell you and give you to understand what our loving Lord Jesus Christ has shown me in my meditations: examine yourself to see what your temptation is. Our dear Lord said, *“We must forsake all and follow him,”* so that we might be truly *Christ-like poor*.

<margin>* Or, Truly spiritually poor.</margin>

18. Now, if your mind still clings to self-centered lust, imagination, and the love of earthly things, then you will experience such temptation within those centers <note>original: "Centres"</note> that still work in you.

19. But if you will follow my simple <note>original: "child-like"</note> counsel, I tell you this: when such temptation arises in you, you must then imagine nothing else for yourself except the bitter suffering and death of our Lord. Consider the mockery and scorn, the contempt and poverty He underwent in this world for us poor people. Resign your *desire* and whole will into that, so that you would very gladly be conformed to His *Image* and, with all sincere willingness, follow Him in His *process* <margin>* Or, Way of life.</margin>, and patiently endure whatever is laid upon you to suffer—and do so willingly for His sake. Desire only to be conformable or like Him. For the sake of His love and will, be content to be lowly, despised, held in contempt, and afflicted, so that you might maintain and keep *this His love in you*. No longer will anything for yourself, but only what Christ wills through you.

20. Dear sir, I fear that there is still something in you that is displeasing to Christ, which is why there is such conflict within you. Christ wills that you should die with Him to your own will, through His death, and arise in His will to live with Him. *Christ is currently in your soul, striving for your soul.*

<summary>Boehme describes the "Third Temptation," where the human will clings to worldly power and pleasure within the "Astral spirit," and advises the recipient to find peace by surrendering their will to the suffering and example of Christ.</summary>
<keywords>Third Temptation, Astral spirit, self-will, resignation, spiritual poverty, imitatio Christi, Jacob Boehme</keywords>

21. Let all earthly will go, and resign yourself wholly and fully; let joy and sadness, comfort and conflict, be all one to you. In this way, you shall, with Christ, be a conqueror over the world, the Devil, death, and hell. At last, you will find by experience what Christ has been in you, and why this has happened to you—for this has been the process of all the children of Christ. I speak this out of Christian affection.

# THE FOURTEENTH EPISTLE.

### TO FREDERICK CRAUSEN, AT GOLDBERG.

->*May the open fountain in the heart of Jesus Christ be our refreshment and constant light.*<-

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'W' featuring floral and leaf motifs within a square border.</image-desc>

1. Worthy, learned, and kind Sir, my friend and beloved brother in Christ: with all hearty wishes for the love, illumination, and blessing of God being offered first; your diligent study of *Divine Wisdom* is very acceptable and joyous to me.

2. And it is all the more so because I perceive in your letter that *God* has opened your heart and spirit to a right understanding. I wish from my heart (as indeed I do not doubt at all) that the precious *coral* <note>original: "Corall" – In Boehme’s mystical language, this refers to the spiritual "tincture" or the life-giving essence of Christ's humanity and blood.</note> in the humanity of Christ might again spring forth—within the spirit of Christ and His tender humanity in *us*—from the inward man in your paradisiacal plant <note>original: "Paradificall Plant" – This refers to the spiritual seed within the human soul that was intended for Paradise but withered after the Fall of Adam.</note> which withered in *Adam*, and that it might bring forth true fruits for the Table of God.

3. And I pray that the noble and precious branch may be firmly grafted into the vine of Christ and spring forth anew from it; and that it may blossom with us amidst this present wicked, thorny world, and help to foretell the *summer* of Christ in His time of the *lily* <note>original: "time of the Lilly" – A signature concept in Boehme’s prophecy, referring to a future age of spiritual purity, peace, and the blossoming of divine knowledge.</note>; indeed

<summary>This page opens Jacob Boehme's fourteenth letter, greeting Frederick Crausen and commending his pursuit of spiritual wisdom. Boehme uses botanical metaphors to describe the restoration of the human soul through Christ, looking forward to a prophetic "time of the lily."</summary>

--- Page 173 ---
<meta>This page continues the Fourteenth Epistle from Jacob Boehme to Frederick Crausen. The previous page introduced the "new birth" and the spiritual growth of the "paradisiacal plant" within the believer.</meta>

Indeed, some branches from Christ's rose garden appear here and there; they spring forth like a wonder of God in the midst of the fire of tribulation in *Babel* <note>original: "Babel" – In Boehme’s writing, Babel represents the confused, false, and institutionalized religious systems of the world, often contrasted with the "true" spiritual church.</note>.

4. But as for your saying that my writings have given you some direction—let it be so. Be thankful to God for it, who thus reveals His wonders and deep, hidden wisdom through humble and uneducated <note>original: "mean and unexercised"</note> people. He sets them as a light to those children who, in the "cradle" of this world, labor in their own Babel and fables. They are convinced by simple humility that their works, will, and life are only a carved image and a forged, selfish invention that has no foundation or root in Him.

5. At present, the Most High has given us many ways to understand how, in a short time, His wonders in His hidden wisdom are [and shall] be declared to the world in *writings for its enlightenment*. In these, our descendants and all who receive understanding from God will not only wonder but rejoice exceedingly.

6. I understood from Mr. *Walter* that you have received some of my writings, which delight you greatly. Yet I wish you also had the latest pieces, which are plainer and clearer and have a sweeter foundation. In these, the manifested God may be known very clearly in all His wonders and works.

7. They will provide more light for you in many areas of your practice; for the foundation of nature is clearly discovered there, as is our very beautiful and pleasant Garden of Christ and the *new birth*.

8. Beloved *Frederick*, it will greatly assist your temporal and eternal practice. I hope that you (being a grafted scion <note>original: "engraffred cyon" – A scion is a shoot or twig inserted into a slit on the trunk or stem of a living plant, from which it receives sap. Here, it refers to a person spiritually joined to Christ.</note>) shall not break off from the tree of Divine Wisdom. For shortly a time will come when it shall be of necessary use, and you shall rejoice among the first who depart from *Babel*.

9. I thank you greatly for the gift <note>original: "Present"</note> I have received. In return, I shall carry it in my will into the *Mystery of the Most High*, and it shall be received as a treasure for you; I recognize through this your true and open heart.

10. However, the Pearl <note>original: "Pearl" – Referring to the "Pearl of Great Price" from the Parables, representing the highest spiritual truth or the Kingdom of Heaven.</note> will not be given because of the gift, but for nothing—just as God has done for us in Christ. Thus, one member of the body is bound to another. I commend you to the sweet and pleasant love of *Jesus Christ* and urge you to continue seeking the Pearl.

->Dated, July 17, 1622.<-
->J. B.<-

# THE FIFTEENTH EPISTLE.

->*The salvation and light of God in the life of Jesus Christ enlighten you, and give you further understanding of His will.*<-

1. <image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'C' featuring floral and leaf motifs within a square border.</image-desc> COURTEOUS Sir and good friend; I cannot but rejoice with you, in that you have given up your life to be a plant of God; and so it springs and buds forth in the body of Jesus Christ, the Son of God. He has born us again <note>original: "begotten us againe" – refers to the concept of the "New Birth" or being born again spiritually.</note> as living creatures in Himself, and has set us before His Father as a lovely plant in His pleasant Paradisiacal Garden, to His joy and deeds of wonder.

2. And I find (if I consider correctly) that you are not only a plant of God for yourself, but like a pleasant herb and flower that does not hold its strength and virtue <note>original: "vertue" – in this context, it refers to the inherent power, essence, or healing property of a plant.</note> within *itself*, but casts forth and diffuses its virtue for a sweet delight <note>original: "rellish"</note> unto all living <margin>\* Or, things.</margin> \* *Essences*; and freely presents itself unto all creatures, whatever becomes of it. In this way, it does not spare itself, but continually produces its power and fragrance.

3. And thus I find it to be with the soul of man, which continually grows and freely yields its power or virtue for *him* to taste who desires it and is capable of receiving its power; be it either to love or anger; to the life of God in Christ, or to the life of pride, leading into the deepest state of misery, which in the end befalls those who are not grown in God.

4. But praise, glory, and honor be unto those who are regenerate <note>original: "regenerate" – spiritually reborn or transformed by God's grace.</note> in Christ, who—although they lose their lives here and appear before the *Sting* of the *Thorny Plant* <note>The "Thorny Plant" likely represents the fallen world, "Babel," or the harshness of earthly existence that opposes spiritual growth.</note> as a poor, useless herb that is trampled underfoot—are like an herb that is cut down and is no longer seen or noticed. Reason says it is quite gone, but for all that, it has its root in the earth and springs up;

<meta>catchword: thus</meta>

<summary>Boehme encourages the recipient by comparing the believer's spiritual life to a plant in God’s garden that must share its inner "virtue" or power with the world. He notes that while the faithful may appear defeated or "cut down" by the world, their spiritual root remains eternal.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, New Birth, spiritual growth, Paradisiacal Garden, regeneration, virtue, Christ, thorns</keywords>

--- Page 175 ---
<meta>This page continues the Fifteenth Epistle, picking up mid-sentence from the previous page's discussion of the soul as a plant engrafted into Christ.</meta>

In this way, the soul of the Saints is engrafted into the holy life of Jesus Christ; it stands in God His Father and springs forth again through death.

5. At this (since we have experienced it effectively), we do rejoice; therefore, we value the life of this world—which consists of the influence <note>original: "source"; in Boehme’s writing, this refers to the "Qual" or the driving qualities of the natural world.</note> of the stars and elements—as the least important thing, and we rejoice that we are the children of God.

6. Since we know that God is *really in us*, and yet He is hidden from our earthly life, we know that our soul is in God and grows up in God, while the body is under the dominion of the stars and elements, according to the workings <note>original: "source"</note> of this world.

7. Thus we are God's image and likeness—He who is all things. Should we not, therefore, rejoice? *Who will separate us from God, if the soul is in God, where no death or destruction exists?*

8. Therefore, my dear faithful friend and brother in Christ, I consider it a great joy that I have found in you a precious plant of God. My soul perceived the scent <note>original: "smelt"</note> of this plant and was strengthened by it when the Oppressor <note>The "Oppressor" refers to spiritual enemies or the forces of darkness that seek to stifle the "new birth" in a believer.</note> would have torn it out of the land of the living—when it lay under the oppressors and the thorny plants of Antichrist intended to devour us.

9. But just as God comes to help the branches that remain in Him with His power so that they might not perish—even though the Devil and death storm against them—so they must spring forth again through death and through the wrath or fierceness of the anger and the *sting of death*. And though God bestows the most noble and precious herb of His garden upon it, His will must still prevail; whatever is sown in Him must grow in Him.

10. We know this because He has given His heart (namely <note>original: "Viz."</note>, the most precious plant within Himself) to become man for us, as a strong, sweet fragrance <note>original: "savour"</note> of regeneration in Him. Thus, when we were in death, we might be able to spring forth with and through Him out of death into God His Father, and bring forth the fruits of Paradise.

11. Since we know that we are the plants [fruits or *nursery*] of God, let us not fear anything, but continually grow in the life of God and bring forth fruit to God’s honor and deeds of wonder; we shall enjoy them eternally.

12. And since we know that our precious life stands in great danger (between the Kingdom of Heaven and the Kingdom of Hell, lying captive to both during this lifetime), we must walk warily and circumspectly so that our pearl <note>The "pearl" is Boehme's frequent metaphor for the divine spark or the purity of the soul's new life in Christ.</note> is not broken. We must not let the *scent of* <margin>\* Sin and iniquity.</margin> *wrath* into us to corrupt and spoil us. Otherwise, the precious fruit is hindered in its growth, and God would complain of us *that He is like a vine-dresser who gleans and would gladly enjoy the precious grapes.*

<summary>Boehme describes the believer's soul as a divine plant rooted in Christ that flourishes despite the "sting of death" and worldly oppression. He cautions the reader to protect this spiritual "pearl" from the corrupting influence of sin and wrath.</summary>
<keywords>regeneration, plant of God, Christ, soul, wrath, pearl, spiritual growth, Antichrist, Paradise</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Fifteenth Epistle, picking up from paragraph 12 on the previous page regarding the soul's growth within the divine life.</meta>

13. Therefore, let us be watchful to fight against the Prince of Wrath <term>Prince of Wrath: A reference to Satan or the antagonistic force of divine anger</term>; so that the precious grapes and fruits of God may grow in us. In these, God may find a pleasant scent and taste, so that we may be a pleasant, sweet fragrance to Him in Christ.

14. We shall fully enjoy this when we are freed from the vanity of this life; then we shall live and flourish in God, and partake of the pure life of God without flaw. He will be our food, and we will be His, so that there may be a pleasant, mutual, Paradisiacal growth in one another—we in God, and God in us—in the eternal source of the holy life in God's nursery <note>original: "Gods Nursery"; a metaphor for the spiritual environment where souls are nurtured</note>, where there is nothing but perfection in pure love.

15. For this cause we work so earnestly and suffer the scorn and contempt of the world. While our earthly life arises in death, our heavenly life may flourish through death, so that the earthly life may appear as something lowly <note>original: "scorne"</note> compared to the heavenly—which indeed is not worthy to be called a life when compared with the heavenly one.

16. And therefore we endure patiently in the earthly life and rejoice in the heavenly, in the hope that we shall be freed from vanity. Then we shall be well refreshed with consolation; what we have been compelled to sow here in tribulation and trouble, we shall reap in great joy.

17. Therefore, my very dear brother in the life of God in which you stand, you are more precious to me because you have awakened me out of <gloss>*</gloss> sleep, so that I might go on to bring forth fruit in the life of God, and afterward rejoice in it with the children of God.

<margin>
* That is, by his writing to him to employ his gift <term>Talent: A spiritual gift or ability, referencing the biblical parable</term>; for he intended to write no more after his first book was forcibly taken from him.
</margin>

18. And I want you to know that after I was awakened again, a very strong fragrance <note>original: "Odour"; a mystical term for spiritual perception or divine presence</note> was given to me in the life of God. I hope to bring forth fruit in it and to awaken those who are sleepy, just as God has awakened me out of the sleep in which I lay.

19. And I urge you, for the sake of the holy life of God in Christ, that in the future you would not grow faint or weary. Instead, reinvigorate and enliven your life in Christ, so that our spirits may be perceived and understood, which cannot happen without the divine power.

20. For everyone speaks from his own inner nature <term>Essences: In Boehme's philosophy, "essences" refer to the fundamental spiritual qualities or "being" that constitute a person’s soul</term> regarding the wonders of God, according to how his life is ignited in God. No one can bring us to an understanding except the only Spirit <gloss>†</gloss> of God. On the day of Pentecost, that Spirit changed the tongues of all nations into one in the mouths of the Apostles, so that the people of all nations could understand the tongues of the Apostles. Even though the Apostles spoke from only one tongue, the hearts and spirits of the listeners were opened in God, so that they all understood them, each in his own language, as if the Apostles had spoken in their own native tongues.

† Out of, or proceeding from, God.

### The Fifteenth Epistle.

21. Thus it is only possible in God for one spirit to comprehend and understand another. I am afraid that in many parts of my writings I will be difficult to understand; however, in God, I am very easy and clear to the *Reader*—if their soul is grounded in God. It is only from that spiritual knowledge that I write.

22. For I have very little knowledge from the academic arts <note>original: "historicall Art"; referring to traditional scholarly or book-learning</note> of this world, and I do not write for the sake of the pride and honor associated with such skill. I was not born of their academic training, but out of the life of God, so that I might bear fruit in the Paradisiacal Rose-Garden of God.

23. And I do this not only for myself, but for my brothers and sisters, so that we might be one holy body in Christ for God our Father, who loved and chose us before the foundation of the world was laid.

24. Therefore, just as Christ did not spare his own life—and his true disciples did the same, freely preaching the Kingdom of God even though they suffered scorn and death in this world for it, and only for the sake of the heavenly Kingdom—so we must not fear worldly scorn and death for the sake of the heavenly life. Instead, we should pray that God would deliver us from all evil and give us unity of mind.

25. But I am sorry that you find me so difficult to understand in some points of my writings. I wish that I could share my very soul with you so that you could grasp my meaning.

26. For I understand that these difficulties involve the deepest points on which the main argument depends, where I have used some *Latin* words. But my meaning rests in truth, not merely in the *Latin* tongue, but much more in the *Language of Nature* <note>The "Language of Nature" (Signatura Rerum) is a central concept for Boehme, referring to an intuitive understanding of the essence of things as expressed through their outward forms and names</note>.

27. For it has been revealed to me in some measure how to discern the spirit of the letters from their very origin. I would very gladly give you the meaning and interpretation of those words I have used and which you have misunderstood; but since it would take up quite a bit of space, and I am currently in a hurry, it cannot be done now. However, I am very willing to offer a very clear interpretation of them very soon.

28. For I have been so busy traveling back and forth and attending to other business that I could not satisfy your request in this matter. I ask you to have a little patience and wait for it.

29. I still have so much to do because of my brother's daughter (who died recently). I must travel to the countryside every week, and I was also forced to make two difficult journeys, which took up all my time.

30. If it pleases God that my traveling eventually comes to an end, I hope that my work will be of great service to many a poor soul in its spiritual hunger. Yet, whatever God wills, let it be done; just as many a blade of grass <gloss>*</gloss> perishes,

<margin>
\* Or, withers.
</margin>

->when<-

31. 32. For I consider myself to be the most simple among them; I have written only a little for my own memory and spiritual exercise. But since it pleases you to read it, I have no reason to hide it from you.

Since he is only a worldly man, educated entirely in the "school of this world," we would have little loyalty or security with him.

->*May the open fountain in the heart of Jesus Christ be our refreshment.*<-

1. Noble, honored, and much-respected Sir: With the salutation and kind wish for Divine love and fullness of joy in our *Immanuel* <note>original: "Immanuel," meaning "God with us," a title for Christ</note>, in his wonderfully sweet power, together with all temporal prosperity of body; I wish to let you know that I have been informed how you are a well-wisher to the \* Fountain of Wisdom and make use of some of my writings. I am also told that you have a great desire for the well-spring of Christ and that noble Wisdom, which has moved me to write to you, seeing that you have perused some of my work.

2. However, there are some people who—out of envy, misapprehension, and a misunderstanding of these works—prattle and storm against them. This can be seen in the attached pamphlet, where a poor, proud, and foolish man boasts and rages, and yet has not the slightest understanding of the source from which my writings flow.

3. Indeed, he places a false and most strange sense and meaning upon them so that he might only confirm his own miserable opinion. He has spread around some writings concerning *God’s Election* <note>original: "Gods Election," the theological doctrine regarding those chosen by God for salvation</note> of us, and by doing so, he thinks to entangle and trap us in despair, thereby opening a gate to all lewdness and immorality.

4. Therefore, he does not like the taste of the open fountain of Christ found in my writings. Consequently, I have made a short declaration regarding his attached pamphlet and have given it only briefly for the consideration of whoever reads my book. This is because the core foundation of the matter is to be found sufficiently and satisfactorily elsewhere in my writings. I have done this so that men may see how this critical pamphleteer thinks to beguile and rob us of our chief treasure, upon which our eternal salvation

...fore there must also be the very *same spirit* to understand them correctly. No speculation [or sharp understanding or idea of reason] can reach them unless the mind is *illuminated by God*. To find this, the way is faithfully shown to the *seeking reader*.

9. I speak in good truth and sincerity before God and man, and I also appeal to the judgment of God and declare: there is no good at all in any *disputing* without God’s light and spirit. Nothing that is permanent, constant, undoubtedly grounded, or well-pleasing to God can arise from *that source*.

10. Therefore, whoever wishes to learn how to understand the right and true way to God fundamentally must depart from and forsake their own reason. Let them enter into a penitent, humble life—resigned to God like a child—and so they shall obtain heavenly power and skill. They shall put on Christ’s childlike spirit, which *shall lead them into all truth*. There is no other true way to God but this one alone.

It required a more extensive description and exposition. I intended to keep it for myself, but it was taken from me against my will and published, as you, Sir, know. I commend myself to your favor, and all of us into the gentle love of Jesus Christ.

# THE SEVENTEENTH EPISTLE.

### *Worthy and much-respected Noble Sir,*

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'T' featuring floral patterns and foliage within a square border.</image-desc>

1. My heartfelt greeting and desire for Divine love and the fullness of joy in our *Immanuel* <note>original: "IMMANUEL," a Hebrew name meaning "God with us," referring here to Christ.</note>, in his wonderfully sweet power, along with all bodily and temporal welfare being first acknowledged: I friendly inform you that I have fully considered the conversation recently held. Since I perceive you to be a *passionate lover of the truth and Divine Mysteries*, I would not miss the chance to visit you with this *letter*, seeing that an opportunity has been given to me to answer somewhat on the topic of a person who opposed me on the subject of God’s free grace and *election* <term>The theological doctrine that God chooses certain individuals for salvation before they are born.</term>; and I have sent this, my answer, for you to read over.

2. However, to the extent that the mind cannot remain satisfied with this small amount, I am ready and willing—if it is desired—to write a book to expand and reveal this topic from its very *center* <term>In Boehme’s philosophy, the "Center" refers to the core or origin from which all spiritual and physical realities emerge.</term>, so that the heart might rest *satisfied upon it*. Although, I should suppose that a Christian might find enough in this little bit to be satisfied regarding this and other topics.

3. But seeing nevertheless that this subject has perplexed many people, and because of it, such opinions are established and finalized that open a door for all wickedness to the world, I am therefore grieved by it. It has been given to me to know from the Most High that this topic has *not yet* been understood from its very foundation. I wish from my heart that it might be understood, so that we might not look *so suspiciously* at one another as "human-devils," but as loving brothers and the natural, dearly bought children of Christ. We should walk in a *right, true love* toward one another, which can never be done while holding such a *notion* and *assumption that God chooses one person and not another*.

4. But if I look upon my brother as my own flesh and spirit,

<keywords>Jacob Boehme, Seventeenth Epistle, Election, Predestination, Free Grace, Immanuel, Divine Mysteries, brotherly love, human-devils, theological dispute</keywords>

Even more, my conscience in the spirit of the Lord convinces me that I ought to love my brother as my own life, or as my God. Would God command me to love <insert>one who is</insert> a damned devil? 5. Therefore, for this reason, I have taken the opportunity to write to you and to Christianly entreat and admonish you to better consider this article of faith. In that consideration, do not allow anything at all to possess your mind or take root in you except the pleasant name of *Jesus*. He came into this world and manifested himself in our humanity to seek and save us poor lost men, who were dead to the Kingdom of God, and to restore again what was lost in *Adam*.

6. I do not write this to be a master over you, but in a brotherly manner for a mutual search and spiritual refreshment with you, so that our faith and confidence toward God may be strengthened in the Lord. For we are all only human, and we should rightly behave ourselves toward one another in both doctrine and life as members of the same body; for he who finds his brother in the spirit of Christ finds himself.

7. Much disputing is not profitable at all; it only creates confusion. Go with me in my writings to the Center of all Beings <term>In Böhme’s philosophy, the "Center" is the spiritual core or origin from which all reality—both light and dark—emerges.</term>, and you shall see the <margin>Or, understanding.</margin> origin of good and evil and be freed from all this error. For you shall find so much in my writings that will give real satisfaction to the mind. As far as the Center of all Beings is understood, such joy arises in the mind that it surpasses all the joy of this world. For the noble and precious <margin>Or, the Philosopher's Stone.</margin> stone of the wise men <note>original: "stone of the wise men," a reference to the Philosopher's Stone, which in alchemy was said to transform base metals into gold, but here symbolizes spiritual transformation and the ultimate truth of God.</note> lies within it. He who finds it considers it of higher excellence than the outer world with all its glory. Should it not be a joy to find and know God, so that a person is able to see and find *all things* within themselves—things that are barely explained in a thousand books—and to know this truth in everything? With whom should I argue and wrangle about religion if that same truth is manifest in my heart, so that I am able to truly behold all things in their root and origin?

8. I do not say this to boast about myself, for I am as *nothing* and God is *all in me*. Rather, I say it so that if anyone has a mind to seek, they might also seek and obtain. Although I did not seek it in that way and did not understand it—indeed, I knew nothing of it—I only sought the pleasant, loving heart of *Jesus Christ* to hide myself there from the wrathful anger of God and our enemy, the Devil. But then, more was revealed to me than I understood or even sought for; and from that revelation, I have written, never thinking I would become known among such high-ranking people.

<meta>This page continues Jakob Böhme's seventeenth epistle, where he explains the divine origin of his writings and the necessity of seeking spiritual truth through the Holy Spirit rather than human reason alone.</meta>

9. For I thought that I wrote only for myself and intended to have kept it by me until my end; yet now it is manifest and has come into many men's hands without my knowledge or effort. Therefore, I am urged to entreat you and others, and to remind you not to look at the simplicity or meanness <note>original: "meannesse"; meaning the author's low social status or lack of formal education.</note> of the author, or to be offended at my person. For it pleases the Most High to manifest his counsel through foolish people who are considered as nothing before the world, so that it may be known and acknowledged that it comes from his hand.

10. Therefore, if my writings come into your hands, I would like you to look upon them as those of a *child* in whom the Highest has driven his work. For there is that hidden within them which no human reason may understand or grasp; but it is childlike, plain, and very easy to the enlightened <note>original: "illuminate"; those who have received the inner light of spiritual understanding.</note>. It will not be grasped by reason unless reason is ignited with God's light; without that, there is no finding. This I desire to remind you of, and all those who read them.

11. Christ said, *“Seek and you shall find, knock and it shall be opened unto you: my Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him for it.”* Herein lies the hidden Pearl; he that will have it must obtain it this way, otherwise there is no finding it—save only a half-blind, lame knowledge, like a deceptive shadow of fancy [or a mere echo]. In the Pearl there is a living knowledge, where a man never needs to ask, “Is it true?” For it is written, *“They shall be taught of God.”* Also, *“We will come to you and make our home in you.”* Also, *“He that does not have the spirit of Christ is none of his.”* And therefore Christ says, *“Seek first the Kingdom of God and its righteousness, and then all other things shall be added to you.”* He bids us to strive and seek after it; not to sit still and wait upon *Election* <term>The theological doctrine of predestination, the idea that God has already chosen who will be saved.</term>, but to come to him (Matthew 10) and to labor in his vineyard; and not wait and expect to be driven, but to come willingly.

12. Seeing then that I have found a wise heart in you, I am the more emboldened to write to you, hoping that you will judge wisely. Now, if anything in my writings should seem dark, obscure, and difficult to be understood, I pray you set it down and send it to me as the opportunity arises; I will make it more simple, plain, and clear. And I commend you and yours, and myself with them, in brotherly union, into the meek, tender love of *Jesus Christ*.

->Dated, July 3, 1621.<-

NOBLE Sir, After wishing you the divine love and fullness of joy in our *Immanuel* <note>original: "Immanuel"; a Hebrew name meaning "God with us," referring to Jesus Christ.</note>, in his wondrous sweet power, and all bodily and temporal prosperity; I friendly inform you, as opportunity now allows, that I have considered the *conference* <note>original: "Conference"; a discussion or formal meeting.</note> we had lately. *to seek and save that which is lost*; that is, the poor, lost, damned sinner, caught in the wrath of God and seemingly predestined to damnation; and not the righteous—those who, like *Abel, Seth, Enoch, Noah, Shem, Abraham, Isaac*, and *Jacob*, are already included in the divine *Love*. Instead, he came to seek and call the poor, sinful man held captive by God’s anger—such as *Cain, Ishmael, Esau*, and the like—to return and be converted. As God said to *Cain, "Rule over sin; do not let it have its power."* <note>original: "rule over the sin let it not have its power"; a reference to Genesis 4:7.</note> If *Cain* could not have done this, God would not have commanded it of him. Likewise, if it had not been possible for *Adam* to have stood firm, then God would never have forbidden him the tree.

5. But since man cannot reach such an absolute conclusion, demonstrate it, or fully satisfy the mind in this way—for the mind searches further for [an explanation of] God’s omnipotence—there is another *study* required: that a person learns truly to know the center of all *essences* <term>essences: the fundamental natures or core qualities of all things</term>, both of love and of anger. One must learn what the eternal love of God is, and what the eternal anger of God is—which hardens and devours man, making him a child of eternal death—and how a person may be freed from this prison and captivity of God’s anger during this life.

6. But seeing as I have declared and set this forth so extensively in my books, I thought the mind should be satisfied; especially in the book *The Threefold Life of Man*, and in the *Three Books of the Incarnation of Jesus Christ*; and yet further and deeper in the book *The Six Points concerning the Grand Mystery* <note>original: "Six points concerning the Grand Mystery"; also known as *The Six Theosophic Points*. The "Grand Mystery" refers to the *Mysterium Magnum*, the hidden origin of all things.</note>. This includes the eternal birth of the Deity and the three principles of the three Worlds—how they exist mutually within each other as one, how there is an eternal peace and agreement between them, and how one generates the other and desires the other, such that one without the other would be nothing. I supposed that the mind would find satisfaction there, seeing as this can be demonstrated in every being and thing.

7. But seeing as Master *N.* has some of these writings in his hands (though not all), please inquire after them. If you have an interest in them, you shall find the foundation not only of this article concerning *Election*, but of all *articles of faith*—and indeed, of everything the mind of man turns itself toward—if the foundation *which is opened there* is followed and achieved.

8. My Noble heart, I pray you do not take as a joke what God manifests to us out of his Love. Do not look upon the simplicity of the men through whom he does this; it is his good pleasure to manifest his power through the weak and simple <note>original: "silly"; in the 17th century, this often meant "simple," "humble," or "innocent" rather than "foolish."</note>, as the world accounts them. It is done for the instruction of the world, seeing as everyone lives in contention and strife and will not allow his Spirit to draw them toward knowing and acknowledging that God’s Kingdom is *within us*. Therefore, the

He directs the reader to his more advanced books for a deeper understanding of the "Grand Mystery" and the balance between God’s love and wrath.</summary>

The center of His Being and of all beings is revealed to them. This is done entirely out of His love for us, so that we might yet depart from miserable strife, contentions, and wranglings, and enter into a brotherly and childlike love.

9. Sir, since I have found a longing mind in you, I would not hide from you that this will be a time of serious intensity. I say that blessed and happy are those who are included under the *Sound of the Trumpet* <note>original: "Sound of the Trumpet"; Böhme refers to a spiritual awakening or a divine warning and call to repentance</note> that has *already sounded*. For there is coming hereafter such an earnest severity that Babel <term>Babel: Böhme’s term for the confused and corrupt state of institutional religion and worldly systems</term> and conflict—along with all pride, ambition, falsehood, and unrighteousness—shall drink a bitter draft, even from the cup that she herself has filled. For the sake of your eternal salvation, I urge you to consider this further; it is well known.

10. I am ready—should your mind not find enough solid ground <term>ground: the underlying reality, source, or foundation of a thing</term> in my writings for its rest and satisfaction—to explain and expand upon it from the center of all beings, provided you note down your questions and send them to me. I hope your mind would then be satisfied. However, satisfaction does not lie in mere intellectual searching; for no searching reaches or obtains the *Pearl* <note>The "Pearl of Great Price," representing divine wisdom or the Kingdom of God (Matthew 13:45–46)</note> without God’s light. A penitent, humble mind is required for this—one that completely surrenders itself to the grace of God and does not search for or desire anything except God’s love and mercy. In that surrender, the *bright morning star* eventually rises, so that the mind finds such a Pearl in which both soul and body rejoice. When this is found, there is no further need for searching or teaching; for it is written, *They shall all be taught by God* <note>John 6:45</note>. The *sound of the seventh trumpet* <note>A reference to Revelation 11:15, signaling the completion of God's mystery</note> opens such a Pearl in the hearts of many who earnestly seek it with a humble will surrendered to God.

11. Therefore, my noble heart, I would not hide this from you: much arguing and obsessive thinking in *self-reason* <term>self-reason: human logic or intellect operating independently of divine revelation or grace</term> does not find the Pearl. Instead, it is found by an earnest, focused, and penitent will. This is more precious and costly than the world; he who finds it would not trade it for the riches of the entire world. It provides him with temporal and eternal joy, so that he is able to rejoice and be happy even in the midst of a dungeon of darkness, and he considers the goods of this world as dirt and dung in comparison to it. *Christ said: Seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you* <note>Matthew 7:7</note>. Also: *My Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him for it* <note>Luke 11:13</note>. *HEREIN LIES THE FOUNDATION.*

12. Let no one say, "My heart is shut up, I cannot pray." Even if my heart says a flat "no," I will still cast myself into the suffering and death...

9. For I find the whole understanding of both good and evil, of God's love and anger, and of both desires (namely, of the darkness and of the light). 21. Dear Brother, here lies the wicked child. Learn only to know what God Almighty is in Love and Anger, and how man is that very same being and an image out of the Eternal Spirit.

22. Do not say, "God wills the evil." He cannot will or desire anything that is evil, according to the property in which he is called *God*. But if I should call this property [namely, the property of Anger] God, then I would be calling Hell "Heaven," darkness "light," and the Devil an "Angel."

23. It is true that all things belong to God [or all is God's]; yet God is only understood in the source [or working property] of the love of the light. [Expe]rience: I have been as deep in your opinion as you yourself were. Yet my Saviour has opened my eyes so that I see. I do not see by my own ability or power, but in *his*; as he knows me in himself, so he will see. I wish with all my heart that you might have an insight into my vision, and that you might see with me from my perspective. I would willingly share my heart and love with you as your own possession <note>original: "propriety"; in this context, it means a personal or private possession.</note>, and look through this glass <note>original: "glasse"; likely referring to a looking-glass or mirror, a common metaphor for spiritual reflection.</note> from within you.

26. But I perceive that I am still mute to you, and that I am not yet known to you in the knowledge that has been given to me; and I wish from my heart that this might yet happen.

27. I entreat and exhort you as a Christian, in all humility, that you would simply gather your *objections* together and send them to me in *writing*. I will respond according to my gifts, as a Christian ought, and I will declare and explain them in such a manner that I hope you shall recognize me as a brother in this matter.

28. Not that I presume to do this by myself, but my desire, which burns in me like fire, demands it of you. And I (as I am) hope in God that we shall both prosper so well in this that God will unite us in his love, desire, and knowledge. It shall not cause you any prejudice, scorn, or disgrace, for I have a heart that can keep a secret.

29. Otherwise, my well-wishing, good intent, and efforts are to no purpose; for I can give you nothing but my good affection and charitable will. If you will accept it, *that is well!* If not, I protest and testify before you and before the face of God that I have begun my Christian duty <note>original: "devoir"; meaning a formal duty or task.</note> toward you and within you correctly; I have done my part, as I am bound in conscience to do.

30. I may come to see you myself, if my affairs permit, provided that it might lead to God’s honor and humanity's salvation. For I know many thirsty souls in that area with whom I might find refreshment, and they in me.

...there shall be a horrible storm of hail and rain, at which the Earth shall quake, and many thousand souls shall be drowned in the water.

34. I would gladly mention something further to you here, but at this time it cannot be. Please take notice of the storm toward the *East*; the one toward the *North* is not far from it. In the *South*, there is a great smoke that causes the eyes of those in the *West* to smart.

He has noted her in his wounds pierced with nails; *his light shall shine from the East to the West as a testimony to all people*.

38. From the South, a Lily arises toward the North. He who obtains it for his own possession <note>original: "propriety"</note> shall sing the song of God's mercy. At that time, the Word of the Lord shall flourish like grass upon the Earth, and the nations shall sing the Song of Babel <note>Böhme refers here to the reversal of the "confusion of tongues" at Babel; a return to a unified spiritual language or "one tune."</note> in one tune, for the beginning has found the end.

39. Think about my obscure <note>original: "darke"</note> sayings, for at this time I might not be more plain. Seeing that men have only sought after pride and covetousness, and have despised the mirror of anger <note>A reference to seeing God's judgment reflected in the world's chaos.</note>; they have not repented but have worked iniquity with iniquity until iniquity devours itself and the wrath of God is fully satisfied.

40. *Human Reason* shall hinder little here with its consultations; rather, it shall blow up the fire and provide further occasion <note>Meaning that intellectual analysis and worldly planning will only aggravate the conflict.</note>.

41. God was good before the distress, but since men forsake God, scorn and misery follow.

42. Let everyone take care of himself; but he who does not seek and preserve himself shall be sought and preserved <note>A reference to the Christian paradox of losing one's life to save it; those who surrender their self-will are the ones God preserves.</note>. And so, I commit you into the love of *Jesus Christ*.

# THE
# TWENTIETH
# EPISTLE.

### *Our Salvation in the life of Jesus Christ in US.*

<margin>1.</margin> Noble Sir, etc. Wishing you all heartfelt desires for Divine light and effective Divine working power in the fountain of Love, *Jesus Christ*, and all worldly prosperity. I thought it good to write to you and, out of a faithful Christian intent and affection, remind you of the discussion between *H. N.* and *D. S.* regarding the *Divine purpose and will for humanity.*

<margin>2.</margin> At that time, *D. S.* did not receive a sufficient answer to his question because I was not practiced in their academic <note>original: "Scholastic"; referring to the formal, logic-based theology taught in universities</note> methods regarding this article of faith, specifically in contemplating the internal foundation through the outward foundation. Also, such meetings—due to the alcohol (to which I am unaccustomed)—darken and cloud subtle and pure understanding.

<margin>3.</margin> Furthermore, because of their use of the Latin language [or academic expressions], I was prevented from understanding the matter at its core. Consequently, he began to triumph with his accepted opinion, yet he did so without a sufficient understanding of the cited Scripture passages and without a sufficient basis in logical reasoning—though he is certainly very well practiced in those academic methods.

<margin>4.</margin> After that discourse, I turned myself through Divine grace toward the internal foundation of Divine Vision to test the matter. I prayed to the Lord that he would open my understanding of its entire foundation, so that I might know it in its own distinct nature <note>original: "Species"; here meaning the specific essence or outward form of a thing</note>.

<margin>5.</margin> As a result, it was shown to me that I (through a Divine introduction into the wonderful works of God) have sufficient reason and...

...and grounded in it. Later, because Mr. B. T. and others requested it, I took the opportunity to do so.

6. My intent was not to despise anyone's opinion or to prejudice them with unchristian disgrace or mocking taunts. Instead, I wrote out of a faithful, sincere Christian affection and a brotherly sharing of my *talent*, which God lent to me.

<margin>
What is contained in the Book of Election.
</margin>

7. This work is so deeply and profoundly grounded that one can understand not only the basis of the question concerning God's will, but also know the hidden God through His manifestation in all visible things. It provides a very clear explanation of how to understand the foundation of the *Grand Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"; a term Böhme uses to describe the chaotic "Great Mystery" or potentiality from which God brings forth the universe</note>. This Mystery is the eternally expressed Word of God, in which Wisdom has worked from eternity and in which all things were seen in a spiritual <note>original: "Magical"</note> manner or *Idea* before they had any created existence.

8. It also explains how the same Grand Mystery brought itself—through the expression or "speaking out" of the Divine Science <term>Divine Science: here used to mean God's innate, certain knowledge or self-awareness</term> through the Word of God (in the context of this world)—into a state of separation and comprehensibility for the Creation. Furthermore, it explains how the origin of good and evil is to be understood within the separation of the Divine Science in the Grand Mystery, across the eternal principles, leading to the Divine manifestation and activity.

9. In this, the hidden God may be understood not only in His being and will, but also in the whole foundation of His manifestation through His expressed Word, which comes out of the eternal powers of the Grand Mystery, the very essence of eternity. It shows how this has become a visible, comprehensible, created, and external being, and explains what the *foundation of all mysteries* is and how it has been sufficiently revealed.

<margin>
* The Spirit of the World <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi"</note>.
</margin>

10. The book also contains a large, detailed explanation of the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Cosmick Spirit"</note> in which the creation of this world lives. Additionally, it provides a very clear foundation for understanding the internal, spiritual, angelic, and soul-based <note>original: "foulish"; referring to the nature of the soul</note> life, as well as the rise, fall, and restoration of humanity. It also discusses the symbolic patterns <note>original: "Typifications"</note> of Scripture in the Old and New Testaments concerning the Kingdom of Nature and the Kingdom of Grace, explaining what God's righteousness and His *Election* or purpose is, and how they should be understood.

11. Finally, it offers a clear demonstration of the lineage within the Kingdom of Nature, tracing from *Adam* through his children. It also describes the Kingdom of the manifestation of grace through the *inspired* voice of grace—the embodied Divine Science—found in the *Word of Love* within the womb of Grace.

12. And then I provide a clear explanation of the passages of Scripture—especially of *the 9th, 10th, and 11th chapters of the Epistle of Paul to the Romans*. On these chapters, reason supports itself, and a full perceptible <note>original: "Sensall"</note> foundation is demonstrated by quoting and examining the Scriptures.

13. Yet this is not done in a logical way, as it is treated in the Schools <term>Schools: the universities and theological institutions of the time, often associated with Scholasticism, a method of learning emphasizing dialectical reasoning</term>, where they only create objections and contradictions against one another, contriving knotty arguments and dilemmas. In that setting, one person will not test and examine the foundation and meaning of another in a perceptible way in the understanding. Instead, they bicker, pressure, judge, and condemn one another as heretics, and revile each other. This is indeed nothing else but *Babel* <note>original: "Babel"; a reference to the Tower of Babel, symbolizing religious confusion and the "divided languages" of competing dogmas</note>, a mother of proud, haughty, grand prostitution <note>original: "Whoredome"</note>, of errors and confusion; where the name of God is blasphemed, and the Holy Spirit is reviled and judged by *reason*, based on the literal Word.

14. I have completely disliked following this approach in using my talent. For not one jot or tittle of the *Law* in the *Scripture* shall perish until all is fulfilled; and the sayings of the *Scripture*, together with their types <term>types: symbolic figures, objects, or events in the Old Testament that are seen as foreshadowing something in the New Testament</term>, must remain true and not be contradictory, as reason supposes.

15. And thereupon I have taken those sayings of Scripture which seem contrary to one another (such as, it is written: *God wills that all men shall be saved*; and then again, *God hardens their hearts, so that they do not understand although they see it*) and I have cleared and reconciled them together. I hope in God and for His children that they will see the divine manifestation of grace and understand it, and depart from such strife and controversy about the will of God and the person of Christ, and see—and learn to understand—the justification of a poor sinner before God.

16. I have faithfully and diligently done this toward everyone according to my gifts, out of a Christian, brotherly heart. I further offer that if anyone should still cling to such a concept <note>original: "conceit"</note> and opinion and were not satisfied in his thoughts, let him set down his opinion with his conclusions in writing in a Christian and friendly way and send them to me. He shall receive such an answer to his questions and objections that he shall see that I meant this in a Christian spirit and that it came from a divine gift.

17. Seeing, Sir, that you—together with your brother Mr. *H. S.* and likewise the deeply learned doctors *J. S.* and *J. D. K.*—are my very much respected friends, and in the Life-Tree of Christ my eternal fellow members and brothers in Christ; and I, as a fellow member (from a religious heart), do rejoice also with them, seeing God has adorned and endowed them with understanding and wisdom,

This has come to pass from the beginning of the world until now, *whenever great changes are about to occur*.

21. Sirs, know for certain that I will not be lacking in giving an answer to any man's high or profound questions, provided they are *virtuous, appropriate, and Christian*; for this knowledge is committed to me in trust from the Most High and given as a free gift of grace.

22. I mention this with a Christian intent and affection: if anyone still has any doubt regarding that opinion, I would see whether I could, in love, help him to free himself from it and bring him into the *Temperature* <term>Temperature: a state of spiritual balance or harmony where the soul's conflicting "qualities" are reconciled</term> of the mind. I would not think any pains too great to share my gifts and understanding with him. And so I commend you and yours into the love of *Jesus Christ*, and myself into your favor.
