# A POSTSCRIPT.

23. The tribulation and destruction of Babel <note>Babel: Böhme’s name for the confused, divided, and hypocritical institutional churches of his time</note> approaches with exceeding haste; the storm arises upon all coasts. It shall be a severe <note>original: "soar"</note> tempest; vain hope deceives, for the breaking of the tree is at hand, which is known in the wonders.

<margin>Domestic and internal <note>original: "intestine"</note></margin>
24. The homegrown fire hurts its own native country; righteousness and truth are trodden underfoot; great sorrow <note>original: "heaviness"</note>, trouble, and calamity grow quickly.

25. Men shall mourn for an old, empty, ruinous cottage on which salvation does not rely; they will be enraged for the nest where Satan has hatched his offspring <note>original: "young"</note>.
<margin>Pride, covetousness, envy, wrath, and all falsehood, under a holy appearance of religion.</margin>

26. The Tower of Babel is without foundation; men intend to prop it up, but a wind from the Lord overthrows it.

<margin>Or, Proof.</margin>
27. The hearts and thoughts of men shall be revealed; for there comes a <term>Proba</term> <note>original: "Proba," Latin for a test or trial of quality</note> from the Lord by which the verbal, nominal Christian <note>original: "titular Christian," meaning one who is Christian in name only</note> shall be exposed in his false heart and soul. He will be like a reed that is tossed to and fro by the wind; seeing that his heart is wavering, now this way, now that, his false foundation <note>original: "ground"</note> becomes manifest.

<margin>The Turk <note>Turk: At the time, this term was used for Muslims, specifically the Ottoman Empire; Böhme predicts their eventual conversion</note> shall become a true Christian.</margin>
28. Many shall betray themselves and ruin both body and property through hypocrisy; the hypocrites and nominal Christians shall quail for fear when their false foundation is revealed.

29. The Oriental Beast <note>Oriental Beast: Likely a reference to Eastern powers or the Ottoman Empire, which Böhme suggests will be an instrument in the destruction of the corrupt Western church</note> gains a human heart; and before this happens, he helps to tear down the Tower of Babel with his claws.

<margin>The Emperor of Germany <note>The Holy Roman Emperor</note>.</margin>
30. In the darkness of the North there arises a Sun which takes its light from the sensory properties of the nature of all beings—from the formed, expressed, and re-expressing Word <note>Word: The divine creative power manifest in the physical world</note>. This is a wonder in which all nations rejoice.

31. An Eagle <note>Eagle: The traditional symbol of the Holy Roman Empire</note> has hatched young lions in his nest and brought them prey for so long that they have grown great. He hoped that they would likewise bring their prey back to him again; but they have forgotten that duty. They take the eagle, pluck off his feathers, and bite off his claws for his unfaithfulness, so that he can fetch no more prey, even if he should starve from hunger.

32. But they fall out over the eagle's nest and tear one another in anger, until their anger becomes a fire which burns up the nest; and this is from the Lord of all beings.

...Christian obligation and good affection by explaining those cited <note>original: "alleadged"</note> texts. I have also set down and described the true basis <note>original: "GROUND"</note> of the divine manifestation in such a way that I hope people will see the truth.

3. But if there is a mind divinely inclined and devoted that can give the honor to God, I hope it will be understood and accepted according to my meaning and understanding <note>original: "apprehension"</note>, and not interpreted otherwise, as happened before. I will move past that and instead prefer Christian love, as we are bound in Christ to instruct one another in a friendly way according to our various gifts. In this, we give God the honor and despise no one for his divine gifts; for he who does so *blasphemes the Holy Spirit*, and against such a person, the Scripture pronounces a harsh sentence.

4. Now, although this treatise is somewhat long, do not let the reader consider it tedious or tiresome. I felt it was of little value for me to try to prove and clarify such a writing without a sufficient foundation; therefore, I have placed the cited passages of Scripture upon their innermost foundation <note>original: "ground"</note> and shown how they *originally* arise out of their center, and what their sense and meaning is.

5. For it is not enough that I should gather a great heap of Scripture passages to oppose and contradict those cited; no, no—*this accomplishes nothing before God and the truth. For not the smallest mark or letter of this law shall pass away until all is fulfilled*, says Christ. The sayings of Scripture must remain true and not clash with one another; and though they seem to be contrary and contradict one another, yet this is only the case for those to whom the understanding of them is not given, and who are not gifted or made capable of explaining and interpreting them.

6. But whoever undertakes to interpret them clearly and correctly must have an understanding of the *harmony* <note>original: "Accordance"</note>, so that he may know how to reconcile those places which seem contradictory to human reason. He must not base them upon *conjecture* or opinion—questioning whether it is so or not—if he intends to teach fundamentally and with certainty. For from opinion and conjecture arises only strife and controversy, upon which "Great Babylon" is built—that is <note>original: "Viz."</note>, spiritual pride and "whoredom" <note>Böhme uses "whoredom" here as a biblical metaphor for spiritual infidelity or the corruption of the church</note>. In this state, a person wishes to be an apostle yet is not sent or acknowledged by God; instead, he runs according to opinion and the prompting or instigation of the *cosmic spirit*.
<margin>The Spirit of the World <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi"</note></margin>

7. illuminate him; he will be far from being able to unite the supposed contradictions of the Scripture sayings, and to speak from **ONE** center in such a way that not the least tittle <note>original: "tittle" — a tiny stroke or point in writing; Böhme means even the smallest detail.</note> is diminished in their harmony [or reconciliation].

8. I set this down, not to displease *N.* or anyone else, but only because of the long-continued disagreements of human reason, in which the world runs astray and truth lies veiled. Because of this, men judge the doctrine of the *will of God* and follow their own reasoning without foundation. But where Christ is born within a person, there strife ceases, and God the Father speaks His Word in Christ through the soul of that person. For such conclusions [and reasonings], there must be an inward divine light which provides certainty; otherwise, there is no foundation for human reason.

9. You may obtain this treatise from Mr. *Michael of Ender* <note>original: "Michael of Ender" — Michael von Ender, a nobleman and friend of Böhme who helped circulate his manuscripts.</note>, who has now received it. It contains about 42 sheets in my own handwriting. If you are pleased to share it with *N.*, as your good friend and kinsman, I am content—provided that you tell him he should not understand it as if I had written anything in it out of anger <note>original: "passionately"</note> against him or anyone else. Such passions or emotions do not reside in my soul without urgent and significant cause. Although I am not without my own faults and shortcomings, my Savior Christ has shown me such grace that all insults <note>original: "invectives"</note> and opposing objections against me fall away. They are rejected like a weed (when I perceive a divine earnestness through a single word proceeding from divine love towards me) which I would not willingly plant in my garden; for from such a thing, nothing but a harmful <note>original: "naughty" — in the 17th century, this meant wicked, worthless, or harmful rather than just mischievous.</note> weed grows again.

10. Furthermore, it is again requested of *N.*, out of Christian love, that since I have explained his cited passages of Scripture according to my limited talents (which are known to God), he would be pleased—if my explanation displeases him and is not, in his opinion, sufficiently grounded and fundamental—to do me the favor of explaining the cited texts himself. I specifically mean the 9th and 10th chapters of St. Paul's Epistle to the Romans, even those very Scriptures which I have explained. Let him explain the whole foundation of the divine will regarding good and evil; how its origin is within man or outside of man; and let him unfold and declare them in an intelligible <note>original: "sensall" — understandable to the senses or intellect.</note> manner.

11. And then I desire that he would declare and explain to me the inspired word of grace regarding the "seed of the woman" in Paradise <note>Böhme refers to Genesis 3:15, the first biblical promise of a redeemer.</note>, and then the two paths: namely, the kingdom of corrupt human nature and the kingdom of grace in the inward-spoken voice of grace.

12. Or, if my explanation regarding *Abraham*, *Ishmael*, and *Isaac*, and also *Jacob* and *Esau*, did not please him, let him, out of Christian love, [explain them himself].

### The Twenty-First Epistle

[He] should show his gifts and explain the basis of them, so that I might find his gifts and understanding in those places. Then, if I can see that God has gifted *him* with a larger measure of understanding in these high mysteries than me, I will accept it with great gladness. I will love him for his gifts and give thanks to our God for them. I will rejoice with *him*, as a fellow member of Christ, in our shared gifts in the spirit of Christ. All of this would lead more to the profit and benefit of our brothers and fellow Christian members; it would be more godly, commendable, and praiseworthy than a baseless contradiction born out of emotions for the sake of man's willful ego.

13. But I pray to my God in Christ that He would be pleased to open his heart, so that his soul may see into the basis of my gifts. Truly, I am a simple man <note>original: "simple man" — Böhme often emphasizes his lack of formal university education to highlight that his knowledge is divinely inspired.</note>; I never studied or learned this high mystery, nor did I seek after it in such a way or know anything of it. I sought only the heart of love in Christ Jesus. But when I had obtained that, with the exceeding great joy of my soul, then this *treasure* of divine and natural knowledge was opened and given to me. I have not boasted of this until now, but I have heartily desired and begged of God to know whether the time had yet come for this knowledge to be revealed in the hearts of many. Regarding this, I obtained a powerful answer, so that I know very well what I have hinted at and mentioned [in my writings].

14. And although I am therefore hated by many in the world, men will shortly see why God has opened and revealed the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "grand Mystery" — likely referring to the *Mysterium Magnum*, the subject of one of Böhme's major works regarding the origin of the manifestation of all things.</note>—namely, the foundation of all secrets and mysteries—to a common, humble, [and lowly] man. Yet I may not reveal all that is made known to me; nevertheless, it might be shared with worthy people if I found it to be God's will and profitable to men. For instance, a while ago a very precious *pearl* <note>original: "Pearl" — a common metaphor in Böhme's work for the "Spirit of Christ" or a specific divine revelation.</note> was revealed to me, which has its own time for practical use and benefit; but it is always a very profitable benefit in my soul. Do not wonder or marvel so much at the simplicity of what God does, for the time of the proud has come to an end.

15. Further, I desire and entreat Mr. *N.* to deal Christianly and candidly, in love, with his gifts, and not to taunt and slander my name as he did before (which causes the gifts of the Holy Spirit to be spoken of as evil). If he does so, he shall be answered with similar modesty, mildness, and respect. But if it should turn out contrary to my good intentions and hope—that I am further slandered by people or in writings—let him know (if I either see or hear of it with certain proof) that he shall not lack a substantial answer in a *divine gift*, and he shall gain no advantage or praise from it.

16. I mean this sincerely, and I exhort him out of Christian love and obligation to answer. If he will not declare and explain...

# The Twenty-First Epistle

[...let him explain] those places in a sensible, extensive answer; then let him reconcile the contradictions which seem to be set against one another. In this way, we shall mutually exchange our gifts and bring them into one common ground, for the love and benefit of our brothers.

17. And I commend you and your family, and all those who seek and desire the child *Jesus*, into the effective, working love of *Jesus Christ*. It is my desire that He may be conceived, become incarnate, and be born in everyone; then strife and conflict will come to an end. When the "seed of the woman" <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted here as the divine spirit or "New Man" overcoming the "serpent" of the fallen human nature.</note> breaks the head of the serpent, we return again into the <term>Temperature</term>; and we are only one in Christ, like a single tree with many boughs and branches.

# THE TWENTY-SECOND EPISTLE

<margin>1.</margin>
<image-desc>Ornate woodcut decorative initial 'M' featuring floral and vine motifs.</image-desc>
MUCH respected Sir and dear Doctor, please give Mr. *N.* my letter to read, but do not give him this specific note. Encourage him toward Christian humility to see if perhaps the eyes of his soul might be opened—something I heartily and freely wish for him. It will be no disgrace to him to love and embrace the **truth**. I perceive very clearly what stands in his way and holds him back: it is nothing other than **self-love**. Because he has until now openly presented and publicized his own foundations so extensively and gained great reputation and respect among many people, my foundational principles do not entirely agree with his. Therefore, **self-love** drives him to oppose me, even though he has not yet grasped my foundation and is still like an infant regarding it.

2. But if the honor of God and brotherly <note>original: "memberlike"</note> love take hold of his heart, he truly has nothing against me or my writings. Indeed, they might even better him and help him grow as a Christian. However, without a willing and loving heart <note>original: "affectionate will"</note>, he will remain blind to them; for no human reason can understand this foundation without the eternal love of God, in which all the treasures of wisdom are hidden <note>original: "couched"</note>.

3. Please send me word back in a letter regarding what his opinion is; his inner motivations <note>original: "hidden-ground"</note> are revealed here. I hope that he will also come to see, since he otherwise has a sharp intellect <note>original: "reason"</note> and has well studied **logic**. Perhaps he will investigate further, but if he chooses not to, his opinion does not cancel out <note>original: "abrogate"</note> the gifts of God. He cannot overthrow my foundation—especially my explanation of those biblical texts—using any **scripture**. I mean him well <note>original: "I meane sincerely towards him"</note>.

4. Furthermore, I would ask you to do me the favor of sending the ***Treatise of Election*** <note>Likely referring to Böhme’s *Von der Gnadenwahl* (On the Election of Grace), written in 1623, which addresses the controversial topic of predestination.</note> to Mr. *N.* for him to read. He is a courteous gentleman, and the debate <note>original: "Disputation"</note> over this topic <note>original: "Article"</note> turned out such that it should not be viewed as if a man were left completely in the dark <note>original: "struck dead in ignorance"</note>.

# The Twenty-Second Epistle

5. But if necessary, I shall explain myself so clearly that they will see the foundation from which I write. Let them give me whatever *questions* they please—whether they concern nature or things beyond nature, time or eternity—I will not be found lacking by Divine Grace, but will give a sufficient answer. This is provided that it is done in a Christian manner, and not out of emotional bias, passion, hair-splitting <note>original: "cavilling"</note>, or insults; I shall deal with them in the same respectful way.

6. In our recent meeting, I was poorly prepared for such a debate, for *wine and rich food hide the foundation of the Pearl* <note>original: "Pearl's ground"; Böhme’s term for the inner divine spark or spiritual essence which is clouded by physical indulgence</note>, especially because I am not used to such things; at home, I live very simply and temperately. Furthermore, Mr. *N.* was not sufficiently answered; but I offer to answer him, *and all others* who have sincere Christian intentions. Let them only give me their questions in writing and explain their own opinions on the matter so that I may see what they conclude. I will give them a fundamental, detailed, and explanatory answer. I will not defend or protect myself using any sect or sectarian name <note>original: "Patronize my selfe therewith"</note> in the foundation of truth; I am not a *Flaccinian* <note>original: "Flaccinian"; a follower of Matthias Flacius, a theologian who argued that original sin became the very substance of human nature. Böhme rejects this sectarian label.</note> as *N.* supposes, but I shall stand upon the true foundation.

7. For I teach no *independent human ability* <note>original: "Selfe ability"</note> *without Christ* to attain the status of God's children <note>original: "the Adoption"</note>, as *N.* thinks; however, I am not satisfied with his opinion, and much less with that of Mr. *N. N.*, which completely contradicts the *Scripture*. For I am dead to all personal opinions and have nothing except what is given to me by God to know. I leave all of you to judge how I know what I know; as a layman, uneducated <note>original: "Illiterate"</note>, and untrained man, I have to deal with you who are educated in the universities <note>original: "high Schooles"</note> and must set myself against *academic learning* <note>original: "Learned Art"</note>. In my own reason, I do not know how to achieve this without God's knowledge, but I look upon what God does. Yet, in the foundation of my gifts, I know well enough what I am doing in this purpose and intention; and yet it is not my own intention, but rather the current time brings it forth, and *HE* who rules all things drives and orders it.

8. Concerning our secret discussion (as you know), you must still be patient and continue in that known process for a good while; in this beginning, no other way will be allowed. It may well be accomplished in the seventh year of this process; for it must be opened through all the six <term>properties of the spiritual foundation</term> <note>In Böhme’s complex cosmology, there are seven "forms" or properties of nature that lead from darkness to light.</note>. Although it is already opened through the *Sun*, the "Key" has scarcely reached the first or second degree of the center of nature. For each property among the six forms of spiritual life has its own unique *Sun* within it, derived from the strength, influence, and origin of the light of nature—that is, from the *Essential Sun* <note>The spiritual source of all light and life</note>—and these must be opened in order, according to how they are born and originated.

# The Twenty-Second Epistle

*Jupiter’s Sun* is opened, and then the powers are discerned like a blossoming tree, and you have come this far.

10. Thirdly, *Mars*—namely <note>original: "Viz."</note>, the fire-soul—is opened. Then *Virgin Venus* appears in her white robes and plays with the soul to see if she might move it toward the desire of Love. She goes in and out, up and down with the soul, and lovingly embraces <note>original: "accolates"; to greet or embrace</note> it. She does this to see whether she might bring the fleeing properties of self-will (where the soul departed from its balanced state <note>original: "temperature"</note> into the unstable life of the body's divided properties) back into herself again. This is so that *Virgin Venus* might be animated [or given a soul] once more and regain the *Fire's Essence* <note>original: "Tincture"; the spiritual life-force or transformative power</note>, which is where her joy and life consist.

11. For *Virgin Venus* is the brightness of the white in the *Sun*, as understood in this context. However, the stability of that shining is not her own; the spiritual water is her own unique property. This water arises out of the fire where the separation begins in the *Saltpeter* <note>original: "Salniter"; a term used by Böhme to describe a potent, explosive spiritual essence</note> within *Mars's Sun*. Then *Virgin Venus* separates within herself and covers herself with a *Copper Garment* <note>Copper is the metal traditionally associated with the planet Venus</note>. *Mars* would like to possess her for himself, but he defiles her exceedingly in his malice, spattering her with earth and rust. He cannot have her as his spouse unless he gives her his own fire-will as her possession—and that he will not do. Therefore, they struggle for a long time; they are married, but they are unfaithful to each other.

12. And even then the *Sun* comes and opens the *Sun of Mercury*, which is the fourth Key. There you shall see great wonders: how God has created the Heaven and the Earth, and also the foundation of the four Elements. If you then observe rightly, you shall see your own proper *Guiding Spirit* <note>original: "Genius"</note> unfolded before you. You will see how the *Word has become Man*—namely, the expressed Word speaking itself forth into the separation of powers. You will see how *Virgin Venus* is separated and how the forms of nature take her into themselves and treat her pitifully. They take her into their own dominance and change themselves within her into a purple color. They would like to murder, but in this place, she is *their baptism to the new life*.

<margin>* Otherwise, God <note>original: "Aliter, God"</note>.</margin>
13. The fifth Key is *Virgin Venus* herself, with which she opens her *Gold*—namely, the Sun—so that she gives her will and fair garland to the "murderers." Because of this, she stands as one humbled <note>original: "impregnate [or humbled]"</note>. At this point, the Practitioner <note>original: "Artist"; the person undergoing the spiritual-alchemical process</note> assumes he has the "new child," but he is far enough from it until its actual *birth*.

14. The sixth Key is *Luna* [the Moon]. When the *Sun* opens this, then *Mars, Jupiter*, and *Saturne* must all forsake their own will and let their fleeing, aspiring pride <note>original: "Pompe"</note> fall; for the *Sun* in *Luna* takes them into the *Incarnation* <note>The process of the spirit taking on form or "flesh"</note>. Then the Practitioner begins to be sad, and thinks...

Through this, *Mars* in *Jupiter* and *Saturne* is made alive <note>original: "quick"</note> in this love of a joyful life, and all the six properties give their will over to *Venus*; and she gives her will to the Sun, and then the life is born that stands in the *Balanced State* <note>original: "Temperature"; the perfect harmony of all elemental and spiritual properties</note>.

15. Dear Mr. *Doctor*, the pen is not to be trusted <note>meaning: written words are risky or insufficient to convey these secrets</note>, yet take care with the work. It will be so and no other way; do not change <note>original: "move"</note> it, lest *Mercury* be enraged before his opening. This is done so that she may become holy and spiritual; then the Sun shines in her, which changes nature into love.

16. Loving Mr. Doctor, the *Philosophical Body* is the spiritual water from the fire and light; namely <note>original: "Viz."</note>, the power of the fire and of the light. When it is severed from its coarseness through the opening of all the properties of nature, then it is truly spiritual. Then the *Solar spirit* receives no other property into itself except that which is able to reach its sensory Sun in the opened state. For the Sun takes nothing into itself except its own likeness; it takes its Heaven out of the earth (if you will understand me correctly), for that is its food, from which it generates a young Sun in itself, which is also called *Sol*. But it is a body; therefore, I say to you, keep to it diligently and precisely. You shall rejoice greatly if God lets you live long enough, provided you have the right Father, for whom I have searched and with whom I am greatly in love.

17. This is well known to me, for I have lately seen it, which makes me not only wonder but rejoice. Much is revealed to me in this; and although I might write more extensively, it is not necessary for this process. Also, the pen is not to be trusted; it may be done another time. I pray you to keep this letter secret and in faithfulness; if I come to you, I may entrust you with something more.

# THE THREE AND TWENTIETH EPISTLE.

### TO CHRISTIANUS STEENBERGER, DOCTOR OF MEDICINE <note>original: "Physick"</note>.

->*Our salvation is in the life of Jesus Christ in us.*<-

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'W' featuring floral and cloud-like motifs.</image-desc>

1. Worthy, learned, and dear Christian friend; sending all heartfelt wishes for Divine Love and Grace: I desire that the fountain of Divine love might be opened to you through the Sun of Life, from which the Divine water flows. I do not doubt that the Bridegroom <note>Christ</note> has called his Bride—namely <note>original: "Viz."</note>, your soul—to this wellspring, since I understand that God has placed you under the Cross and tribulation <note>meaning suffering or trials</note>.

2. This is the first mark and sign of the noble *Sophia* <note>Divine Wisdom, personified as a feminine figure in Böhme’s theology</note> with which she marks her children. For she usually manifests herself through the thorns of God’s anger, like a beautiful rose on a thorny bush; this happens as long as the soul keeps its vow and faithfulness, for there must be a faithful and firm bond and covenant between the soul and this burning fire of God’s love.

3. A person must set such a purpose for themselves: that they will enter into Christ's bitter passion <note>suffering</note> and death, and die there daily to their sins and evil vanities <note>meaning worthless or worldly pursuits</note>, and pray earnestly to God for the renewal of their mind and understanding. 4. This Mystery is understood <note>original: "comprehended"</note> through faith, where the divinity and humanity are then joined according to that same internal ground, in the same way that fire heats through an iron; and yet the iron retains its own substance, but as long as the fire burns within it, it is changed into pure fire.

5. It is not that the creature <note>the human being</note> grasps it by its own power, but rather it is grasped when the will completely resigns itself to God. The spirit of God rules in this resigned will, and the will is the true temple of the Holy Spirit, where Christ dwells *essentially* <note>meaning in actual substance, not just as a symbol</note>. This is not in an imaginary, thought-like, or creaturely way, but as fire is in the iron, or as the sun is in a plant <note>original: "hearb"</note>, where the influential power of the sun forms itself and becomes substantial within the <term>tincture</term> <note>the essential inner quality or life-force</note> of the plant.

6. This is also how it should be understood in the human spirit: when the holy power of God forms and images itself in man's spirit and faith, it becomes a spiritual being [or essence]. Only the soul's "mouth of faith" lays hold of this, not the earthly man of flesh and blood, who is mortal. It is an immortal being, in which *Christ* dwells in man; it is the heaven of God stamped upon the "little world" <note>the microcosm, or individual human being</note>, and it is a revelation of the throne <note>original: "place [Throne or seat]"</note> of God where paradise springs forth again and bears fruit.

7. Therefore the *Dragon* <note>symbolizing the devil or the egoistic fallen nature</note> must first be slain; and although he still clings to the earthly flesh like the rind and bark on a tree, the spirit lives in God. As Saint Paul says, "*Our citizenship <note>original: "conversation"; from the Latin 'conversatio' meaning conduct or citizenship</note> is in heaven*." And as Christ also said: "*He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him; also, without me you can do nothing.*"

8. Therefore I say, if anyone is a true Christian, he is so in *Christ*. He is begotten and born into the life and spirit of Christ and puts on the resurrection of Christ. In this way, the satisfaction <note>the atonement or debt-payment</note> of Christ is shared with him. Thus Christ also overcomes sin, death, the Devil, and hell within him; and so he is reconciled and united with God in Christ.

9. For the new birth is not a grace "imputed" from the outside—where we would only need to comfort ourselves with Christ's merits while continuing in the hypocrisy of sin. No, it is a childlike, innate grace: God has placed Christ, along with justification, upon the convert, so that Christ also redeems him within himself by the power of his resurrection from God’s anger. Otherwise, he is no Christian, no matter how much he may flatter others or make devout, hypocritical displays.

<summary>Jacob Böhme explains that true Christianity is an internal, substantial transformation where Christ dwells within the believer like fire in iron, rather than a mere external or intellectual belief. He emphasizes the "new birth" as an actual spiritual essence that overcomes the fallen nature (the Dragon) and unites the soul with God.</summary>

### The Twenty-Third Epistle

10. Regarding the interpretation of some words (and also what you requested of me) that are specified in my book called *Aurora* (which contain very hidden meanings, the knowledge of which was given to me by the Most High); I want you to understand that at present it is not convenient to write about this extensively and explicitly in letters, seeing as the times are dangerous and the Enemy of Christ is horribly raging and raving. Until a little time has passed, I will give you a short hint for you to consider further.

11. First, there is a twofold meaning of the *Northern Crown* <note>original: "Northern Crowne"</note>. The first points to the *Crown of Life*: namely <note>original: "Viz."</note> the Spirit of Christ, which shall be manifested in the midst of the great darkness—that is, in the contrition [or distress] of the conscious nature of the conscience, where a specific motion is present. Then comes the Bridegroom: namely, the power of Christ in the midst of such a motion.

12. The other meaning is a figure of the *outer kingdoms*, where there will be great confusion, entanglements, and contentions when the nations are in conflict. There also is the figure, namely the *Victory*, hinted at as it stands in the spiritual figure: how things will go, *and which people shall conquer at last*, and how during that lamentable time of tribulation *Christ shall be made manifest and known*. After and during that miserable time, *the great mysteries shall be revealed*, so that people shall be able to know the hidden God in the Trinity even through *Nature*. Through this knowledge, the *foreign nations shall be converted and become Christians*. Within this is signified how the sectarian contentions in religion shall be destroyed by such a manifestation, for all gates will be thrown open. Then all the unprofitable talkers <note>original: "Praters"</note>, who at present lie like so many bars before the *Truth*, will be removed. All shall acknowledge and know *Christ*. This manifestation shall be the last; then the Sun of Life shall shine upon all nations. At that very time, the *Beast* of iniquity together with the *Whore* shall *end their days*, which is signified by the characters *Ra. Ra. Ra. P. in R. P.* <note>These are Böhme's cryptic symbolic characters referencing the Book of Revelation</note> as can be seen in the Revelation.

13. We do not dare to make this extensive interpretation any clearer at present; all will reveal itself in time. Then people will see what it was, for there is still a completely different time to come.

14. Concerning the *language of nature*, I assure you that it is a reality; but what I understand of it, I cannot teach or give to another. Indeed, I can give a description of it and how it is to be understood, but it requires much space, and there would have to be a personal meeting and conversation about it. It is not something to be set down in writing.

15. Also, regarding the philosophical work of the *Tincture* <term>the essential life-force or spiritual alchemy sought by Böhme</term>, its progress is not to be described so bluntly or plainly. Although I do not possess it in practice <note>original: "Praxis"</note>, the Seal of God lies before it to conceal...

He also addresses the "language of nature" and the spiritual alchemy of the "Tincture," noting that some truths remain concealed or require personal instruction.</summary>

the true foundation of it, upon pain of eternal punishment, unless a man knew for certain that it might not be misused. It is not made of earth, stones, or metals, and yet it is of the ground <note>original: "Ground"; meaning the underlying foundation or essence</note> of all metals. Moreover, it is clear: the work is easy and the art is simple; a boy of ten years might perform it. But the wisdom within it is great, and the greatest mystery. Everyone must seek it for themselves; it is not for us to break the seal of God, for a fiery mountain lies before it, at which I myself am amazed and must wait to see if it is God's will. How should I teach others explicitly about it? I cannot yet make it myself, although I know something of it. Let no man seek more from me than I have already clearly enough indicated; and I commend you, along with all the children of God, into the love of *Jesus Christ*.

# THE TWENTY-FOURTH EPISTLE.

### In Answer to a QUESTION: Why the Statue of one who was Deceased Wept, or Shed Tears?

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'T' featuring floral and vine motifs within a square border.</image-desc>

1. Regarding the question, it is obscure to the *understanding*, and it requires a Joseph <note>A reference to the biblical Joseph, who interpreted dreams and mysteries (Genesis 40–41)</note> to explain it; for it is a magical <note>original: "Magicall"</note> thing and very wonderful. Therefore, it is difficult to answer, because it proceeds from Magic <note>original: "Magia"; in Böhme’s philosophy, this refers to the creative, spiritual power of the will that underlies all reality</note>.

2. Yet I will explain and show you very briefly what my opinion is on the matter. I do not mean to conclude or pass an absolute, final judgment concerning it, but rather to leave it to you and other *enlightened men of God* to reach your own opinion and understanding. As to whether God has enabled me to resolve <margin>* Or, resolve it.</margin> it, I leave that to your judgment, as you know the condition of the person mentioned better than I do; for all things proceed according to the time, measure, and limit of that thing.

<margin>† Or, a stone statue crafted by a stonemason, or an image set up as a monument.</margin>
3. A hard, rough stone statue † has no life that is mobile or active, for the elemental vegetable life <note>Böhme uses "vegetable life" to describe the basic growth-force and vitality found even in minerals and plants</note> remains mute and still within it. It is locked within its first impression <note>The initial state of compression or formation of the material</note>; yet, it is not as if it were a *nothing*. There is nothing in this world in which both the elemental and the sidereal dominion <note>original: "Sydereall Dominion"; the governing influence of the stars and heavenly bodies over the physical world</note> do not reside. However, it is more mobile, active, and working in one thing than in another; and we cannot say that the four elements, along with the stars, do not have their *daily influence* in all things.

4. Because this is a *hard stone*, the *miracle* is beyond the usual and ordinary course of nature. Therefore, we can in no way say that it has a natural cause within the stone, as if the physical operation of the stone itself should move and produce this effect. Rather, it is a *magical motion from the spirit*, whose image is carved and portrayed in the stone.

5. For a stone consists of three things, and indeed all beings consist of these three things, though they are enclosed in a twofold property: namely, in a spiritual property and in a physical <note>original: "corporall"</note> property. Those three things, of which everything in this world consists, are *Sulphur, Mercury*, and *Salt* <note>In Böhme's thought, these are the "Three Principles" or fundamental forces of all reality, both material and spiritual</note>, existing in two properties: one heavenly and the other earthly. It is just as God dwells in Time, and Time in God, and yet Time is not God, but is produced out of God as a portrayed image of eternity.

6. So a human being likewise is made from time and also from eternity, and consists of three things—namely, *Sulphur, Mercury*, and *Salt*—in two parts. One part is out of time—that is, the outward body—and the other part stands in eternity—that is, the soul. Seeing then that man, time, and eternity all stand within one dominion in a person, we must consider the *question* from this perspective.

<margin>* The little world from the great world <note>original: Microcosmus ex Macrocosmo</note>.</margin>

7. For man is a *little world* <term>microcosm</term> made out of the *great world* <term>macrocosm</term>, and has the properties of the whole great world within him. For God said to him after the Fall: *you are earth, and to earth you shall return*. That is, you are *Sulphur, Mercury*, and *Salt*. In these three elements stand all things in this world, whether they are spiritual or physical—except for the soul, which stands in a property according to the rights of the eternal nature, as I have sufficiently demonstrated in my writings.

8. Now when a person dies, the outward light in the outward *Sulphur* is extinguished and goes out along with its outward fire, in which the life has burned. Then the body falls to dust and enters again into that from which it came. But the soul, which is brought forth out of the eternal nature and infused into Adam by the spirit of God, cannot die; for it is not made of time, but is of the eternal generation.

<margin>† Or, set its mind upon.</margin>

9. Now if the soul has † set its heart on <note>original: "put its desire into"</note> any temporary <note>original: "temporall"</note> thing, and has imprinted itself upon it—or strongly focused its imagination upon it—then it has impressed the property of that thing into its desire. It holds onto it magically, as if it possessed it physically. 

Indeed, it cannot hold the physical body—meaning the elemental body—but it holds the starry body <note>original: "sydereall body"</note> until the stars also consume it. It often happens that people appear after their death in houses with their own bodies, but the body is cold, dead, and numb. The spirit of the soul only puts it on through the astral spirit for a time, until the body putrefies.

10. Also

### The twenty-fourth Epistle.

10. Also, many a person is so strongly possessed by the <term>Astral</term> <note>original: "Astrall [or starry]"; Böhme refers to the "spirit of the stars," a semi-material layer of the human being that mediates between the eternal soul and the physical body</note> Spirit, through the *Desire* of the soul, that it is a long while in decaying. For the desire of the soul brings the sidereal spirit into it, so that the elements are, as it were, impressed with an astral life. This is especially true if the soul has not yet attained rest, and if during the life of the body it had strongly imagined something (and taken it to heart), and in the meantime the body died before it had released its desire or removed it from that thing. Therefore, the will still continually runs in that same impression, and it would gladly fulfill its purpose, but cannot. Thereupon, it seeks the cause or reason for its detainment and would gladly rest in *Eternity*; but the impressed thing has its effective working and driving until the stars consume it. Formerly, in the *Catholic Religion* <note>original: "Popish Religion"</note>, there was something handled concerning this, but without sufficient understanding.

<margin>* Or, shed tears.</margin>
11. Now you may easily consider how it happened that the *engraved gravestone* \* shed water or wept. It is not done by the power or virtue of the stone, but by the strength and might of the *spirit* to whom the stone belongs, and whose *image* it bears. Also, it is not done from the soul's own essence, but magically through the astral *spirit*. The *constellations in the spirit of the soul* have impressed themselves into the sidereal spirit in the stone, all according to the soul's desire. By this, it has signified that there was something that lay heavy on its mind when it lived; and this sadness [or sore pensiveness of spirit] was still in the sidereal spirit. For *Christ said, "Where your heart is, there is also your treasure"* <note>Matthew 6:21</note>; also, in the Revelation of Jesus Christ it is written, *"our works shall follow us."* <note>Revelation 14:13</note>

12. Dear Sir, it is not appropriate for me to judge further in this matter. Consider whether the mentioned person had something in her that lay heavy upon her before her end: whether anyone had done her wrong, or she had done wrong to anyone, or whether the care for her husband and children (insofar as she was a holy person) troubled her, seeing any of them going on in an evil course. Thus, through the power of the sidereal spirit, through the stone, she might give such a warning <note>original: "admonition"</note> for amendment. Noble Sir, consider yourself rightly; I may likely hit upon the truth among all these mentioned things. But since I never knew the person, and also know nothing of her, I leave the judgment to your *favor*; you know better than I what her condition was in this regard. I write only of the *possibility* of how it may be, and pass no further judgment or determination.

13. But if this should be laughed at and accounted ridiculous, I do not care; I am not deceived. I understand (I bless God) this foundation <note>original: "ground"</note> very well; for such knowledge I have not learned

2. Because he stood upon that same root, he became capable of experiencing the same.

# The twenty-fifth Epistle.

and has awakened and opened in him the Gate of the first Principle (being the severe, earnest Source) <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, the "First Principle" represents the dark, foundational, and often wrathful fire of existence, which must be transformed by light.</note> which however burns in the great created World, and is wholly ignited <note>original: "enkindled"</note> in the damned.

12. But the right man, whom God created—who alone is the true right man—is yet hidden in this *Corrupt* man. If *he denies himself in his beast-like <note>original: "beastiall"; referring to the animalistic or fallen nature of humanity</note> form, and does not live according to the acting, driving, and will of the same, but surrenders himself to God with his whole mind, thoughts, and senses; then this man lives in God, and God works in him the will and the deed, for all is in God.*

13. The truly holy and heavenly man, who is hidden in the monstrous <note>original: "monstrous"; here meaning distorted or unnatural in comparison to the original divine image</note> man, is as much in Heaven as God is; and Heaven is in him, and the heart, or light of God is begotten and born in him; that is, God in him, and he in God. God is nearer to him than the *beast-like* body.

14. The beast-like body is not his own native country where he is at home; instead, he is with it *outside of Paradise*. But the right man, reborn <note>original: "regenerate"</note> and born anew in Christ, is not in this world, but in the *Paradise of God*; and although he is in the body, yet he is in God.

15. And though the beast-like body dies, yet nothing is done to the new man, except that he then comes forth right out of the contrary will and house of torment into his native country. There is no need for any far removal or distance of place to which he thinks he must go for things to be better with him; for God is manifest in him.

16. The soul of man is out of the first Principle of God, but in that state, it is *no holy Being*. But in the Second Principle <note>The "Second Principle" is the realm of Light, Love, and the Kingdom of Heaven.</note> it is manifest in God, and *is a Divine Creature*; for even there the Divine light is born. Therefore, if the Divine light is not born <insert>begotten or brought forth in it</insert> [<gloss>namely, the Soul</gloss>] then God is not in it, but it lives in the most original, earnest Source, where there is an eternal contrariety <insert>enmity, or contrary will</insert> within itself.

17. But if the light be born, then there is joy, love, and pleasant delight in the Creature, and the new Man, which is the Soul, is in God. How should there not be *knowledge* where God is in the creature?

18. Now it does not depend on the willing, running, and toiling of the creature to know the depths of the deity; for the soul does not know the divine Center, or how the divine essence is generated; but it depends on God’s will, how he will manifest it.

19. Now then, if God does manifest himself in the soul; what—

<summary>Böhme describes the dual nature of man: a "beast-like" physical body existing outside Paradise and a "new man" hidden within who lives in God. He explains that spiritual life and knowledge occur when the soul moves from the dark "first Principle" of existence into the divine light of the "second Principle."</summary>

# The twenty-fifth Epistle.

...has the soul done toward it? Nothing? It has only the longing or laboring <note>original: "travelling"; here meaning the labor and pains of childbirth</note> toward the birth, and looks to God, in whom it lives; from whom the divine light becomes apparent and shines within it: and the first fierce [earnest] Principle <note>In Böhme’s system, the "First Principle" is the dark, consuming fire or "sourness" of existence that must be transformed into light.</note>, from which movement originally arises, is changed into triumphing joy.

20. Therefore, it is a very unjust thing that the world so rages and raves—so tyrannizes, reproaches, condemns, and reviles—when the gifts of God show themselves differently in men, and all do *not have one and the same knowledge.*

21. What can a man take for himself if it is not born in him? This, nonetheless, does not stand in a man's choice, as he desires or prefers it, but as his "Heaven" is within him, so likewise is God manifest in him.

22. For God is not a God of destruction in the birth [or universal generation], but an illuminator, an igniter <note>original: "enkindler"</note>, and a nourisher; and each creature has its own center within itself, *whether it lives in the holiness of God or in the anger of God; God will, however, be manifest in all creatures.*

23. If the world were not so blind, it might know the wonderful being of God in all creatures. But now that it rages and raves so much, it does so entirely against itself and against the *Holy Spirit* of God, at whose light they shall one day be astonished. They shall not hinder the Son which the laboring <note>original: "travelling"</note> Mother brings forth in her old age, for this the Heaven declares.

24. God shall enlighten him against all the raging and raving of the Devil; and his light [splendor or glory] shall reach from the *East* to the *West*; I write *not of myself, but I only foretell that this is at hand and shall come to pass.*

25. I would gladly have pleased you at present with what I promised, wherein all that is here touched upon and hinted at might be clearly explained, and also what that good and well-known *Doctor has desired regarding the origin, being, life, and purpose <note>original: "drift"</note> of man and of his soul, and also his final end; however, it is not yet finished.

26. For the gifts which were once given to me by God are not therefore quite dead and gone; although they were hidden by the Devil and the world, yet now they often appear and show themselves deeper and more wonderful.

27. And very shortly (God willing) you shall receive something of them; for there is a higher beginning made toward it, especially concerning the *THREE PRINCIPLES* <note>Böhme’s primary cosmological framework: the First Principle (dark fire/will), the Second Principle (light/love), and the Third Principle (the visible, material world).</note> of the Divine...

# THE TWENTY-SIXTH EPISTLE

### TO

<margin>* Carel von Endern.</margin>
# *CHARLES OF ENDERN.

<margin>1.</margin>
<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'T' featuring two figures, possibly angels or cherubs, flanking the letter amidst foliage.</image-desc>
MAY THE Love in the heart of God the Father, and the light of his power in the life of Jesus Christ, be our refreshment. May it help us toward the new birth, so that the true Image may appear for God's honor and his deeds of wonder, and cause the fair sprout of *his Lily* <note>The "Lily" is a recurring symbol in Böhme’s work, representing spiritual purity, the growth of the soul, and the upcoming age of the Holy Spirit.</note> to grow *in us* in the Paradisiacal Garden of Jesus Christ.

2. Noble, Right Honorable Sir, I offer my humble and most willing service, with hearty wishes for all temporal and eternal prosperity. I have received from your servant <note>original: "your Man"</note> a *measure of grain* <note>original: "a measure of Corne"; in Böhme’s time, "corn" referred to any cereal grain, such as wheat or rye.</note> which you sent to me, and I thank you most kindly. I pray that Almighty God blesses you in abundance for it.

3. Since, Noble Sir, you are so *humble* and do not look upon or regard what the world does—and because you also do not value the subtlety [or clever pride] of the high-ranking—you instead seek and labor after that which the Lord of Heaven builds. Although it appears as foolishness to this world, it seems good in his sight to carry out his work through humble, low, plain, and *childlike people*, so that he alone might be exalted and no man might have cause to boast. You likewise may surely hope for the same knowledge, which is more beautiful and excellent than all the pomp and riches of the world. For everything that is temporal leaves and forsakes a person, but the honorable garland [or trophy] of Christ does not forsake a person at death; instead, it brings him to the heavenly, triumphant host of angels, into his true eternal native country [or home].

4. Now, seeing as we know and understand exceedingly well that we are only pilgrims in this world, staying in a strange lodging in very great danger,

<summary>Jacob Böhme writes to Charles of Endern, thanking him for a gift of grain and praising his humility in seeking spiritual truth rather than worldly status. He frames the human experience as a dangerous pilgrimage toward an eternal home.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Böhme, Charles of Endern, the Lily, new birth, humility, pilgrims, spiritual knowledge</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the twenty-sixth epistle to Charles of Endern. Böhme continues to contrast worldly wisdom and status with the spiritual pursuit of the "eternal native country" and the personified "Virgin of Wisdom."</meta>

danger, lying captive in a foul <note>original: "fore"; likely a transcription error for "foul" or "sore," meaning miserable.</note> and hard prison, and must continually fear and expect death. Therefore, Noble Sir, you do very well and act more wisely than the prudent of the world, in that you look about you and endeavor after your *eternal native country*, and not after the pomp, power, and riches of this world, as the high and great ones generally do.

5. I have no doubt that you shall obtain a very fair garland from the *Virgin* of the eternal wisdom of God. If this comes to pass, it will be of more value and acceptance to you than all temporal riches and this whole world with all its being and splendor. <gloss>Crown or trophy of Sophia <note>Sophia is the Greek word for "Wisdom," often personified in Böhme's theology as a divine feminine bridge between God and the soul.</note></gloss> If I had no actual <note>original: "effectuall"</note> knowledge of this, I would not write. For from the "wise" of this world (who, solely out of self-pride and without God's Spirit, arrogate and attribute all knowledge and understanding to themselves), I receive not only poor thanks, but also nothing but derision and scorn. In this I rejoice, all the more because I bear reproach for the sake of the *name* and knowledge of *God*.

6. For if my knowledge had been gained in *their school*, then they would embrace and love their own; but because it is from another *school*, they do not know it. Moreover, they despise it, as they have done to all the prophets, *Christ*, and his *apostles*. This shall not trouble or turn me aside; but as I have begun, I will depend on my God and Creator with the greater earnestness and fixed resolution. I will commit myself to him; let him do with me what he pleases.

7. I attribute no wisdom to myself; moreover, I do not rely upon any purpose or intention of reason. For I see most plainly, and find it as clear as the sun, that God goes about his work in a completely different way.

8. Therefore, if we act in a childlike manner and not according to our reason (but only depend on him with true desire and right earnestness, putting all our confidence in him), then we obtain the noble Virgin of his wisdom sooner than through our sharp inventions and acute reasonings. For when she comes, she brings true wisdom and heavenly understanding along with her, and without her, I know nothing.

9. But since you have a great delight in reading such writings concerning the Highest Being (and as I hope it is by God's providence), I will not withhold from you what the *Chief Good <note>original: "cheifest good"; Böhme's term for the ultimate divine reality.</note> has entrusted to me*. Soon I will send you something *that is more complete*; for a very wonderful and excellent book has been begun concerning the *Life of Man*. If it pleases the Lord to continue to guide my hand, it shall clearly reveal what man is and what he must do to obtain the Chief Good.

### The twenty-sixth Epistle

10. For it goes very clearly through the three *principles* <note>original: "Principles"; these are Böhme's three realms of existence: the dark fire-world (the Father), the light world (the Son), and the outer world of nature.</note> and shows the whole foundation <note>original: "ground"</note>, so that a man (unless he willfully chooses to be blind) may *know God, the Kingdom of Heaven, and himself*. It likewise explains our lamentable fall and also the restoration in the life of *Jesus Christ*. It shall especially treat of the fair *lilies* which **God** will bestow upon the *final age* <note>original: "last World"</note>, which will be very pleasant to read.

11. And though I do not sufficiently know the full and whole foundation of what it shall be, yet I see it in great depth. I hope, if **God** grants enough grace, not to give up until it is finished; and also in the future to finish the promised writings which are now *suppressed* <note>original: "kept back"</note> by the oppressor <note>Böhme likely refers to the local religious authorities in Görlitz who had forbidden him from writing.</note>. This includes [my exposition] upon *Moses*, where the great wonders of **God** shall be *clearly* revealed to the light of day—the wonders which **God** will freely bestow and afford to the final age.

12. However, *at present*, everything is in *Babel* <note>Böhme uses "Babel" as a symbol for the confusion, corruption, and division within the institutionalized church.</note>, and there a great division <note>original: "rent"</note> shall be made. Yet let no one despair; for just as **God** helped the children of *Israel* with consolation during the *Babylonian Captivity* and sent them *prophets*, even so shall *lilies* now grow up in the midst of *thorns*. This is wonderful.

13. Also, no one should think that the entire destruction of the city of *Babel* shall happen even *now*. There shall truly be an exceedingly great *division*, such as people *now* do not believe; for the *Antichrist* is not *wholly* revealed, though he is certainly revealed in part.

14. People shall *suppose* that they have completely rooted him out, and after some sorrow, great joy shall follow. They shall make laws and covenants, together with severe, sharp articles of religion—yet for the most part, these will be for the advancement of their own honor and power. People shall suppose that the Holy Spirit of Heaven speaks and that there is now a *golden age* <note>original: "golden World"</note>; yet it remains full of **God’s** anger and is still in *Babel*. The true essence of the right life in *Christ* is not yet within it.

15. Also, the Rider on the *Pale Horse* <note>A reference to Revelation 6:8, symbolizing death or pestilence.</note> shall come after and cut many down with the *sickle*. Yet in the meantime, the *lily* springs up among the wonders, against which the last *Antichrist* shall raise *persecution*. It is then that his *end* comes, for the appearance of the *Lord* terrifies him.

17. Blessed is he who seeks the Lord with full earnestness, for He shall not be found in history <note>likely meaning "external historical accounts" or "dry academic study"</note>, but in true trust and in the right...

# THE TWENTY-SEVENTH EPISTLE.

->TO<-
# *CHARLES of ENDERN.

<margin>1.</margin>
<image-desc>Large ornamental drop cap 'N' with floral and vine motifs within a square border.</image-desc>
NOBLE, Right Honorable Sir: My humble, ready, and willing service, with all cordial wishes of God's love and grace to <gloss>your new creature</gloss> <note>original: "your new creature"; referring to the spiritually reborn self or "New Man" in Pauline theology</note> in the new man, <gloss>in the body of Jesus Christ</gloss>, as also all temporal <note>original: "temporall"; worldly or time-bound</note> prosperity and blessing for the earthly body, are here offered.

2. I have considered your noble heart and mind, which is kindled and inflamed with love not only toward God, but likewise toward his children. This has exceedingly rejoiced me in *Christ*. I must specifically recognize your true earnestness and zeal, which I know and acknowledge; for you have put much effort into my few writings of the first part <note>Böhme is likely referring to his first work, *Aurora*, which circulated in manuscript form before being seized</note> and disregarded the murderous [or confusing] cries of the Oppressor <note>original: "Oppreffour"; a reference to Gregor Richter, the primate of Görlitz, who led the persecution against Böhme</note>. 3. This persuades me that God has opened a little gate [of his wisdom] to you, which was firmly shut to the Oppressor. This is because he sought it through *human art and pride*; therefore, it was hidden from him. For he was offended by the status of the writer <note>Böhme was a self-taught shoemaker, a fact that the university-educated clergy found scandalous</note> and did not consider what is written in the Holy Scripture: *My power is made perfect in weakness* <note>original: "My power is mighty in the weake"; 2 Corinthians 12:9</note>; and how Christ thanked his Father that he had hidden these things from the prudent and wise and revealed them to babes. And he said further, "Yes, Father, for so it has pleased you!" <note>Matthew 11:25–26</note>

4. Also, I am truly persuaded and convinced in my spirit that you have not done this out of any *curiosity*, but as becomes the children of God who seek the precious pearl <note>A reference to the "Pearl of Great Price" from Matthew 13:45–46, a common metaphor in Böhme's work for divine wisdom or the inner Kingdom of God</note> and are desirous

oppressor *had devoured it; but even then it sprouted forth as a green twig, wholly unknown to me.*

10. And though I know nothing of my self regarding what God is about to do—and his counsel and the way he will take are hidden from me, so that I can say nothing from my own authority—it is also possible that the oppressor might accuse me of *pedantic pride*. He might claim that I would only arrogantly boast of my small gifts (which were given to me by grace) and thereby set forth the thoughts and imaginations of my heart for my own vain glory and boasting.

11. Yet I declare in the presence of God, and testify to it before his judgment (where all things shall appear, and everyone shall give an account of his deeds), that I myself *do not know* what has happened to me or how things go with me, except only that I have a driving will <note>original: "driving will"; a sense of inner compulsion or divine motivation</note>.

12. I also do not know what I shall write; for when I write, *the Spirit dictates the same to me in great, wonderful knowledge, so that I often cannot tell whether I (as to my spirit) am in this world or not*. I rejoice exceedingly at this, and therein sure and certain knowledge is imparted to me.

13. And the more I seek, the more I find—and always deeper—so that I many times consider my sinful person too weak and unworthy to approach such *high mysteries*. But then the spirit sets up my banner and says, "*Arise! You shall live in them eternally and be crowned with them; why are you amazed?*"

14. Therefore, noble Sir, I give you to understand in few words the basis and cause of both the will and *search* behind my writings. If you have a mind to read anything in them, I leave it to your choice. I am sending you now what was written formerly when I was with you—namely, from the beginning of the twenty-second chapter to the end. There, indeed, the noble coral <note>original: "Corall"; Böhme often uses gemstone and mineral imagery to describe spiritual states; here it refers to a stage of spiritual revelation</note> is opened, and my mind shows me that you shall find pleasure and delight in it. Herein you shall also obtain a *little pearl* <note>original: "little Pearle"; Böhme’s recurring metaphor for the spark of divine wisdom or the "Pearl of Great Price" found in Christ</note> if your mind is approved and directed toward God.

15. The rest (which consist of about thirty sheets) our well-known and good friend has; he shall give them to you. There are very high and deep things contained in them, and they are very worthy of *preservation*. You shall likewise have them if you please to read them.

16. And although I intended to keep these writings somewhat *quiet and secret*, it is nevertheless manifest; for I hear that haughty people desire them. Through such people, the enemy (being a destroyer) might do away with them; for I know well what kind of enemy the Devil is, who contradicts and opposes me. Therefore, I entreat you to deal wisely and carefully; I shall speedily (if need require) call for them.

### The Twenty-Seventh Epistle

17. And shortly, if God permits, more and deeper things shall be written regarding *Moses* and the *Prophets*; and then at last concerning the whole *Tree of Life*, within the *Being of all Beings* <note>original: "Being of all Beings"; Böhme uses this to refer to the divine essence or the source of all existence</note>. ## IMMANUEL <note>Hebrew: "God with us."</note>.

My dear Christian brother and friend: I send you all my heartfelt wishes for divine love and further illumination, along with true perseverance, constancy, and patience, so that you may patiently endure the *Cross of Christ*.

### *Our Salvation is in the life of Jesus Christ.*

2. I have received the letter you sent, and I rejoice in the Lord my God, who so richly and abundantly imparts *His grace* to us. He opens our hearts so that we, through the combination <note>original: "conjecture"</note> of our gifts, desire to search into His wisdom and wonders.

3. Your offered <note>original: "tendred"</note> friendship is very pleasing and acceptable to me. # THE
# THIRTY-SECOND
# EPISTLE.

### *Our salvation consists in the effective, working love of Jesus Christ within us.*

---

1. My very loving and Christian friend; I wish you the highest peace with the hearty love of a fellow member of Christ. It is my desire that the true Sun of the effective love of Jesus Christ may continually arise and shine in your *spirit, soul, and body*.

2. I received your letter dated the 24th of *January* fourteen days after *Easter*. I rejoiced to see in it that you are a thirsty, fervent, and eager *searcher* and lover of the true ground <note>The fundamental basis or underlying reality.</note> [of the knowledge of Divine Mysteries], which I perceive you have sought and searched for with diligence.

3. That my writings have come into your hands and please you is certainly caused by the appointment of God. He brings lovers to [that which they love] and often uses strange means by which he satisfies the desire of those who love a thing. He feeds them with his gifts [and graces] and puts an *<term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for the fundamental essence or being of a thing.</note> of the true fire <margin>Or, living spark.</margin>* into their love so that it may burn rightly. You may rest assured that if you continue your constancy in the love of truth, it will open, reveal, and manifest itself to you in its flaming love and make itself certainly known. However, the search for it must be begun correctly; for we do not attain the true ground of divine knowledge by the sharp searching and speculation of our reason from without. Instead, the searching must begin *from within*, in the *hunger* of the soul, for reason penetrates no further than its own <term>Astrum</term> <margin>Or, constellation.</margin> of the outward world, from which reason has its origin.

4. But the soul searches its own <term>Astrum</term> <note>Boehme uses the term "Astrum" to refer to the inner celestial or spiritual configuration of the soul, corresponding to the "stars" of the macrocosm.</note>, namely, in the inward...

<summary>In this opening to his thirty-second letter, Jacob Boehme encourages a new seeker of divine truth, explaining that spiritual knowledge is a gift from God that must be sought within the soul rather than through external human reason.</summary>

<keywords>Jacob Boehme, spiritual enlightenment, divine mysteries, Ens, Astrum, reason, soul, inner search, mystical theology</keywords>

inward spiritual world from which this visible world has its origin, outflow, and production, and in which its ground [and foundation] stands.

5. But if the soul wishes to search its own *Star* <note>original: "Astrum"; a spiritual constellation or influence.</note> [or spiritual constellation]—namely, the *Great Mystery* <margin>Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note></margin> [or the eternal divine nature]—it must first wholly yield up all its power and its will to divine love and grace. It must become like a child and turn itself toward its *Center* through repentance and a desire to do nothing but only what the Spirit of God is pleased to search through it [or employ it for].

6. And when it has thus yielded and resigned itself, seeking nothing but God and its own salvation—as well as how it may serve and love its neighbor—and then finds within itself a desire for divine and natural knowledge, it may assure itself that it is then *drawn* [and inclined] toward it by *God*. Then it may rightly search and find the deep ground mentioned in my writings.

7. For the Spirit of God searches through that soul and brings it at length *into the depths of the Deity. As Saint Paul says, the Spirit searches all things—even the deep things of God.*

8. Dear sir, it is a simple, childlike way that leads to the highest wisdom, though the world does not know it. You do not need to seek wisdom in remote places or travel to foreign countries for it; she stands at the door of your soul and knocks. If she finds an empty, resigned, and free place in the soul, she will reveal herself there indeed and rejoice in it more than the sun does in the elements. If the soul yields itself up to wisdom for full possession, then she penetrates it with her flaming fire of love and unlocks all mysteries to the soul.

9. Sir, you may perhaps wonder how a plain layman could come to understand such high mysteries, having never read them nor heard them from any man. But, dear sir, I tell you that what you have seen in my writings is but a glimpse of the mysteries, for a man cannot write them down. If God should count you worthy to have the light kindled in your soul, you would see, taste, smell, feel, and hear unspeakable words of God concerning this knowledge. That is the true *School of Divine Wisdom of Pentecost* <note>original: "Theosophicall School of Pentecost"; referring to the direct revelation of the Holy Spirit as experienced by the Apostles.</note> where the soul is taught † by <margin>† From or by.</margin> God.

10. After this, there is no more need for searching and painful toiling [over it], for all gates stand open. A very simple, ordinary <note>original: "mean"; here meaning humble or of low social status.</note> man may attain it if he does not hinder himself by his own willful [imaginations] and efforts. For it lies within man *already* and only needs to be awakened [stirred up or quickened] by the Spirit of God.

11. In my talent [or writings] (as I was able in my simplicity)...

<margin>* That is, the book titled *The Way to Christ*, containing a treatise on Repentance, Resignation (or Self-Denial), and Regeneration.</margin>

12. But as for the basis of the high *Natural Mysteries*—which you, Mr. Walter, and Mr. Leonhart Elvern desire a further and clearer explanation of—please ask Mr. Walter for it. I would have liked to make it even clearer, but because of the great depth of the subject—and also out of concern for the *unworthy*—it cannot be done. *Christ says in Matthew 7:7: "Seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you."* No one can give this understanding to another; *everyone must receive it for himself from God*. One may certainly provide a <term>manuduction</term> <note>original: "manuduction"; a leading by the hand or a guided introduction.</note> or direction to another, but he cannot give him the actual understanding of it.

13. Yet know that *a Lily blossoms for you in the Northern Countries*. If you do not destroy it with the sectarian contention of the learned, then it will become a great tree among you. But if you choose to argue rather than to know the true God, then the ray (or beam of light) will pass you by and *hit only a few*. Afterward, you will be forced to draw water for the thirst of your souls from among foreign nations.

14. 15. I will freely give you what the Lord has given me; only take care to employ it rightly. It will be a witness for you against those who mock. Let no man look at my person; this is a mere gift of God, bestowed not only for my sake, but also for your sake and for all those who shall come to read these works.

16. Let no man watch any longer for the *Time* to come; it is already born (begun or come about). Whomever it shines upon, it hits. Whoever is awake sees it, and he who sleeps does not see it. The time has appeared and will soon appear more fully. He who watches sees it; many have already felt it. However, a great tribulation must first pass over before it is wholly manifest. The cause of this is *the contention of the scholars*, who tread the Cup of Christ underfoot and argue about a "Child" <note>Boehme often uses the image of a child to represent the birth of the new spirit or Christ within the soul.</note> who was never in a worse state since humanity began.

### The Thirty-Third Epistle

And I exhort you, as my fellow-wrestler, to fight a good fight in faith and wait in patience for the revelation of *Jesus Christ*, and continue to stand fast.

23. Beloved Mr. *Marcus*: that you and your father are in good health rejoices and gladdens me. I have received the box of comfits <term>comfits: sugar-coated seeds, nuts, or spices; a traditional type of sweetmeat</term> and return thanks to you for them.

25. *That which my native country casts away, other nations shall take up.*

26. I send to you and your father a copy of my books for each of you, and some for good friends; for I heard that previously you had obtained some of them for everyone.

27. I have none of the other writings at hand; I would gladly have sent some of them to you, but I hope to come to those parts shortly. Then, God willing, I will bring some along with me. I commend you to the kind and gracious love of *Jesus Christ*.

28. The enemy’s intention is evil; yet by his actions, he publishes and spreads my talent abroad. It is greatly desired here, and many a hungry soul is refreshed by it, even though the ignorant cast their reproach and scorn against it. *You shall yet hear wonderful things*.

29. For the time is <margin>\* Born <note>The original text uses "Borne" to mean the time has arrived or been brought forth</note>.</margin> come, of which I was told three years ago by a *vision*: namely, the time OF REFORMATION. As for the end result, the event, or exactly when it will happen, I commit that to God; I do not yet know it perfectly.

30. And with this, I commend you to the love of *Jesus Christ*.

->Dated May 8, 1624.<-

# THE THIRTY-FIFTH EPISTLE.

# A LETTER

->From<-

# JACOB BOEHME. <note>original: "Behmen"</note>

## Written from Dresden to Görlitz <note>original: "Gerlitz"</note>, during the time of his persecution; dated June 13, 1624.

->TO<-

## Doctor Kobern.

---

->*God with us.* <note>original: "Immanuel"</note><-

---

1. My very dear sir and Christian brother: I heartily desire the continual working of the love of Jesus Christ in you, so that your pearl tree <note>original: "Tree of Pearle"; a metaphor for the growth of divine wisdom and the soul's development in Christ</note> may grow great under the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ through such agitation and trial. I pray that we all, in that power, may withstand the wrathful enemy of Christ in faith and in the meekness of Christ—the enemy who at present roars like...

--- Page 257 ---
<meta>Jacob Boehme continues his letter to Doctor Kobern, warning him that the spiritual path invites the fury of the Devil, who acts through worldly persecutors. He encourages the Doctor to respond with patience rather than force.</meta>

...like a raging lion; he sets himself mightily against Jesus and his children. We must fight the good fight with *Paul* so that we may eventually gain the prize—*our salvation*—through it. For the sake of temporary honor and pleasure, we must not deny Christ once we have acknowledged the truth; otherwise, it would be very difficult to recover it again.

2. For my part, I thank God in *Jesus Christ* that he has signed me *with his marks* and daily makes me like his image. I pray to him that I may remain steadfast, and also that he would deliver my enemies from the abominable death of eternal horror in which they are currently held captive without knowing it. May he bring them also into the light, so that they might know *this way* and enter our eternal brotherhood <note>original: "Eternall Fraternity"</note>.

3. Yet to speak judiciously about these things, we clearly see with our own eyes that this way is entirely opposed to the Devil, because he rages so much against it without cause. It is indeed a great wonder that he should cause such an uproar against such a small work of devotion. Surely it must not please him, but smell foul to him <note>original: "favour ill with him"</note>. Meanwhile, there are many larger books full of nonsense <note>original: "Foppery"</note>, folly, and even idolatry to be found, which he does not oppose. His spite is directed only against the Way to Christ, so that no one might walk in that path.

4. For especially at this time, he thinks he will set up his kingdom powerfully; yet he sees now that it has breaches everywhere. For the attacker <note>original: "Assaylant"</note> breaks in from many directions, especially from the *North*. At present, we can do no better than to ignore this enemy and overcome him with *patience* under the *Cross* of Christ and with earnest repentance. Eventually, he will become weak and faint, and this firebrand will come to an end.

<margin>Note: This happened in the seventh year after the author's death.</margin>
<margin>\* Gregory Richter, the Primate of Görlitz <note>original: "Garlitz"</note>.</margin>
5. For he is but a fiery flash of God’s anger, which must be quenched with divine love and humility. We must in no way add fuel to it to make it burn, but instead kill it with *Christ’s victory*. Just as Christ overcame the wrath of God and hell with his love, crushed death, and ruled mightily over all his enemies, so these enemies within the anger of God shall not prevail for long. As Christ has taught us, we should feed our enemies with food and drink and rejoice when they afflict us for his sake; our reward is in heaven.

<margin>\* Or, reproaches.</margin>

Instead, we shall overcome him with patience and prayer. I do not care about his unjust revilings <note>original: "\* revilings"</note>; I have a clear conscience regarding him. The time is coming quickly...
