...that such an enemy will be cut in pieces by the sword of God’s power.

7. It is right that we should consider the time; for Babel <note>Babel: Boehme’s term for the corrupt, confused, and divided state of the worldly church and society</note> burns throughout the whole world, and there is woe in every street. Only, men do not see it yet, but are blind to it.

8. I give you very great thanks for your brotherly faithfulness and Christian care in having taken some of my wife’s things into your keeping. If the High Priest <note>High Priest: Boehme’s satirical title for his chief persecutor in Görlitz, the Pastor Primarius Gregory Richter</note> insists on assaulting my house, let him do it, so that it may be known in all countries what a maker of uproars he is. It will lead much to the honor of him and his followers; he will gain a great deal of credit in the Electoral Council <note>Electoral Council: The governing body of the Elector of Saxony in Dresden</note> for having stormed my house using his "trusty officers" and breaking the windows. If others were to do or cause such a thing, the Council would not tolerate them in the city.

9. Therefore, I marvel greatly that they make such an uproar in Görlitz without cause, giving occasion for such an evil report <margin>Or, Evil report concerning the City.</margin> against the city. If the reasons for it were investigated, it would sound very strange indeed. Nevertheless, it must be so, for the time has come <note>original: "the time is Borne"</note>. Something else will suddenly follow this; this is but a sign, type, or figure. Seeing as they have so solemnly celebrated the Pentecost <margin>The day of Pentecost.</margin>, the Holy Spirit must surely be assisting them powerfully! By this, it may be clearly seen what spirit they are children of, and which spirit they serve. This will give us even more reason to avoid them. I suppose it is loathsome enough; it stinks of Pharisaical pitch and hellish soot. Oh, that God would finally have pity on the simple people, who are so very blind and pull down the judgment of God upon themselves—which will shortly be poured forth.

10. Their consistency <note>original: "stability"</note> is easily seen: that which they approve of at one time, they disallow at another. Oh, if some Jesuits were to come and return the Church from Luther back to Rome again, what "good Papists" they would make!

11. But let it go as it does; silence is best. They hunt after a gnat <note>The "gnat" is Boehme himself</note> and think they have caught venison. But there lies hidden a small grain of mustard seed of the Cross in it, which put Christ to death; that shall burst their guts and grow to be a great tree, and no one can resist this.

12. My wife does not need to have any window shutters made. If they want to break the windows, they may, and then the "fruits" of the High Priest will be seen. Let her have a little patience. If she cannot find a place in Görlitz, I will find a place for her somewhere else where she shall have peace enough. But let her stay inside at home and not go out except when necessary, and let the enemy rage—he will not eat her up.

If she cannot find a place in *Görlitz*, I will find a place for her somewhere else where she will have enough peace. But let her stay inside at home and not go out except when necessary, and let the enemy rage—he will not devour her.

### The Thirty-Fifth Epistle

<margin>* The Prince Elector of Saxony.</margin>
13. I must wait yet a while here and wait to see what God shall please to do; for I have only recently gained a little acquaintance among the *Great Ones* here, which happens daily. I am well so far, thanks be to God, but I have not had any opportunity to request anything for my *protection* from the Lords, as the \* Prince Elector <note>John George I, Elector of Saxony (reigned 1611–1656)</note> has gone on a journey, and some of the chief lords are with him.

14. Though I do not rely upon any worldly protection, I will venture it in God’s name and trust him only, from whom I have received my Talent.

<margin>† Doctor Aegidius Strauch.</margin>
15. Next Sunday, there is a conference arranged here at my landlord’s house, which the † Superintendent <note>A high-ranking Lutheran official who oversaw several parishes; here referring to Aegidius Strauch</note> himself desires to have with me. I am invited to **Supper**, where some of the Prince Elector’s counselors of state will be present; whatever happens there, I shall let you know at the first opportunity.

16. For he loves my *Treatise of Repentance*; he only wishes to ask, and hear from me personally, concerning some points which are too high for him—specifically, *from what basis they flow*. I am well pleased with this and shall observe the outcome.

17. So I also expect the decision of *Privy Counselor Losz* <note>Joachim von Loss, a powerful official in the Saxon court</note>, to whom I shall go as soon as possible. Whatever happens there, I will let you know at the first opportunity. I hope all will go well; as God wills, so I will. Who knows what God wants done, or what he will do with me? I marvel at it myself—how I am led so wonderfully without any intent or purpose of my own.

<margin>* Referring to a table drawer.</margin>
18. By this bearer, I send two Reichsthalers <note>original: "Rixdollers"; silver coins used in the Holy Roman Empire</note> to my wife for her needs; if she wants for anything, she knows well where she may get it. The key of the \* drawer lies in the parlor by the warming pan, upon the shelf. *Your treatise lies in the drawer*; you may ask for it. Your letter which you sent to Zittau <note>original: "Zitta"</note> has not yet come to my hands. If anything happens, let me know; if there is no reliable messenger at hand, just send it to Mr. Melchior Berntten at Zittau, as he has an opportunity to send things here every week. Let him know so that he may send it away as we have agreed.

19. Greet my wife and two sons for me, and exhort them to Christian patience and prayer, and to intend no personal revenge, so that the enemy may gain no advantage.

20. The business with Mr. Furstenau’s family is indeed not good, nevertheless, it will prove to be no great matter. It is the High Priest’s <note>Boehme's nickname for his antagonist, Pastor Gregorius Richter</note> own reproach; and it would even turn to his great disgrace if it were well-answered. I wish his Prince only knew the truth of it; he would protect him thoroughly <note>original: "with a witnesse"; an idiom meaning "with a vengeance" or "undeniably"</note>. These are the "good fruits" of the High Priest.

**21.** I hope to visit you very soon; even if I should return here again, it *will not cost me my life* <note>original: "cost me my neck"</note>. It is only a mad outcry, for there is nothing in it but the *priest's bell-clapper* <note>The "clapper" is the part of the bell that strikes the side; Boehme uses this as a metaphor for the noisy, repetitive accusations of the clergy</note> which sounds so "sweetly." It is easy to judge whether it is Christ’s voice or the Devil's; you do not need to be so mortally afraid of this quarrel. It is not a business you need to be ashamed of; it is nothing but Babel’s \* bell, <margin>\* Or, peal.</margin> which is rung to give warning [or to sound the alarm].

**22.** Just stand by it firmly in the Spirit of Christ, and then Christ’s \* bell will also be rung; may God give them and us all a good mind.

**23.** Please greet Mr. *Frederick Renischen*; I could do nothing for him here yet, for things here are done very much through favoritism, and there are many people waiting around whenever there is anything to be gained. I would very gladly serve him in love if I were only able; I cannot yet advise myself <note>meaning: "I don't even know what to do for myself yet"</note> until God helps me. My [son] *Jacob* shall still remain at *Görlitz* so that his mother may have some comfort there until I can arrange things otherwise. That would have happened already if I were not staying here; let her only have patience. And so I commend you to the love of Jesus Christ.

<meta>This page begins "The First Epistle" and introduces the author's critique of worldly philosophy compared to spiritual knowledge. It continues the introductory matter of the collection.</meta>

# THE
# FIRST EPISTLE.

->*Grace, peace, and mercy; light, life, and power from God our Father, and Jesus Christ our Lord.*<-

<margin>1.</margin> DEAR and very worthy friend, it makes me especially glad and joyful to find that you have such an intimate, entire thirst after the precious Pearl and fair Lily of Paradise—namely, after the light and life of God. This is especially true in this age, which is so filled with the excess of vanity and iniquity, even though Jesus Christ is richly preached to the world and all people; yet he is hardly known correctly by anyone—or by very few—according to the Spirit. <margin>according to the flesh</margin>

<margin>2.</margin> For when we search the writings of the philosophers and learned men—not only those among the heathens, but the Christians as well—we shall find (when they write of the wisdom and knowledge of nature and of all things) very little to show that they laid the right foundation. Nor do they show that they built their structure upon HIM from whom all things proceed and upon whom they rest: namely, God himself. Because of this, it is an easy matter to judge what kind of building and structure that is which stands only upon the sand and miry bog of self-wisdom, opinion, and reason. One can see whether this knowledge and science of theirs is true and real, or rather a mock wisdom and a boastful <note>original: "vapouring"</note> display of knowledge—the same kind of which Saint Paul says that it does not edify <term>edify: to build up or strengthen spiritually; from 1 Corinthians 8:1</term>, but only puffs up.

<margin>3.</margin> Let a man consider for himself whether anyone can speak truly and essentially <term>essentially: regarding the true nature or "essence" of a thing</term> about a thing without its true foundation, and how he can teach correctly about nature and the knowledge of it without the very Creator of that nature and without the knowledge of HIM who founded it. How can there be light where a person makes themselves the light, and where the creature leads itself astray from its Creator? And how can that be wisdom which does not lay its foundation in the highest and essential wisdom, and does not lead us back to that wisdom again, but only to an imaginary conceit <term>conceit: a fanciful notion or excessive pride in one's own ideas</term>?

<summary>The author addresses a friend, praising their spiritual thirst for divine truth while critiquing worldly philosophers for building their knowledge on human reason rather than on God, the true foundation of nature.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, spiritual wisdom, Pearl of Paradise, Lily of Paradise, philosophy, divine foundation, self-wisdom, Saint Paul</keywords>

--- Page 267 ---

# Concerning Jacob Boehme <note>original: J. B. T.</note>

The Milky Way <note>original: *via lactea*</note>, or "Saint Jacob’s white path," was given to the European nations as a special, significant sign of a total new birth [and manifestation] out of the *upper fiery crystalline waters*. This was meant to stir up many profound, learned, and deep-searching minds. As one effect of this, he happily finished his last *mystical book*, which (as he often told me personally) was most worthy of reading: namely, the *Mysterium Magnum* <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*, meaning "The Great Mystery"</note> [or *Commentary*] on Genesis, in the year 1623. 

This occurred between the years 1604 and 1607 (when the new stars appeared again), marking the exit of the seven or *seventh trigonal conjunction* <note>An astrological alignment of planets occurring in the same zodiacal "triplicity" or element, seen by mystics as signaling a new age.</note>, and the eighth from the *seventh central beginning*. Thereupon, in the following year, 1624—in the *Jubilee*, or fiftieth year of his age, according to the Mystery—he returned to his grave, or re-entered the *magical and mental principle*.

<margin>
\* His first book.
† Divinity.
</margin>

4. At first, his book \* **Aurora** in its rising (which is the root or mother of philosophy, astrology, and † **theology**, etc.), and also the little book *The Way to Christ* (which begins, according to the order of the New Testament, with repentance and faith as the entrance into the holy kingdom of God), were abused. Even his own person, and afterward his dead corpse—and at last his poor grave and the wooden cross in the churchyard—were assaulted and defaced with blind, furious zeal and very unseemly behavior. 

Yet these matters were never brought to a proper [legal] hearing. This blessed Jacob Boehme was never convicted of any error in the *Evangelical faith* <note>The term "Evangelical" here refers specifically to the Lutheran/Protestant faith of the time.</note>. Rather, as it appears by his life and conduct <note>original: "Life and Conversation"</note>, and by his sound writings concerning **Election** and the two Testaments [namely, **Baptism** and the **Lord’s Supper**], as well as concerning the suffering, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ, he was found to continue steadfastly until his very end in pure and unsophisticated *Lutheranism*. He also sufficiently declared this in a specific defense against the false and hearsay criticism of Gregory Richter, the Senior Pastor <note>original: *Primarius*</note> in 1624, who was the *Primate of Görlitz*.

5. The contention regarding the "sealed grave" of Christ and of his faithful witness Jacob Boehme is of similar importance and consequence as the dispute regarding the blessed Martin Luther. Luther’s grave at Wittenberg was surrounded and troubled by people from the North and South (not to mention the Eastern and Western nations). Yet, although it was dearly purchased, it has successfully remained under the protection of his **Electoral Highness**. Thus, in both the past and present age, these two dear and faithful witnesses of the true, clear, and pure *Evangelical light* and righteousness have remained like Moses in their graves, undisturbed by the "Babylonians" <note>A common term used by reformers to describe those they viewed as part of a corrupt or "confused" religious establishment.</note>. Evangelical Christendom has received a especially remarkable, real, and wonderful sign by which they may know the gracious visitation of God and His spirit in Christ Jesus, their only and eternal head and savior.

*Writings that are immediately revealed and communicated from God are not like the books of other men—scraped together by the spirit of astral wit <note>original: "Astrall wit"; referring to intellectual cleverness derived from the natural or "starry" world rather than divine inspiration.</note> or earthly reason, patching and piecing, picking and choosing here and there according to its fancy, theoretical hints, and astral flashes of illumination. They are not written by writing then canceling, adding, or interlining. Instead, they are written by the author himself, with the overshadowing and indwelling cooperation of the great and secret Spirit of God throughout. They are produced in one continuous draft and by the instinct of a pen that is given, not taken or usurped. Of this, I myself and many others are eyewitnesses from the author’s original manuscript and handwriting. Therefore, these writings should be viewed and judged far differently than they would be by the eyes of common historical reason.*

7. Not to mention that the "fullness of time" has **not yet come** wherein these and other wonders hidden until now might be generally, fully, and satisfactorily known and received. Yet it is continued and accomplished in God and by God, through Christ and his holy Spirit of grace. By this grace, the hidden Kingdom of God—and within it, the **Sealed Image** of **Jesus Christ**—is opened again. It is very successfully and effectively advanced in those seekers who desire and love the glory of our Lord and Savior **Jesus Christ** with inward, complete light, eternal joy, and jubilant, triumphant melodies of the heart. This is for the glory of the Most High and the salvation of our souls and our senses, which have turned away from divine light and righteousness. The loss of this light is infinitely greater than the gain of the whole world. To obtain it, we must lose ourselves and all that we have in God, the highest and chiefest good. Thus we shall find true, constant rest and assured peace forever, only in the **pierced living Rock** <note>A reference to the side of Christ pierced during the crucifixion.</note> and heart of **Jesus Christ. Amen.**

8. Toward this high and happy goal, we ought all, with the assistance and help of divine grace, to apply ourselves (as much as is possible in this mortal life) without any lingering delays. We should labor to enter into the light and walk in it while we have it, enjoying it here in time and hereafter in eternity. O *Jesus!* The only and real light and salvation of our souls, who has come into the world to free us from the power of night, darkness, and eternal death: grant us and give us this. So be it. Amen. Amen.

# A WARNING
## From J. B. T.
### TO
# THE READER.

<margin>1.</margin> The reader should be warned not to search deeper into these very profound writings, nor to climb higher through their own willpower, nor to imagine deeper things than they can understand. Let them always be satisfied with the capacity and reach of their own understanding. For within that understanding, they remain in a state of spiritual reality <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Essence"; in this context, it refers to a grounded state of being or spiritual substance where the soul is safe from delusion.</note> where they will not fall into error, no matter how deeply the Spirit leads them. *Far more will be given to one person than to another*; the only boundary or limit is that everyone must remain steadfast in *humility toward God*. They must completely surrender <note>original: "resigne up"; a central concept in Boehme's theology meaning the total submission of the human will to the Divine.</note> themselves to God, so that God may work in them both the will and the deed as He pleases.

<margin>2.</margin> When you do this, you become as if dead to your own self; for you desire nothing but God’s will, and God’s will becomes your life. This will moves within itself, even unto the * Thousandth Number <note>original: "Thousandth Number"; a mystical reference to the completion of a divine cycle or the full manifestation of God’s order.</note>, and searches the depths of the Deity and all its wonders. He leads your surrendered will into the Virgin of His Wisdom, so that you may contemplate and see all wonders. However, you must not let your imagination wander away from Him toward those wonders; as soon as you do so, you depart from God’s will—which is eternal liberty—and you become a prisoner of your own imagination. Take note of this: every act of imagination creates a state of being <term>essence</term>, and you exist within it. You must escape from that state, or you will not see God.
<margin>* The Crown of the Virgin Sophia <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, is a central figure in Christian mysticism, representing the mirror of God and the bride of the purified soul.</note></margin>

<margin>3.</margin> Therefore, Christ teaches us humility, love, mercy, and purity of heart. He commands us to seek God’s will and to surrender ourselves to it; for within God’s will, we can do all things. Our own nature must not do it, but God Himself is active within us; He is our deed and our actor if we perform any wonder. For

# A Warning from J. B. T.

No human soul shall say or think, "I will perform wonders." No, that cannot be; for wonders that surpass external nature proceed only from the center of Eternal Nature out of the *Tenth Number* <note>original: "Tenth Number"; in Boehme’s mystical numerology, the number ten represents the return to divine unity and the completion of a spiritual cycle.</note>. The creature <note>original: "Creature"; here referring to a human being as a created thing.</note> cannot <insert>reach into</insert> this on its own. But if the soul is resigned to the will of God, then God performs wonders within that creature. For it is His pleasure to manifest Himself in the weak—<insert>in the low, meek, and humble mind.</insert> The strong, however, are stubborn in their own will and will not resign or surrender it to God; such a person trusts only in their own cleverness.

<margin>* The Eternal fire <note>original: "The Eternall fire"; in Boehme's philosophy, this represents the first principle or the divine energy that powers all existence.</note>.</margin>

4. Thus, his will exists apart from God and can do nothing. If he then speaks of the being and will of God, he is a liar; for he does not speak from the Spirit and will of God, but from his own self—from his own "weening" <term>supposing or imagining</term> and *conjecture*. In this, there is nothing but doubt <insert>and uncertainty, even though he may allege, quote, and pull in any number of sayings from other men (according to his own understanding) to confirm his opinion and path.</insert> This is the source of the many divisions, *controversies*, and contentions regarding *faith* and divine knowledge: that men attempt to seek God through their own will and skill. Men want to find God within their own will, but He is *not* there. For He dwells only in that will which resigns itself—along with all its reason and skill—to *Him*. To such a person, He gives real, living knowledge and power to know and understand His *Being*.

5. Therefore, we shall seem silent, obscure, and merely "historical" <note>original: "hystoricall"; in this context, it refers to a dry, intellectual knowledge of religious facts without the living, spiritual experience of them.</note> to everyone who is not born of God. For, according to the outward man, we are in this world, but according to the inward man, we are in God. The inward man, born of God, speaks of the Kingdom of Heaven; the outward spirit, produced from the *principle* <note>original: "Principle"; Boehme’s term for the fundamental realms of existence (light, dark, and this world).</note> of this world, speaks of this world. Consequently, one person's understanding is very different from another's; everyone *apprehends and interprets according to the wisdom they have been gifted.*

6. Not everyone will understand my writings according to my own mind <insert>meaning, and understanding</insert>—indeed, *perhaps* not a single person will. Instead, everyone receives according to their own gifts, for their own edification and profit, according to how the Spirit has its own property <insert>form, and Idea</insert> within them.

7. Anyone who does not seek <insert>to be</insert> a new person, born in God <insert>or through regeneration in the Spirit of Christ</insert>, and does not wholly and sincerely apply themselves to that goal, should leave my writings alone and refrain from judging them. I have written nothing for such a "seeker." Furthermore, such a person will not be able to fully understand our meaning, even if they study <insert>and strive</insert> much over it, unless they enter into *resignation in Christ*. There, they may obtain and grasp the spirit of the *Universal* <note>original: "Universall"; likely referring to the Universal Spirit or the totality of Divine Wisdom.</note>; otherwise, all effort will be in vain. We also warn the curious, the *critic*, the speculator, and the rational "artist" <term>Artist; here meaning a person who relies on human art, logic, or technical skill rather than divine inspiration.</term>

I also do not know what I shall write, for when I write, the Spirit dictates to me in great and wonderful knowledge. It is to such an extent that I often do not know whether, in my spirit, I am in this world or not. At this I rejoice exceedingly, for then sure and certain knowledge is imparted to me; the more I seek, the more I find, and continually deeper. I often consider my sinful person too mean, low, and unworthy to address such mysteries; but then the Spirit sets up my banner <note>original: "Banner"; a symbol of divine protection and a call to spiritual duty.</note> and says, *"Arise! # A Warning from J.B.T. <note>original: "J.B.T."; initials for Jacob Boehme Teutonicus (1575–1624), a German mystic and theologian.</note>

...above the reason of all men—yes, deeper than the foundation of this world is?

19. Dear Christians, it proceeds from God's love toward you, so that you might finally see the root and ground of your *school contentions* <note>original: "School contentions"; refers to the formal theological and philosophical disputes between various academic and religious factions of the time.</note> and controversies of academic reason. For many have fought, but not at the right place [mark or gate], which is why they have fallen into contending, disputing, wrangling, and verbal jangling. This has filled the world and almost completely destroyed all brotherly love. Therefore, God calls you with a higher voice, so that you might see from where all things, both good and evil, arise and proceed originally, to the end that you should cease from strife and learn to know Him really and fundamentally. This knowledge has been hidden from the beginning of the world until now, and has been revealed only in the children of the saints.

<margin>* Note.</margin>
20. If you have a desire and delight to read my writings, read them diligently, and especially apply yourselves to the *Center of All Beings*; and then the *Three Principles* <note>Boehme’s cosmological theory describing the Dark World (divine wrath), the Light World (divine love), and the Outward World (the visible universe).</note> will be plain and easy to you. I know and am assured that if you apprehend the center in the spirit, it will afford you such joy as far surpasses the joy of the whole world. For the precious *Stone of the Wise Men* <note>The "Philosopher's Stone," a legendary substance in alchemy; here, Boehme uses it as a metaphor for Christ or spiritual transformation.</note> lies within it, which gives the certainty and real ground of all things. It frees a person from all trouble and perplexing thoughts in the controversies of *religion*, and it opens up to him the highest mystery that is in him. It brings that work to which nature has chosen him to the highest perfection, and it is able to see into the heart of everything. Is this not a *jewel* surpassing all the treasures and riches of the world?
<margin>* The Philosopher's Stone.</margin>

It is not new, and there shall also be nothing new except only the true knowledge, in the Holy Spirit, of the *Being of All Beings* <note>original: "Being of all Beings"; the essential nature of God from which all things originate.</note>. My writings are not written for the wise and prudent of this world, nor for the "fat swine of the Devil" who despise the light of nature and walk in brutish ways, but for the hungry, seeking children of God who shall profess the Kingdom of Heaven. We must give bread to the children who are worthy, so that they may eat and praise our Father in heaven, *but not cast pearls before swine.*

He must be *born again* <note>original: "Regenerate"</note> anew of Christ—of Christ’s flesh and blood, of that Word which became man—and walk in God’s love. Then he will attain the *true* <note>original: "right"</note> understanding and value it as a great jewel, for the mind does not give up until it reaches the innermost ground.

27. We will only faithfully warn the reader, as he loves his own soul and *eternity*, to beware of doubting, unbelief, and contempt, lest he in any way dally with these high mysteries and thereby blaspheme the Holy Spirit of God. Otherwise, his mind may become like *Lucifer’s*. When Lucifer saw the greatest mystery—that the Deity stood in such humility—he was offended. He turned himself away from the light of love and entered into the strong power of the fire. In his own wit and cunning craft, he wanted to lord it over God, which is completely contrary to the laws of eternity. He thought God should be subject to him. He wanted to be a creator <note>original: "former"</note> in nature and rule the magical ground as a special lord and artist. He wanted to play and sport with the *Center of the Transmutation <term>The process of changing one quality or substance into another.</term> of the properties* and do all things as he wished and pleased. He despised God’s love and humility, and therefore he was cast out of his own place as a creature into eternal darkness—into the *Abyss* of the *Harsh Command* <note>original: "Auſtere Fiat"; 'Fiat' is Latin for 'let it be done,' referring here to the creative or restrictive power of God's word.</note>. There he must remain for all eternity. Had he only directed his imagination toward the light of the Majesty, like the other angelic thrones, he would still have been an *angel*. But he went out of God’s love and into his anger; thus, he is now a devil, *that is* <note>original: "Viz."</note>, an enemy of God’s love and all holy angels. For the Kingdom of Heaven, the angelic world, and the power of the heart of God consist of love, meekness, and humility.

28. But I am not surprised that human reason <note>original: "selfe-reason"</note>—which is only learned in the "letter" of the law without God’s Spirit—taunts, quibbles, and condemns everything that does not precisely agree and conform to the *canons, rules, and institutions of the universities* and high *schools*. This reason comes from the outside (whereas God’s Spirit is from within); it is a mixture of good and evil. It passes like the wind and is driven back and forth. It values human judgment; it gives its credit and verdict only according to how the high and *great ones*—those who have the respect and authority of the world—judge and censure. It does not know the mind of the Lord, for that mind is not *in it*. Its understanding comes from the stars <note>A reference to the common Early Modern belief that human intellect and personality are influenced by astral or natural forces, distinct from divine revelation.</note>, and it is nothing but a counterfeit shadow of imagination in comparison to divine wisdom.

29. Although the children of God do not all have the same gift, style, or form of expression (for knowledge is manifold), it is our duty to test their hearts and wills. When we find that they arise and spring from one *Center*—namely, from the Spirit of Christ—we should rightly be satisfied with that Center. We should leave the manner of expression to the highest *Language* <margin>* Or, Language.</margin>, that is, to the Spirit of God’s wisdom.

31. The Spirit of God himself judges all things. If that Spirit is in us, why should we then confuse <note>original: "amuse"</note> and captivate our minds with such empty talk? Even so it is in *us* men; we should rather congratulate and heartily love one another because God reveals his wisdom so variously in us.

I want only to be the instrument <note>original: "Instrument" — a tool or means used by someone to achieve a purpose.</note> and *HE* the hand that works.

40. I do not first gather sayings and literal concepts for my knowledge by collecting them from many books. Instead, I have the letters within me. Do not heaven and earth and all things lie within man—even God Himself? Should a person not then dare to read in that book which he himself is?

# A Warning from J. B. T.
<note>original: "J. B. T." — This refers to Jacob Boehme, the Teutonic philosopher (1575–1624), a German mystic whose works were widely translated into English in the mid-1600s.</note>

49. But you are drunk, and go astray, and seek the *Key* to the Book, and contend about the Key: everyone says, "I have the Key"; and none will open his own life’s Book. Everyone might have the Key to God in himself if he sought it in the *right place*; but you choose rather to contend than to seek the Key in yourselves. Therefore you are blind, even all of you who contend; you court your own delusive shadows of fancy, and act like one who beats the air. Why do you not go into the *Center*? <note>original: "Centre" — In Boehme’s philosophy, the "Center" refers to the inner spiritual core where the divine light meets the soul.</note> With such kind of seeking, you will not find the Key, however learned you may be: *it helps nothing.*

50. It does not lie in art <note>original: "Art" — Referring here to academic skill or human craftsmanship/learning.</note> and reason, but in an earnest, resolved, and fixed will to go out from the self, and forsake all self-knowledge, and to cast yourselves with a penitent, humble desire into God’s knowledge, disclaiming all your own knowing, and desiring nothing but God’s knowing—yet in such a manner that He may know in you whatever He pleases. And so you shall attain divine knowledge and find the *Key* for which you contend.

51. Loving sirs and brothers in Christ: become scholars of the wisdom of God; let no man say of himself that he understands it. We know nothing of God—what God is—unless God’s spirit is the knowledge within us. Otherwise, our knowledge is but a fiction <note>original: "Fable"</note>, a continual confusion, always learning and yet understanding nothing of the foundation in the Center.

52. What does it matter if I am able to speak and dispute much about wisdom from the writings of others, and could even memorize <note>original: "con"</note> the whole Bible by heart, yet understood nothing of what the wise men spoke from their spirit and knowledge? If I do not likewise have the same spirit which they had, how can I understand them?

53. To such knowledge as this, no speculative assumptions <note>original: "conjecturall supposals"</note> or the gathering of an abundance of texts and sayings to ratify and confirm what we intend and conclude upon belong. No saint or wise man has done so. Instead, there belongs a living spirit from God, which is able to look into the Mystery <note>original: "Mystery" — Likely the "Mysterium Magnum," the hidden source of all things in Boehme's thought.</note> and walk in its own unique knowledge.

54. God’s spirit must be in the reason if reason is to see God. An humble, resigned heart is required for this, and no proud, contemptuous boasting in the reason. Where reason vaunts and pretends an enlightened [corrected] judgment, this is nothing else but an astral-sidereal [starry or celestial] illumination, <note>original: "Astrall Sydereall illumination" — In 17th-century mysticism, this refers to intellectual sharpness derived from the natural world or the influence of the stars, which was seen as inferior to direct divine revelation.</note> through which it becomes subtle and quick of apprehension.

<margin>* That is, a Christian in name only.</margin>
...monstrous disguise <note>original: "Cap"</note> of the Devil, and walks in pride. Such a person is no Christian, but a titular Christian—a Christian from the teeth outward: a confounding <term>Babel</term> <note>original: "Babel" — Referring to the Biblical Tower of Babel, Boehme uses this term to describe the confusion and "noise" of conflicting religious dogmas and sectarian fighting.</note>. All contemptuous, disdainful, and contentious books and pamphlets are such a Babel, for they cause only confusion.

56. If we showed one another the way of God in love, humility, and in the fear of God—as it becomes the children of God—there would not be such contention and contempt in the world. By these disputes, the simple <term>Lay-man</term> <note>original: "Lay-man" — A person who is not a member of the clergy or a professional scholar.</note> is deceived and misled. He falls into condemning and despising his brother who is not of his own opinion or religious denomination, yet he knows no reason for it at all. The one is just as blind in religion as the other; for without the spirit and power of God, religion is nothing but human invention and guesswork.

57. For true religion does not consist only in outward words or devout appearances—not in verbal confessions and outward professions—but in *living*, working, and effectual *power*. It is the desire, from the ground and bottom of one's heart, to practice and carry out what he knows in love toward another.

58. It must come to the practice and the deed, or else it is nothing but a painted, feigned faith—a historical Babel. Where God's spirit is not, there is no faith and no Christian. But where the spirit is, it works pure works of love. It teaches and reproves meekly and mildly; it is not puffed up and disdainful like the <term>Pharisaic Reason</term> <note>original: "Pharisaicall Reason" — Boehme’s term for intellectual pride that judges others based on rules while lacking inner spiritual life, similar to the Pharisees in the New Testament.</note> in Babel.

58. Where there is a good spirit in man, it should *draw good out of evil, and not pervert anything to a wrong sense and use*. The spirit of God seeks nothing but good; He contends with no one, for He loves man. Where He exists in a person, He drives them to love and humility toward their neighbor. He teaches and instructs with meekness, mildness, and forbearance, as a loving father does his children. He does not "push with the horn" of revilement and scorn. He does not come with thunder and lightning—like the anger in the Father’s nature on <term>Mount Sinai</term> or through the prophet <term>Elias</term> <note>original: "Elias" — Elijah. Boehme contrasts the "fire" of the Old Testament law with the "light" of the New Testament.</note>—but with a still, soft voice, *as in the Day of <term>Pentecost</term>*.

59. God has <term>Regenerated</term> <note>original: "Regenerated" — Spiritually reborn.</note> us again in <term>Christ</term>, in love, and not in the quality of the fire. He did this so that we should meet and assist each other with a kind, Christian, and friendly will, and with moderate, modest, and mild behavior and sincerity. We should entreat and admonish each other as brothers. We must help the weak and direct those who go astray, lovingly showing them the way. We must not immediately cast them into God's anger or the hellish fire, as the proud Pharisaic reason in Babel does, which spits out hell and damnation against those who are not of its own <term>Sect</term>, way, and opinion.

[...be careful and take heed of the cunning insinuations and mixture of the spirit of this world and the imagination of the Devil, so that the true human spirit of the will—which proceeds from the fire of the soul into the light—is not infected and poisoned in its course <note>original: "curse" — likely a printer's error for "course," meaning the soul's path or progress, though it could refer to the soul's fallen state.</note>.]

70. There is no better medicine or antidote than the desire for love and humility. So long as a person proceeds and judges in love and humility through the seeing [or **illumination**] of the divine power, *his word is God's word*, for it is approved by the spirit of God. *He* moves upon the wings of the wind in the pure human spirit of the will, as David says, *The Lord goes on the wings of the wind*. <note>Boehme is referencing Psalm 104:3.</note>

<margin>B</margin>
71. You will find from none of the prophets or apostles that anyone has spoken from the mouth of another, but rather from his own unique gifts. Indeed, sometimes the spirit has brought in a text and thereby clarified another scripture, but the main part of the matter flowed from his own unique spirit and mouth.

<margin>B</margin>
72. *Who has forbidden us from speaking from the gifts of our spirit?* Who says that we must only speak with someone else’s <note>original: "strange"</note> mouth—not from our own spirit—as Pharisaic reasoning <note>original: "Pharisaicall reason" — referring to a legalistic, rigid way of thinking that mimics the biblical Pharisees.</note> would have it?

<margin>B</margin>
73. *Who has made a law that the spirit should remain silent? Who has turned the speech of the spirit into another form except for the Antichrist?* It is he who has set himself up as lord over God’s spirit and has changed the voice of the holy children [or the **Holy Scriptures**] into his own character and will.

74. The great apostles never commanded this of us. Instead, they said, *Remember Jesus Christ, who died for us and has risen again*, and they told us to teach and preach. They did not silence any man's spirit or command him to change his language entirely into their words. Did they not all speak with one another, each from his own tongue, and yet from one and the same spirit—and that was *Christ's*?

<margin>B</margin>
75. Today we have the same spirit, provided that we are **born again** <term>Regenerate</term> of him. Should he not be able to say and speak what is necessary for this time? Who is the reason that the center of the **Holy Trinity** <term>Tri-unity</term> manifests and reveals itself? It is even the seeking of humanity—their own desire.

76. People argue at present about Christ's person, about the **election** <note>original: "Election of God" — the theological debate over predestination and whom God chooses for salvation.</note> of God, [about the ordinances and way of divine worship], and therefore they fight, wrangle, and insult one another. God’s love will no longer tolerate this, but rather manifests itself so that man might see what he is doing and turn away from strife and contention. He should enter into a truly apostolic life and no longer argue about knowledge—as has been the practice for a long time in **Babel** <note>original: "Babel" — for Boehme, this represents the "City of Confusion," specifically the divided and argumentative state of institutional Christianity.</note>.

<summary>Boehme argues that true spiritual expression comes from an individual's unique relationship with the Holy Spirit rather than through rigid mimicry of existing texts. He condemns religious authorities who try to silence the Spirit, blaming this control for the sectarian conflicts and "Babel" of his era.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, Holy Spirit, personal revelation, Antichrist, Babel, religious strife, spiritual rebirth, Trinity</keywords>

<page-num>28</page-num>
<header>A warning from J. B. T. <note>original: "J. B. T." — initials for Jacob Boehme, Teutonicus (the Teutonic Philosopher).</note></header>

77. But consider that now a simple mouth must speak and declare such great things, and not one that is high-ranking and deeply learned. Ask God why he does it. If a shepherd, as **David** was, should become a king by God's command, the world would not believe it until he sat in royal honor.

78. Did not Christ come in a low, humble condition and form? Also, were not his Apostles ordinary people? God can still do this, so that he may invalidate, make foolish, and bring to nothing the self-serving logic of this world. I declare to you: we speak what we know and testify to what we see.

<margin>6</margin>
79. There grows a **Lily** <note>In Boehme’s symbolism, the "Lily" represents the coming spiritual renewal and the flourishing of the divine life within humanity.</note> in the human **essence**, which shall speak of the great deeds and wonders of God in its own unique tongue; *it shall sound over the face of the whole Earth*, Hallelujah.

80. Therefore, let no one argue about opinions; all contention is the image of an **idol**. Christ has told us of his **omnipresence** <note>The quality of being present everywhere at once.</note>, but he spoke of no specific opinion when he said that *he would be with us always, even to the end of the world* (**Matthew 28:20**). He did not say he would be in this or that opinion. Rather, when he described his presence, he said: *Just as the lightning arises and shines toward the West, so shall the continual coming of the Son of Man be* (**Matthew 24:27**). And he said: *The Kingdom of God is within us* (**Luke 17:21**).

81. The light and power of Christ arise in the internal foundation of his children and give them light throughout the whole course of their life. In this fountain of light, the **Kingdom of God** is in man. If a man does not have this, let him argue, profess, and dispute as much as he wants; he cannot bring it into himself with any opinion. But if he has it, then from this fountain, pure streams of love will flow and issue forth. Let him only pay close attention that the Kingdom of Christ is **regenerated** <note>born again or spiritually renewed</note> in him—that Christ becomes man (or is born) in him. Otherwise, he is no Christian, regardless of what opinion he holds. He must stand in the **Vine**, Christ, as a living branch bearing fruit (**John 15**). Opinion is of no use to him at all; only real faith is, which expresses itself through love—or is powerful and effective in the breaking forth of love—*and works good works* (**Galatians 5:6**). If he does not have the works of love, then he has no faith. Opinion creates no salvation; instead, it is **Babel** <note>original: "Babel" — referring to the Tower of Babel, used here to mean a state of spiritual confusion and sectarian conflict.</note>, a confusion of the language of unified love. No one is a Christian unless he loves his neighbor and desires [and endeavors] to do him good.

82. **Grace imputed from without** <note>original: "Grace imputed from without" — the theological idea that righteousness is "credited" to a believer's account externally rather than being an internal change.</note> [or an external appropriation and assignment of grace], without the innate, child-like grace of a son, is completely false. When Christ works in a person, then he is a Christian; and then the suffering, merits, and satisfaction of Christ—

<summary>Boehme argues that true Christianity is an internal transformation of love rather than an adherence to external opinions or doctrines. He claims that God chooses humble messengers to bypass human logic and that the "Kingdom of God" must be born within the individual.</summary>

...benefit him; when he has Christ within him as an **intercessor** <note>original: "Interceffour" — one who mediates or speaks on behalf of another.</note> who has already accomplished it, and who does it also in him [ <gloss>namely, destroying sin, death, and Hell within him</gloss> ] and applies his merit to him. Then the Kingdom of God is found in that very merit. Otherwise, all imaginary opinions and speculative guesses are false. No work pleases God except what he himself performs by his Spirit within a person. Therefore, let us be children of Christ, and not children of images, opinions, and mental idols.

83. Christ has bequeathed his Kingdom to us in his **Testaments** <note>original: "Testaments" — likely referring to the Sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper, or the New Covenant.</note>. Whoever wishes to receive it must become a child [ <gloss>he must be born again in the spirit of Christ</gloss> ]; otherwise, there is no inheritance. Practicing repentance is better than a desire for vast knowledge. If knowledge is not given by God to a person, he will not understand the **basis of the Divine Mysteries**. But if it is given to him, then he has no need for opinion [ <gloss>or a mental idol</gloss> ]. To remain steadfast in the humility and simplicity of Christ, and to hold close to his love and grace without despising anyone, is **good Christianity**. Everything that speaks of itself is **Babel** <note>original: "Babel" — referencing the Tower of Babel; Boehme uses this to describe the confusion and pride of institutional churches and sectarian fighting.</note>. In Christ, we are all members, and only one body.

84. And so I commend all those who seek and desire the **Child Jesus** into the gentle and powerfully active love of Jesus Christ, so that he may be conceived, embodied, and born in everyone. Then, strife and contention will come to an end. **When the seed of the woman breaks the head of the serpent** <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, signifying the victory of Christ (the seed) over evil (the serpent).</note>, we return to the **Harmony** <note>original: "Temperature" — in Boehme's philosophy, this represents the "Temperamentum," a state where all spiritual forces are in perfect balance and peace.</note>. In Christ we are only one, like a tree with many boughs and branches. **AMEN.**

This is a diagram <note>original: "Scheam"</note> or map in which it is briefly explained <note>original: "deciphered"</note> and portrayed how God is to be considered outside of Nature <note>The state of God before or beyond the creation of the natural world.</note> in himself, and then within Nature according to the three principles of the divine manifestation.
